The ancients did not approve of this women's baptism [γυναικοβάπτισμα] so much that Epiphanius traces it to heretical authors; and elsewhere he does not grant it even to the Blessed Virgin, since otherwise she herself would rather have baptized her son than John. But the Papists rashly bring a lawsuit about the power of teaching against the first teachers of our churches, when they themselves make the power of baptizing so common and indiscriminate. The Lutherans follow the Papists at some distance, from the same presumption of necessity and the same excessive admiration of signs. Nor do the Socinians differ in rendering this common view, though by an opposite error, inasmuch as they abolish every mystery from the sacraments.

units.la: V. Ad exempla, in hac causa allata, respondemus: Zipporam, animo commotam, inspectante viro, coq; Propheta eximio, infantem circumcidisse; non ob filii, ut fere videtur, sed ob mariti, salutem. Ubi multa a præsenti quæstione aliena. Necipsum turbidæ fœminæ factum, si vel omni vitio careret, exemplum facere posset; cum alia olim circumcisionis alia baptismi ratio sit. Septuaginta autem discipuli, a Christo undiquaque dimissi, Luc. 10: 1. Philippus, Eunuchum propter viam mergens, Act. 8. Ananias, Paulum abluens, Act. 9. Fratres denique, jussu Petri, Cornelium, domumque ejus, Christiano ritu lavantes, Act. 10. pro privatis haberi non possunt: cum & Euangelistæ aut diaconi fuerint; & Christo, Apostolisque auctoribus illud egerint; nec sine auctoritate & vocatione sacras aquas tractaverint. Et fuit quidem Phabe, de qua Rom. 16. Ecclesiæ ministra, sed alio in ordine; non ad salutarem undam ministrandam, sed ad externas Ecclesiæ necessitates curandas. Nec supra fidem est, tria millia à solis Apostolis unico die ablutos; Act. 2: 41. ut ad illud laicorum ministerium adscitcere non sit opus.
units.tr: V. To the examples brought forward in this matter we reply: Zipporah, moved in spirit, circumcised her infant while her husband, an eminent prophet, looked on; not, as seems mostly to be the case, for the salvation of her son but of her husband. Many things here are foreign to the present question. Nor could the deed of that agitated woman make an example, even if it were free of every fault, since the circumcision of old and the rite of baptism are of different kinds. The seventy disciples, sent out everywhere by Christ (Luke 10:1); Philip, drowning the eunuch on the road (Acts 8); Ananias, washing Paul (Acts 9); and finally the brothers, at Peter's command, washing Cornelius and his household in the Christian manner (Acts 10), cannot be regarded as private persons. They were either evangelists or deacons, they did it with Christ and the Apostles as their authors, and they did not handle the sacred waters without authority and calling. Phoebe, of whom Rom. 16 speaks, was indeed a minister of the Church, but in a different order: not to administer the saving wave, but to attend to the external needs of the Church. Nor is it beyond belief that three thousand were washed in a single day by the Apostles alone (Acts 2:41), so there is no need to appeal to that lay ministry.

units.la: VI. Elementum, sive materia baptismi, est aqua pura. Et baptisabantur in Iordane. Matth. 3: 6. Act. 8: 28. & 10: 47. Quæ hic, tum ut mergendi, tum ut mersos purgandi vim habet, consideratur. Sanguinis enim usus,paracto vero sacrificio,in sacris dudum cessavit. Ac removenda inquinamenta illa, quæ Pontificii huic sacramento addiderunt: qui, ex præsumpta baptismi necessitate, saliva, lacte, aliisque liquoribus, baptisare fas habent.
units.tr: VI. The element, or matter, of baptism is pure water. And they were baptized in the Jordan. Matt. 3:6. Acts 8:38, and 10:47. Here it is considered both for its power to immerse and for its power to cleanse the immersed. For the use of blood, since the true sacrifice has been offered, has long since ceased in the sacred rites. And those additions which the Papists have made to this sacrament must be removed: they, from the presumed necessity of baptism, hold it lawful to baptize with saliva, milk, and other liquids.

units.la: VII. Socinians autem, qui in alteram partem eunt, baptismum sine aqua commenti sunt; ac de Christiana initiatione & doctrina illum sumunt; istumque loci Matth. 28: 19. Profecti, docete omnes gentes, baptisantes eos &c. sensum reddunt. Sicuti & baptismum Iohannis pro doctrina ejus intelligunt, Act. 18: 25. & Tit. 3: 5. lavacrum regenerationis pari ratione de doctrina Euangelica explicant. Isto autem tendunt, baptismum aquæ necessarium non esse, nec ritum istum divina auctoritate niti, cum ne Apostoli quidem ipsi, aliique præstantes viri, baptizari legantur. Unde, etsi circa initia Ecclesiæ utcunque usurpatus fuerit, ad Christianos a gentibus discernendos; nunc quidem postquam orbis Euangelium accepit,& testera ista non amplius opus est,illum inutilem, quin & jugum, esse.
units.tr: VII. The Socinians, who go to the opposite extreme, have devised a baptism without water. They take it of Christian instruction and doctrine, and render the passage Matt. 28:19, Go, teach all nations, baptizing them, etc., in that sense. Likewise they understand the baptism of John as his teaching (Acts 18:25), and they explain Titus 3:5, the washing of regeneration, in the same way, of the Gospel doctrine. Their aim in this is to show that water baptism is not necessary, and that this rite does not rest on divine authority, since not even the Apostles themselves, nor other eminent men, are read to have been baptized. Hence, although it was in some measure employed at the beginnings of the Church, to distinguish Christians from the nations, now that the world has received the Gospel and that token is no longer needed, it is useless, indeed a yoke.

units.la: VIII. Nos vero extra dubium habemus, Apostolos a Iohanne ablutos. Quod & de Christo legimus. Quanquam alioqui non adeo absurdum esset, eos, qui primum ad baptisandum mittuntur, ab aliis tinctos non esse. Ut in Iohanne patuit. Apostolos autem ipsos aqua baptisasse, idque ex Christi iussu, Matth. 28: 19, 20. ex ipsorum Actubus non uno loco constat. Vide cap. 2: 38, 41. & 8: 13. & 9: 18. & 10: 47. & 16: 15. & 18: 8. Quæ autem illi pro doctrinæ baptismo adferunt, exclusa aqua, nullum colorem habent. Nam & Christus Matth. 28. expresse aquæ baptismum a doctrina Euangelii distinguit, eumque præcepto suo firmat, & in Ecclesia perpetuum esse jubet. Et ubi de Iohannis baptismo in Actis c. 18: 25. Tantum sciens baptismum Iohannis: sermo est, universum ejus ministerium intelligitur; quod a celebri ejus baptismo nomen habet, qui hic includitur. Qui baptismus certe aquæ fuit. Denique in verbis Paulinis Tit. 3: 5. Non ex operibus justis, quae fecimus cimus nos; sed ex sua misericordia servavit nos, per lavacrum regenerationis, renovationis Spiritus sancti, vel metaphora est, vel potius metonymia: nam regenerationem lavacrum appellat: vel quod ipsa instar lavacri animam purget; vel potius quod salutarem illam regenerationem per signum ejus externum, baptismi undam, exprimere voluerit. Non autem doctrinam Evangelii simpliciter appellavit baptismum.
units.tr: VIII. We, however, hold beyond doubt that the Apostles were washed by John, as we also read of Christ. Although otherwise it would not be so absurd that those who are first sent to baptize were not baptized by others, as was evident in the case of John. That the Apostles themselves baptized with water, and that by Christ's command (Matt. 28:19, 20), is clear from their own Acts in more than one place. See chapters 2:38, 41; 8:13; 9:18; 10:47; 16:15; 18:8. But what they bring forward for a baptism of doctrine, with water excluded, has no colour. For Christ too, in Matt. 28, expressly distinguishes baptism with water from the doctrine of the Gospel, confirms it by his precept, and orders it to be perpetual in the Church. And where Acts 18:25 speaks of John's baptism, knowing only the baptism of John, the discourse concerns his whole ministry, which is understood here, since it takes its name from his famous baptism. That baptism was certainly with water. Finally, in Paul's words, Titus 3:5, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, this is either a metaphor, or rather a metonymy, since he calls regeneration the washing, either because it cleanses the soul like a washing, or rather because he wished to express that saving regeneration through its external sign, the water of baptism. He did not simply call the doctrine of the Gospel baptism.

units.la: IX. Actio, seu ritus, circa hoc elementum est, vel mersio, vel aspersio, indeque consequens ablutio. Mersione utebantur Judaei, Apostoli, ac primaeva Ecclesia, praesertim in regionibus calidioribus. Variique huc spectant modi loquendi, apud Apostolum, Rom.6: 3, 4. Consepulti sumus ipsi, per baptismum, in mortem. Col. 2: 12. Ei consepulti per baptismum. Gal. 3: 27. Nam quicunque in Christum baptizati estis, Christo induti. In Occidente autem, ac plaga mundi frigidiore, invaluit aspersio: in qua etiam sacramenti mysterium servatur, sic ut etiam sub ministerio Mosaico, in sacro cultu multiplices irrorationes ac βαπτισμὸς adhibitas legimus: Expiato me hyssopo, ut mundus sim. Psal. 51: 9. Accedistis ad sanguinem aspersionis, praestantiora loquentem pro Abel. Hebr. 12: 24. conf. 9: 13, 14. 1. Pet. 1: 2. Denique regionum, sub Occidente recedentium, intemperis, ac tenellorum infantium periculum, satis illam in externo ritu immutationem absolvunt, vel excusant saltem; sicuti veterem quoque Ecclesiam nonnunquam mas-persionibus usam, vel ex clinicorum, aliorumque baptismo, quibusdam videtur.
units.tr: IX. The action, or rite, concerning this element is either immersion or sprinkling, and from it follows washing. The Jews, the Apostles, and the primitive Church used immersion, especially in warmer regions. To this point refer the various modes of speech in the Apostle: Rom. 6:3, 4, We were buried with him through baptism into death. Col. 2:12, Buried with him through baptism. Gal. 3:27, For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. In the West, however, and in the colder parts of the world, sprinkling prevailed, and in it too the mystery of the sacrament is preserved. Thus even under the Mosaic ministry we read that manifold sprinklings and washings [βαπτισμὸς] were used in sacred worship: Purge me with hyssop, that I may be clean. Ps. 51:9. You have come to the blood of sprinkling, speaking better things than Abel. Heb. 12:24; compare 9:13, 14; 1 Pet. 1:2. Finally, the harshness of the regions receding in the West and the danger to tender infants sufficiently account for that change in the external rite, or at least excuse it, just as some think the ancient Church too sometimes used sprinklings, as in the baptism of the sick in bed and of others.

units.la: X. Ita quoque indifferens fere est mersionum vel aspersionum numerus; qui nullo praecepto definitus est. Unde variatum in eo est in Ecclesiis, aliis unicam, aliis trinam mersionem praeferentibus: sive unitati divinae essentiae, sive Trinitati personarum, aut triduanae Christi in sepulchro morae, significandae. Quanquam & haeretici olim hunc vel illum ritum erroribus suis obtentui sumserunt; atque isto velo sententias suas, in dividenda Trinitate, vel eadem neganda, obtexerunt. Constat autem unicam mersionem antiquitus apud Judaeos Christianosque primaevos usitatissimam fuisse.
units.tr: X. Likewise, the number of immersions or sprinklings is almost a matter of indifference, since no precept fixes it. Hence the Churches have differed on this point: some prefer a single immersion, others a threefold one, to signify either the unity of the divine essence, or the Trinity of persons, or Christ's three days in the sepulchre. Yet heretics too have at times taken up this or that rite as a cover for their errors, and under this veil they have concealed their opinions, either dividing the Trinity or denying it. It is certain, however, that in antiquity a single immersion was most common among the Jews and the earliest Christians.

units.la: XI. Mersionem comitabatur Triuni numinis appellatio, in cujus nomine, tanquam trium testium coelestium, 1. Joh. 5: 7. quemadmodum Judaeorum baptismum tres testes terrestres requisivisse vidimus, fideles obsignabantur, juxta mandatum Christi, Matth. 28: 19. Baptisantes eos in nomen Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus S. Non quod totidem verbis ac syllabis Ecclesia adstringeretur: quæ Latinorum superstitio est, qui Græcorum formulam damnant, Baptizetur servus Christi &c. Sufficit enim rem ipsam tenere, atque in baptismo SS. Trinitatis invocationem, ac publicam fidei illius professionem edere: ejus antiquissima formula, ac sequentium symbolorum rudimentum, hæc ipsa verba exiterunt.
units.tr: XI. The immersion was accompanied by the invocation of the triune Godhead, in whose name the faithful were sealed, as in the name of the three heavenly witnesses, 1 John 5:7. Just as we have seen that Jewish baptism required three earthly witnesses, so the faithful were sealed according to Christ's command, Matt. 28:19: Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. This was not because the Church was bound to these exact words and syllables; that is the superstition of the Latins, who condemn the Greek formula, Let the servant of Christ be baptized, and so on. It is enough to hold to the thing itself, namely to invoke the Holy Trinity in baptism and to make a public profession of that faith. These very words were its most ancient formula and the starting point of the creeds that followed.

units.la: XII. Unde nec Apostolos ulla formula usos videmus; qui plerunque in nomen Domini Jesu baptizasse leguntur, Act. 2: 38. 10: 48. 19: 5. Quanquam enim unus foret baptismus, ac una fides, diversa tamen erant inaugurationis verba, pro vario baptizandorum statu & respectu. Apostoli, ubi Judæos tingerent, in fidem Domini Jesu eos adigebant, Act. 2: 38. & 18: 16, 38. Hæc enim tum propria Christianismi nota erat, an Jesus Nazarenus foret Messias. Cæteris in rebus à Patrum fide, ac veteris Ecclesiæ dogmatibus nulla in re dissidebant. Cum autem cum Gentilibus non de Messia solum, sed de vero Deo, atque universa religione, controversia foret; illi, juxta Christi præceptum, de Gentium baptismo, Matth. 28: 19. ante omnia in Triuni Dei fidem imbui, atque ista formula initiari, debebant.
units.tr: XII. Hence we see that the Apostles did not use any fixed formula either. They are generally read to have baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, Acts 2:38; 10:48; 19:5. For although there was one baptism and one faith, the words of initiation nevertheless varied according to the state and circumstances of those being baptized. When the Apostles baptized Jews, they bound them to faith in the Lord Jesus, Acts 2:38; 18:16, 38. For at that time this was the distinctive mark of Christianity: whether Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah. In other matters they did not differ at all from the faith of the Fathers and the doctrines of the ancient Church. But since the dispute with the Gentiles concerned not only the Messiah but the true God and the whole of religion, they had first, according to Christ's precept about the baptism of the Gentiles, Matt. 28:19, to be imbued with faith in the triune God and initiated with that formula.

units.la: XIII. Atque hæc antiqua & vera baptismi administratio fuit, juxta Christi institutum. Quæ tamen non ultra alterum sæculum in Ecclesia, in simplicitate sua perduravit: accedentibus sensim variis ritibus, & inquinamentis, ab institutione Christi alienis; quibus nativa baptismi facies deturbata, & totius Ecclesiæ simplicitas & pulcritudo non parum delibata est. Quod hisce gradibus factum est. Prima quoad ministrum mutatio facta est, & jam tertio sæculo laicis quoque tingere permissum fuit. Deinde tempus, quod hactenus liberum erat, definitum, & celebrioribus anni tempestatibus, paschati ac pentecosti, adstrictum est. Aliis Ecclesiis alii dies baptismales erant. Quanquam iste rigor non usque tenuit, ac paulatim de eo remissum; & ablata dierum superstitione, baptismo libertas reddita rursus fuit. Porro quoad locum, cum primitus ad obvium flumen deducerentur novi fideles, 1. Joh. 1: 31. Matt. 3. Act. 2. & 8. & 10. Constantini tempore erecta in templis βαπτιστήρια, & sacri fontes. Cumque præterea privata in fidelium ædibus forent oratoria, ubi docebatur nonnunquam & baptizabatur; id quoque prohibitum fuit. Denique variis ritibus baptismus inquinatus; ac, labente tempore, omisso verbi ministerio, in meram scenam ac histrioniam commutatus est. Quod in Papatu potissimum apparuit, ubi, in sacrorum mysteriorum usu, meris spectaculis, ac inani pompa, populis detinetur; in quibus tamen religionis summa constituitur. Nec illis veluti picturis, uti olim, de rebus spiritualibus admonetur; sed singularis praeterea efficiendi vis ac efficacia illis adscribitur: atque ita, omisso Ecclesiae sponso, Ecclesia imagine ejus, ductisque perperam lineis, sese oblectare, ac non sine idololatriae probro ei inhaerere, ac quicquid illud est tantum non colere jubetur.
units.tr: XIII. This was the ancient and true administration of baptism, according to Christ's institution. Yet it did not last in its simplicity in the Church for more than a second century. Various rites and corruptions, foreign to Christ's institution, gradually crept in, by which the native face of baptism was distorted and the simplicity and beauty of the whole Church were not a little impaired. This happened in the following stages. First, the change was made regarding the minister, and already in the third century laymen were also permitted to baptize. Next, the time, which had hitherto been free, was fixed and restricted to the more solemn seasons of the year, Easter and Pentecost. Different Churches had different baptismal days. Yet this strictness did not hold for long; it was gradually relaxed, and with the superstition about days removed, freedom was restored to baptism. Further, as to the place: whereas at first newly converted believers were taken down to a river that happened to be near, John 1:31; Matt. 3; Acts 2, 8, 10, in the time of Constantine baptisteries [βαπτιστήρια] and holy fonts were erected in churches. Moreover, since there were private oratories in the homes of the faithful where teaching and sometimes baptism took place, this too was forbidden. Finally, baptism was defiled by various rites, and as time passed, with the ministry of the Word dropped, it was turned into a mere show and theatre. This appeared chiefly in the Papacy, where the people are held by the use of sacred mysteries, by mere spectacles and empty pomp, and yet the sum of religion is placed in these things. Nor are they reminded of spiritual things through such pictures as in former times; rather, a peculiar power and efficacy of producing effects is ascribed to them. And so, the Church's Bridegroom being neglected, the Church is ordered to delight herself in his image, to trace lines wrongly, to cling to it not without the reproach of idolatry, and practically to worship whatever it is.

units.la: XIV. Praecipui veterum ritus ac caerimoniae hae erant: 1. Sponsores, seu susceptores, baptizando dati. Quod ferventibus persecutionibus , ut aliqui baptismo testes essent; postea, nulla magnopere urgente necessitate, in Ecclesia retentum fuit. Graveautem est, anxiae de educando infante curae eos praeterea involvere & onerare. Nec recte Pontificii, ex sponsione illa, cognationem spiritualem, quae matrimonio quoque impedimentum faciat, fabricant. 2. A susceptoribus baptisandonomen imponebatur, atque in Ecclesiae tabulas referebatur. 3. Sequebatur sollemnis Satanae, omniumque operum ejus, abrenunciatio. 4. Eam comitabatur fidei professio; ad quam fidei candidati aliquo tempore ante in Ecclesia praeparabantur. Ac fiebat ea, pro locorum diversitate, variis adhibitis symbolis; quae ad baptismi formulam pleraque composita & expressa fuerunt. Sicuti & ea ipsa antiquissimis temporibus pro fidei formula fuit. 5. Dehinc orationibus & votis advocabatur Spir. S. super baptisandum. Cujus salutaris gratia manuum impositione, & deinceps sacro chrismate, & crucis signaculo, confirmabatur. 6. Tum, festa pompa, ac Psalmorum cantu, ad lavacrum ductus, vestes ponebat; nudusque de sacro fonte renascebatur. Ut autem foeminarum verecundiae consuleretur, discretis locis viri foeminaeque lavabantur, aliisque modis pudori prospiciebatur. 7. Descendebat in aquam non baptisandus solum, sed & minister. Qui inter sacra verba, neophytum mergitabat, & de fonte eductum suscceptori tradebat. 8. A quo acceptus, lac & mel degustabat; quo sic infantaretur, ut Tertulliani verbum est. 9. Et candida veste induebatur; quo animi candorem & puritatem obsignabant; quam de nivea veste animo praecipere jam tum debebat. 10. Denique ita initiatum ad S. Coenae quoque mysteria admittebant veteres; quod non de adultis solum, sed & de infantibus intelligendum est.
units.tr: XIV. The chief ancient rites and ceremonies were these. 1. Sponsors, or sureties, were appointed at baptism. At first, during fierce persecutions, they were there to act as witnesses to the baptism; later, though no pressing necessity any longer required it, the practice was kept in the Church. It is burdensome, moreover, because it involves and weighs these sponsors down with anxious cares about the upbringing of the infant. Nor do the Papists rightly fabricate from this sponsorship a spiritual kinship, which also creates an impediment to marriage. 2. A name was imposed on the one to be baptized by the sponsors, and it was entered in the Church's registers. 3. There followed a solemn renunciation of Satan and all his works. 4. This was accompanied by a profession of faith, for which the candidates were prepared in the Church for some time beforehand. It was made, according to the diversity of places, with various creeds used, most of which were composed and framed to match the form of baptism. Indeed, this very thing was the form of faith in the most ancient times. 5. Then, by prayers and vows, the Holy Spirit was invoked upon the one to be baptized. By the saving grace of this invocation he was confirmed by the laying on of hands, and afterwards by the holy chrism and the sign of the cross. 6. Then, with festal pomp and the singing of Psalms, he was led to the laver, put off his garments, and was reborn naked from the holy font. But to protect the modesty of women, men and women were washed in separate places, and decency was provided for in other ways. 7. Not only the one to be baptized went down into the water, but also the minister. Amid the sacred words he dipped the neophyte, and when he had been brought up from the font, he handed him to the sponsor. 8. Received by him, he tasted milk and honey, by which he was to be made an infant again, as Tertullian's phrase has it. 9. And he was clothed in a white garment, by which they sealed the candour and purity of the soul, which he ought already to conceive from the snowy garment. 10. Finally, the ancients admitted to the mysteries of the Lord's Supper those thus initiated; and this must be understood not only of adults but also of infants.

units.la: XV. Atque hi praecipui eorum ritus erant, quo sacramenti majestatem augerent, & res spirituales, cunctumque baptismi mysterium, qualicunque imagine adumbrarent. Quo tamen obtextu sequioribus sacerdotibus culis cærimoniæ immensum auctæ; &, fastidita Christi simplicitate, baptismus, non ornatus, sed fœdatus & pollutus est. Quo choragio istius Ecclesiæ scenam instrui decebat, quæ sensim, pro ipso Christo, quædam signa ejus fidelibus tradere, &, pro Servatore, idolum ejus amplecti cœperat. Unde non sacramentis solum, sed & sacramentalibus, tanta a Pontificiis tributa ad gratiam ingenerandam efficacia; & tanta necessitas, ut sine anathematum metu nihil de ista sacramentorum pompa ac cultu, deque illis, quæ venditant, mysteriis omittere nunc liceat. Non contenti autem veterum ritibus, quorum nonnullos omiserunt, & mutarunt, solent illi præterea baptismi aquam incantamento quodam lustrare & consecrare. Nec isto elemento contenti, additum demceps & sal, & sputum, aliaque inquinamina; quæ partim ori ingerunt, quartum auribus & naribus allinunt; adhibito magico vocabulo, Ephphatah. Tum & frontem, & pectus infantis sacerdos crucis signo terit. Et, non sine Christiani populi contumelia, quasi fidelium infantes diaboli mancipia essent, Exorcismo utitur. In quo videntur sibi antiquum ritum imitari; ubi qui de Gentilium idolalatria ad Christianam fidem accedebant, ad baptismi aquas, diabolo, omnique ejus pompæ, abrenunciare jubebantur. Nec recte Lutheri asseclæ istud de Romanæ Ecclesiæ pompa in baptismo suo retinuerunt. Mittimus alia eorum instituta, alterum Chrisma, cereos, repetitum crucis signum, obtestionem capitis baptizati, pedilavium, impositionem manuum cum osculo pacis, ac linguæ Latinæ usum, quo hæc sacra occultant, ac alia. Nam ad viginti duas cerimonias numerus excrevit; plus quam in ullo Veteris Test. ritu unquam contigit. Quo solo illæ facile damnantur ac concidunt. Nec quæsitarum significationum, aut mysterii alicujus, color sufficit. Nam & plus quam simplicem rerum spiritualium picturam Pontificii in iis collocant: neque illo prætextu superstitiosos cultus introducere, ac Ecclesiam onerare licet. Nec Spiritus S. ullibi ad ritus illos, sive veteres, sive recentiores, alludit; quo male referunt sequentia loca, Gal. 3:27. 1. Pet. 2:2. Heb. 10: 32. & 6:4, 5. 2. Cor. 1:21, 22. 1. Joh. 2:20. Sed occasione potius locorum illorum ac phrasium illi olim effecti, & in Ecclesiam introducti sunt. Quod institutum temerarium fuisse, ex eventu, secutisque ad istud exemplum corruptelis innumeris patet.
units.tr: XV. These were their chief rites, by which they sought to enhance the majesty of the sacrament and to shadow forth, in some kind of picture, the spiritual things and the whole mystery of baptism. Yet under this pretext, through the increasing folly of inferior priests, the ceremonies grew enormously, and, Christ's simplicity being despised, baptism was not adorned but disfigured and polluted. It was with this sort of stage-machinery that the scene of this Church ought to be fitted out, a Church which by degrees had begun to hand down to the faithful certain signs of Christ in place of Christ himself, and to embrace his image in place of the Saviour. Hence the Papists ascribe such great efficacy not only to the sacraments but also to the sacramentals for producing grace, and such great necessity, that it is not now lawful, on pain of anathema, to omit anything from this pomp and worship of the sacraments, or from those mysteries which they peddle. Not content, however, with the ancient rites, some of which they have omitted and some changed, they are accustomed also to purify and consecrate the water of baptism with a certain incantation. Nor being content with this element, they have since added salt, spittle, and other defilements: some of these they put into the mouth, and a fourth they smear on the ears and nostrils, with the magic word Ephphatah. Then the priest also marks the infant's forehead and breast with the sign of the cross. And, not without insult to the Christian people, as if the infants of the faithful were slaves of the devil, he uses an exorcism. In this they seem to imitate an ancient rite, in which those who came to the Christian faith from the idolatry of the Gentiles were ordered to renounce, at the waters of baptism, the devil and all his pomp. Nor did Luther's followers rightly retain that ceremony of Roman pomp in their baptism. I pass over their other institutions: the second chrism, the candles, the repeated sign of the cross, the adjuration of the head of the baptized, the foot-washing, the laying on of hands with the kiss of peace, and the use of the Latin tongue, by which they hide these sacred things, and others. For the number of ceremonies has grown to twenty-two, more than ever occurred in any rite of the Old Testament. This alone easily condemns and overthrows them. Nor is the colour of any sought-after meaning or mystery sufficient to excuse them. For the Papists place in these things more than a simple picture of spiritual realities, and it is not lawful to introduce superstitious worship and burden the Church under that pretext. Nor does the Holy Spirit anywhere allude to those rites, whether ancient or more recent; the following passages are wrongly cited for them: Gal. 3:27; 1 Pet. 2:2; Heb. 10:32; 6:4, 5; 2 Cor. 1:21, 22; 1 John 2:20. Those ceremonies were rather devised in former times on the occasion of those passages and phrases, and introduced into the Church. That this practice was rash is clear from the outcome and from the countless corruptions that followed this example.

units.la: XVI. Subjectum, cui baptismus administratur, sunt omnes fœderati; sine ullo gentis, sexus, aut ætatis discrimine. Matth. 28:19. Act. 16:15. Cum omnes, qui fœdere continentur, fœderis tessera insigniri ac
units.tr: XVI. The subject to whom baptism is administered is all who are in covenant, without distinction of nation, sex or age. Matt. 28:19. Acts 16:15. Since all who are included in the covenant ought to be marked with the token of the covenant and consecrated,

units.la: Baptismi, subjectum, omnes fœderati; ac consecrari debeant. A quo honore ac beneficio Anabaptistæ temere infantes Christianorum excludunt; non sine verborum contumelia sacrum hunc ritum lacerantes, dum sacras aquas hoc pacto profanari clamitant, & ludos istos propemodum infantiles, ac baptismi mimum, ab Ecclesia exulare debere contendunt. Pariterque Socinianî ritum istum omnem nunc inutilem, aut, ubi mollius loqui volunt, adiaphorum censent. A quo etiam non adeo abhorrere videntur Remonstrantes.
units.tr: the subject of baptism is all who are in covenant, and who ought to be consecrated. The Anabaptists rashly exclude the infants of Christians from this honour and benefit. They tear apart this sacred rite with no small abuse of words, crying out that the holy waters are profaned in this way, and insisting that these almost childish games, a mime of baptism, must be banished from the Church. Likewise the Socinians now consider the whole rite useless or, where they wish to speak more gently, indifferent. The Remonstrants too do not seem to shrink far from this view.

units.la: XVII. Nos autem divina auctoritate istam Ecclesiæ consuetudinem niti docemus: &, tum ex Dei fœdere; tum ex baptismi natura; tum ex infantium ac fidelium conditione; denique ex Veteris Testam. auctoritate ac consensu; ac Apostolicæ quoque, sequentisque Ecclesiæ, usu illum confirmamus. Ista omnia enim infantes quoque obsignandos, & a reliquo puerorum grege, qui nec Dei nec Ecclesiæ filii sunt, distinguendos clamant.
units.tr: XVII. We, however, teach that this custom of the Church rests on divine authority. We confirm it from God's covenant, from the nature of baptism, from the condition of infants and believers, and finally from the authority and agreement of the Old Testament, and also from the practice of the apostolic and following Church. All of these loudly declare that infants too are to be sealed, and to be distinguished from the rest of the children, who are not sons of God or of the Church.

units.la: XVIII. Primo enim, ad fœdus Dei fidelium liberos, vel in ipsis cunis, pertinere, illisque etiam promissiones factas, tota Scriptura testatissimum est. Hoc est fœdus meum, inter me & vos, & semen tuum post te: natus dies octo circumcidetur vobis omnis mas. Gen. 17: 10, 12. Vos statis hodie omnes coram Iehova — omnis vir Israëlis, pueri vestri, uxores vestræ; & advena tuus — ut transeas in fœdus Iehova Dei tui. Deut. 29: 10, 11, 12. Baptizetur quisque vestrum, in nomine Iesu Christi — vobis enim est promissio, & liberis vestris. Act. 2: 38, 39. Horum (puerorum) est cælorum regnum. Matth. 19: 14. Omnes vos unus estis in Christo Iesu. Gal. 3: 29. Unde parvulos illos Christianos sacris undis arcere, ac fœderis Dei signis, & testeris, & pignore, privare velle, & nefas, & crudele est. 1. Quid enim baptismus aliud, quam Christianæ militiæ tessera, & rudimentum, & maximorum Dei promissorum obses & arrhabo est? Etenim per unum Spiritum omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus. 1. Cor. 12: 13. Qui autem rei significatæ compos & particeps est, ei sacrum signum negare velle non ferendum est. Rem autem baptismo signatam, peccatorum remissionem, regenerationem, ac divini Spiritus dona, etiam ad infantes pertinere, ex locis mox citatis vidimus. Unde non, tanquam profani, & a fœdere Dei exules, habendi sunt; sed uti nova Ecclesiæ soboles, sacro baptismi symbolo inaugurari & Ecclesiæ inseri debent. Conf. Act. 10: 47. 111. Quo Veteris Testamenti prædictio pertinet, quæ ad Ecclesiam parvulos quoque in ulnis & humeris gestandos edixit. Jes. 49: 22. Quos advenientes Ecclesiæ limine arcere, ac complexu Christi excutere velle, impium, & Dei increpatione dignum est. Matth. 19: 14. Hinc etiam fidelium liberi dicuntur sancti.
units.tr: XVIII. First, it is most clearly attested throughout Scripture that the children of believers, even in their cradles, belong to God's covenant, and that the promises were made to them as well. This is my covenant, between me and you, and your seed after you: every male among you shall be circumcised when he is eight days old. Gen. 17:10, 12. You all stand today before the LORD your God, every man of Israel, your little ones, your wives, and your stranger, that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God. Deut. 29:10, 11, 12. Let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ... for the promise is to you and to your children. Acts 2:38, 39. Of such (children) is the kingdom of heaven. Matt. 19:14. You are all one in Christ Jesus. Gal. 3:29. Hence it is both wicked and cruel to wish to keep those little Christians away from the holy waters and to deprive them of the signs, the witness and the pledge of God's covenant. 1. For what else is baptism than the token and the beginning of Christian warfare, and the hostage and earnest of God's greatest promises? For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body. 1 Cor. 12:13. To wish to deny the sacred sign to one who shares in and partakes of the thing signified is not to be tolerated. We have seen from the passages just cited that the thing sealed by baptism, namely the remission of sins, regeneration and the gifts of the divine Spirit, pertains to infants as well. Therefore they are not to be regarded as profane and exiles from God's covenant, but as a new offspring of the Church, to be initiated with the sacred symbol of baptism and grafted into the Church. Cf. Acts 10:47. 111. To this belongs the prophecy of the Old Testament, which declared that the little ones too would be carried in the arms and on the shoulders into the Church. Isa. 49:22. To wish to keep these, as they come to the threshold of the Church, from the embrace of Christ and to shake them off is impious and deserves God's rebuke. Matt. 19:14. Hence the children of believers are also called holy.

units.la: 1. Cor. 7: 14. Semen sanctum. Ezr. 9: 2. quae non est sanctitas naturae, sed foederis. Quod si delibatio sancta est, & massa; & si radix sancta, & rami. Rom. 11: 16. Imo haec vel maxima fidelium consolatio est; quod, promissis Dei freti, de sancta progenie bene sperare; inque liberorum suorum grege, quos, in Ecclesiae sinu positos, faustis sub penetralibus enutriri, & in sancta patrum disciplina, iter vota ac preces piorum, adolescere vident; futurae aetatis spem praecerpere, ac novum istum populum, surgentesque Ecclesiae spes, & incrementa, mirari, deque eo laetari ac gloriari possint. IV. Sed & in Vet. Test. infantes praecidi, ac religioso ritu a Deo signari solitos, legimus. Novum autem foedus cum eo, quod cum Abrahamo initum fuit, re & substantia idem est. Rom. 4: 1114. Gal. 3: 14-18. Foederatis autem nunc aeque accensentur liberi, ac olim, uti visum est. Signi autem foederis locum pro circumcisione nunc occupavit baptismus. In quo etiam circumcisi ipsis — consepulti ipsi in baptismo. Col. 2: 11, 12. Unde praeceptum illud, de domesticis ac foederatis omnibus obsignandis signo foederis, ad illos quoque pertinet: praesertim cum ritu longe faciliore, non sanguine, sed aqua, illa inauguratio peragatur: Baptizetur quisque vestrum in nomine Jesu Christi — vobis enim est promissio, & liberis vestris. Act. 2: 38, 39. v. Nec desunt Novi Testamenti exempla. Nam Apostolos integras domos baptisasse, in Actis ipsorum nonnunquam legimus. Plane ad ritum Judaeorum, quos, in proselytorum initiatione, omnem eorum familiam, cum circumcisione, tum baptismo, expiasse, supra vidimus. VI. Ac secuta est Apostolos primitiva Ecclesia: de cujus sensu ac consuetudine ex Irenaeo, Tertulliano, Cypriano, Origine, aliisque Ecclesiasticis auctoribus, constat. Quae aliunde puerorum baptismum, quam ab Apostolis habere non potuit. VII. Et certe ritum illum Deo gratum esse, nec benedictione ejus carere, rebus ipsis manifestum fecit; cum eo pacto Ecclesiam per tot saecula conservaverit & propagaverit; quae de baptismi fonte jugiter renata, novaque sobole ad extremum mundi finem identidem exultans, aquas istas non infoecundas, & Spiritu Dei plenas esse, dubitare non finit.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7:14. Holy seed. Ezra 9:2. This holiness is not of nature but of the covenant. For if the firstfruit is holy, so is the lump; and if the root is holy, so are the branches. Rom. 11:16. Indeed this is the very greatest consolation of believers: relying on God's promises, they may hope well for a holy offspring. Among the flock of their children, whom they see placed in the bosom of the Church, nurtured under happy roofs and growing up in the holy discipline of the fathers through the vows and prayers of the godly, they may anticipate the hope of a future age, and marvel at, rejoice in and glory in this new people, the rising hopes and growth of the Church. IV. But we also read that in the Old Testament infants were customarily circumcised and marked by God with a religious rite. The New Covenant, however, is the same in reality and substance as the one made with Abraham. Rom. 4:11–14. Gal. 3:14–18. Children are now reckoned among the covenanted just as they were of old, as has been shown. The place of the sign of the covenant, in place of circumcision, is now occupied by baptism. In whom you were also circumcised... buried with him in baptism. Col. 2:11, 12. Hence the command to seal all members of the household and all the covenanted with the sign of the covenant applies to them too, especially since that initiation is performed with a far easier rite, not with blood but with water: Let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ... for the promise is to you and to your children. Acts 2:38, 39. v. Nor are examples of the New Testament lacking. For we sometimes read in their Acts that the Apostles baptized whole households. Clearly this follows the custom of the Jews, whom, as we saw above, in the initiation of proselytes, all their family was cleansed both by circumcision and by baptism. VI. The primitive Church that followed the Apostles also did so, as is evident from the meaning and custom of Irenaeus, Tertullian, Cyprian, Origen and other ecclesiastical writers. Otherwise it could not have had the baptism of children from any source but the Apostles. VII. And certainly the fact itself has shown that this rite is pleasing to God and does not lack his blessing, since by this means the Church has been preserved and propagated through so many ages. Renewed continually from the font of baptism, and rejoicing again and again with new offspring until the end of the world, it does not allow us to doubt that those waters are not barren but full of God's Spirit.

units.la: XIX. Urgent in adversum Anabaptistas & Sociniani, Paedobaptismum merum ritus sacri profanationem esse; & nec auctoritate ulla, nec ratione, a nobis usurpari; cum baptismus ille divino mandato; infantes fantes autem fide careant, & nec veterem hominem exuere, nec novum induere, possint; non nasci enim, sed fieri Christianos; ac proinde non sine rei sacræ ludibrio infantes quotidie in Ecclesia tingi.
units.tr: XIX. The Anabaptists and Socinians press against us that infant baptism is nothing but a profanation of the sacred rite, and that we practise it on neither authority nor reason. That baptism was instituted by divine command, they say, but infants lack faith and can neither put off the old man nor put on the new, for they are not born Christians but made so. Therefore, they argue, infants are dipped daily in the Church without any mockery of the sacred thing being avoided.

units.la: XX. Nos de mandato respondemus, illud expressis verbis non requiri. Usitata enim hactenus in Ecclesia erat infantium initiatio: nec ignotus erat ipse Pædobaptismus, si quis a sæculi erroribus ad Judæorum sacra, cum domesticis, transiret. Quæ proselytorum lotio cum in nova Ecclesia retineretur, atque angustiorem præterea formam acciperet, simul omnis ejus usus retentus intelligebatur. Nec peculiari præcepto de infantibus tingendis opus erat; cum idem fœdus, idemque fœderati manerent (nisi quod non Judæi solum, sed & gentes, admissæ sunt) sola autem in externis signis mutatio esset. Quæ si fidelium parentum liberis, contra ac hactenus in Ecclesia usitatum erat, administrare nefas erat, contrario præcepto, ac expressis verbis, illud vetari oportuisset. Quanquam non omni præcepto baptismum istum carere, ex loco Math. 28: 19. satis intellitur: ubi gentium baptismus instituitur, atque omnes gentes ad Christi discipli-nam colligi, & baptizari jubentur; qua universali voce etiam credentium ex gentibus liberi intelliguntur. Nec valet exceptio, Christum doceri primum gentes, tum autem baptizari, velle. Quod in infantes, disciplinæ adhuc immaturos, non convenit. Resp. enim, usurpare Euangelistam verbum μαθητεύειν, quod est, discipulum facere; quod non de institutione solum, sed etiam de qualibet inauguratione, & discipulorum initiatione, intelligitur. Cum autem gentium baptismum hic locus præcipue spectet, adultos quidem primum erudiri, tum autem baptismo initiari debuisse, statuimus. Et infantes quod attinet, non quoslibet gentium liberos de sinu parentum rapi, & promiscue lavari debuisse, concedimus. Sed, ubi parentes crediderint, eorum liberos adhuc profanos haberi, & a sacris signis excludi, non ferimus. Quod præsertim postmodum, constituta gentium Ecclesia, locum habuit.
units.tr: XX. We reply concerning the command that it is not expressly required. For the initiation of infants had been customary in the Church up to that time, and infant baptism itself was not unknown, if anyone passed from the errors of the age to the sacred rites of the Jews together with his household. When this washing of proselytes was retained in the new Church, and moreover received a narrower form, it was understood that all its use was retained at the same time. Nor was a special precept about the baptism of infants needed, since the same covenant and the same covenanted persons remained (except that not only Jews but Gentiles too were admitted), and only the external signs were changed. If it had been wrong to administer this to the children of believing parents, contrary to what had been customary in the Church, a contrary precept, in express words, ought to have forbidden it. Yet that this baptism is not without a precept is sufficiently understood from Matt. 28:19, where baptism of the nations is instituted and all nations are commanded to be gathered into the discipleship of Christ and baptized. By this universal word the children of believers from the nations are also understood. Nor does the objection hold that Christ wished the nations to be taught first and only then baptized. That does not suit infants, who are not yet mature enough for discipleship. We reply that the evangelist uses the word "to make disciples" [μαθητεύειν], which is understood not only of instruction but of any initiation and admission of disciples. Since this passage chiefly concerns the baptism of the nations, we hold that adults ought first to be taught and then baptized. As for infants, we concede that the children of the nations were not to be snatched from their parents' bosom and washed indiscriminately. But where parents have believed, we do not tolerate that their children should still be regarded as profane and excluded from the sacred signs. This especially came to apply afterwards, when the Church of the nations had been established.

units.la: XXI. Similiter nec rationi infantium baptismus refragatur; quasi illi fide careant, adeoque nihil in ipsis sit, quod obsignari possit. Si hæc enim ratio valeret, etiam a circumcisione Judæorum liberi arcendi fuissent. Quid vetat autem infantes inseri Christo, utque ipsi debitos a prima ætate insigniri, ac divini præterea amoris pignus capere? Si generis humani, si reipublicæ, cur non & Ecclesiæ partem facere possunt, ejusque leges subire, vere Christiana soboles? de fide autem infantium ob-
units.tr: XXI. Likewise, infant baptism is not refuted by the argument that infants lack faith and so there is nothing in them that can be sealed. If that argument held, children would also have been excluded from the circumcision of the Jews. And what forbids infants to be grafted into Christ, to be marked from their earliest age as belonging to him, and to receive a pledge of divine love besides? If they can be part of the human race and of the commonwealth, why can they not also be part of the Church and subject to its laws, as a truly Christian offspring? As for the faith of infants, the inquiry is ob-

units.la: Quibus satis fit. fcura investigatio est, cum nos ætatis illius non meminerimus & arcana fit Spiritus operatio, cujus modum omnem nos definire non possumus. Neque regenerationis initia,ac novæ vitæ femina,minus in ipsos cadere possunt, quam corruptæ naturæ languor, & labes, quam ex primo humani generis parente hauserunt. Sufficit autem, rem significatam baptismi ipsis convenire, quæ ipsis obsignetur; ne quis chartam puram, in qua nihil scriptum est, isto baptismo obsignari criminetur. Quod autem ad Sacræ Cœnæ epulum non admittantur, manifesta ratio est: Non enim omnia sacramenta omnibus, atque omni tempore conveniunt. Non enim de agno paschali recens nati infantes esitarunt. Regula autem Christi sequenda est. Nec alii ad sacrum epulum admittendi, quam qui panem hunc a vulgari internoscere, Christique domini mortem & beneficia celebrare, & sanctum illud nomen publice fateri possunt.
units.tr: This is enough for them. The inquiry is obscure, since we do not remember that age, and the working of the Spirit is secret, and we cannot define every mode of it. Nor can the beginnings of regeneration and the seeds of new life fall upon them any less than the languor and stain of corrupt nature which they drew from the first parent of the human race. It is enough, however, that the thing signified by baptism belongs to them and is sealed to them, lest anyone accuse a clean sheet of paper, on which nothing is written, of being sealed by that baptism. As for their not being admitted to the feast of the Lord's Supper, the reason is plain: not all sacraments suit all people and every time. Indeed, infants just born did not eat of the paschal lamb. The rule of Christ must be followed. Only those may be admitted to the sacred feast who can distinguish this bread from common bread, celebrate the death and benefits of Christ the Lord, and publicly confess that holy name.

units.la: XXII. Sub fœderatis autem continentur, quicunque fidem Christianam, quanquam non prorsus puram, confitentur. De Ecclesia enim, quæ nævos quoque suos & errores habet, Christus liberos nihilominus tollere potest. Non excludendi spurii, nothi, aliive natalium labe vel parentum vitiis notabiles. Communis enim omnium mater est Ecclesia, quæ suo sinu nascentes excipit & fovet: Nec unius parentis labes Ecclesiæ fidem obscurare, Deinque benedictionem auferre ab ea potest. De monstrosis partubus, mente motis, Dæmoniacis, prudenter iudicandum: hoc interim tenendum, non facile, in quo quicquam Christi esse suspicari licet, ab hoc sacramento arcendum esse. Præpostere autem Pontificii infantes, non plene natos, aspergunt.
units.tr: XXII. Those are included under the covenant who profess the Christian faith, though not altogether pure. For Christ can nevertheless take children out of the Church, which also has its blemishes and errors. Spurious children, bastards, and others marked by a stain of birth or by the vices of their parents are not to be excluded. For the Church is the common mother of all; she receives and cherishes those who are born in her bosom. Nor can the fault of one parent obscure the faith of the Church or take away the blessing from her. Concerning monstrous births, those of disturbed mind, and the demon-possessed, judgment must be exercised prudently. Meanwhile this should be held: that one should not readily exclude from this sacrament anyone in whom there is reason to suspect something of Christ. The Papists, however, absurdly sprinkle infants who are not fully born.

units.la: XXIII. Nec probandi veteres, e Marcionis schola hæretici, qui vel ipsis mortuis, vel, eorum loco, aliis viventibus vicarium baptismum largiti dicuntur. Nedum ut baptisari debeant res inanimæ; quales bestiæ, naves bellicæ, urbium propugnacula, vexilla, ipsumque æs campanum; quæ sollemnioribus ritibus a Pontificiis inaugurantur quam ipsi Christianorum infantes. Quod non ferendum rei sanctissimæ ludibrium est. Quomodo enim divina gratia, quæ sacramento hoc obsignatur, in res illas cadere potest? Præsertim cum juxta adversarios ex opere operato ad sacramenti usum ea conferatur. Frustra autem dedecus hoc velare conantur excogitato commento, non illum baptismum, sed consecrationem & Ecclesiasticam initiationem esse; qua ad miraculosos effectus, fodandas tempestates, dæmones pellendos &c. illa polleant. Veri enim babaptismi ritus, & formam, & verba, in pudendis istis baptismis sacrilegi homines tenent; quod ex ritualibus ipsorum videre est. Et superstitiosa ac magica sunt, quæ de pellendis tempestatibus, dæmonibus &c. adjiciunt, nec magis illa juvant, quam Ethnicorum idololatrarum bombi magici, atque æra laboranti solita succurrere Lunæ.
units.tr: XXIII. Nor are the ancient heretics of Marcion's school to be approved, who are said to have granted vicarious baptism, either to the dead themselves or, in their place, to other living people. Still less should inanimate things be baptized, such as beasts, warships, the bulwarks of cities, banners, and even the bronze of a bell, which the Papists inaugurate with more solemn rites than they use for Christian infants. This is a mockery of the most holy thing that cannot be tolerated. For how can the divine grace that is sealed by this sacrament fall upon those things? Especially since, according to our adversaries, it is conferred on them ex opere operato by the use of the sacrament. They try in vain to cover this disgrace with a contrived pretext: that it is not baptism at all but a consecration and ecclesiastical initiation, by which those things are endowed with miraculous powers, such as dispelling storms, driving out demons, and so on. For these wicked men keep the true rite, form, and words of baptism in these shameful baptisms, as can be seen from their rituals. And what they add about driving off storms, demons, and the like is superstitious and magical, and these things help no more than the magic noises and bronze gongs that idolatrous Gentiles customarily used to aid the labouring moon.

units.la: CAPUT VIII.
units.tr: Chapter VIII.

units.la: De re significata Baptismi.
units.tr: On the thing signified by baptism.

units.la: I. Equitur tertio interna baptismi gratia ac significatio. Est enim baptismus non teslera solum Christianismi, ac publicum ejus signum: sed & sanctissimum fœderis sigillum, cunctorumque ejus beneficiorum arrhabo & pignus; ac speciatim nostræ in Christo insitionis, sacræque istius communionis, obsignatio. Quod per partes, tum in elemento, tum in ritu, quo usurpatur, videndum.
units.tr: I. Next, third, comes the inward grace and meaning of baptism. Baptism is not only the badge of Christianity and its public sign, but also the most holy seal of the covenant, the earnest and pledge of all its benefits, and specifically the seal of our engrafting into Christ and of that holy communion. This is to be considered part by part: in the element, and in the rite by which it is used.

units.la: II. Atque aqua quidem, cum vim purgandi habeat, pulcherrimo emblemate, tum purissimam Christi obedientiam, ipsumque sanguinis ejus rorem; tum sanctificatorem Spiritum, adumbrat. Accedamus cum vero corde, per certioratam fidem, adspersione purgatis cordibus a conscientia mala. Et abluto corpore aqua munda &c. Hebr. 10: 22, 23. Et spargam super vos aquas mundas & purificabimini: Ezech. 36: 25. Et sanguis Jesu Christi filii ejus purificat nos ab omni peccato. 1 Joh. 1: 7. conf. Apoc. 7: 14. Quæ duo quibusdam conjungi videntur, Joh. 3: 5. Nisi quis fuerit genitus ex aqua & Spiritu, non potest ingredi in regnum Dei. Sicuti & in Veteris Test. lustrationibus & purificationibus, non sanguinem solum: Et omnia fere secundum legem sanguine purificabantur. Hebr. 9: 22. Sed & aquam adhibitam constat. Lavabis me, & super nive albescam. Psal. 51: 9. & ignem, Num. 31: 22, 23. & oleum, Lev. 14: 1619. quæ omnia symbola ac typi erant veræ purificationis per sanguinem & Spiritum Christi. Matth. 3: 11. 1. Joh. 2: 20. 1. Pet. 1: 2. quæ etiam per aquæ symbolum nobis nunc exhibentur: unde illius nunc etiam sacer in sacramentis usus manet.
units.tr: II. Water, because it has the power to cleanse, portrays with a most beautiful emblem both Christ's most pure obedience and the dew of his blood, and also the Holy Spirit who sanctifies. Let us draw near with a true heart, in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water, etc. Heb. 10:22, 23. And I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: Ezek. 36:25. And the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin. 1 John 1:7. Compare Rev. 7:14. Some think these two are joined together: Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God, John 3:5. Likewise in the purifications and cleansings of the Old Testament, not blood alone was used: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood, Heb. 9:22. But it is also clear that water was used: Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow, Ps. 51:9; and fire, Num. 31:22, 23; and oil, Lev. 14:16–19. All these were symbols and types of the true purification by the blood and Spirit of Christ: Matt. 3:11; 1 John 2:20; 1 Pet. 1:2. These are now also shown to us through the symbol of water, and that is why its sacred use in the sacraments remains.

units.la: III. Ritus externus, cum submersionis ac suffocationis, tum ablutionis imaginem habens, duplicem quoque figuram gerit; & partim mortem sionis. tem ac sepulturam Christi, nostrique cum illa communionem; cujus rei ἀντίτυπον in Veteri Test. fuit arca, diluvii undis innatans, iisque mersa, nec unquam submersa: partim peccatorum ablutionem per sanguinem & Spiritum Christi, sive peccatoris justificationem & sanctificationem significat. Consepulti sumus ipsi, per baptismum in mortem — ut in novitate vitae ambulemus. Rom. 6: 4. Cui rei, arcae, nunc respondens exemplar baptismi nos quoque servat; non quo carnis sordes abiciuntur, sed stipulatio bonae conscientiae apud Deum &c. 1. Pet. 3: 20. Resipiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum, in nomen Jesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 2: 38. Salvavit nos per lavacrum regenerationis. Tit. 3: 5.
units.tr: III. The outward rite, which has the image both of submersion and suffocation and of washing, also bears a twofold figure. It partly signifies the death and burial of Christ and our fellowship with it. The antitype [ἀντίτυπον] of this in the Old Testament was the ark, floating on the waves of the flood and sunk by them, yet never sunk. Partly it signifies the washing away of sins through the blood and Spirit of Christ, that is, the justification and sanctification of the sinner. We were buried with him by baptism into death, that we also should walk in newness of life. Rom. 6:4. The like figure whereunto, even baptism, doth also now save us, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God, etc. 1 Pet. 3:20. Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins. Acts 2:38. He saved us by the washing of regeneration. Titus 3:5.

units.la: IV. Ita ut baptissimi effectus fit, omnia Christi in Ecclesiam beneficia isto sacramento nobis adumbrare & obsignare. De sacra enim unda renati primum & praecipue Christo inserimur, Rom. 6: 3, 4. post quod fidei tyrocinium, deinceps justificamur, & noxarum remissionem adipiscimur. Quod expiatrices illae aquae vel praecipue significant. Baptismus resipiscentiae ad remissionem peccatorum. Marc. 1: 4. Baptizetur quisque vestrum in nomine J. Christi, in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 2: 38. Surgens, baptizator, & abluitor a peccatis tuis. Act. 22: 16. Porro & nativas sordes & originis labem, ista ablutionis ac mersionis imago significat; & Spiritus S. aquas aquae illae externae figurant; ac proinde Sanctificationis quoque pignus ac obsces sunt. Unde regenerationis lavacrum, in quo veteres sordes ponimus; & resipiscentiae baptismus apud sacros scriptores occurrit. Tit. 3: 5. Matth. 3: 2. Luc. 3: 3. Tandem, cum ista omnia in hac vita valde imperfecta sint, atque in futurae vitae auspicium potissimum abluamur, etiam glorificationis pignus, & bonae ac laetae conscientiae ἐπερώτημα, ac arrhabonem, in aquis istis possidemus, 1 Pet. 3: 21. Nec levis futurae post mortem resurrectionis adumbratio est in mystica illa immersione & emersione. Saltem mortem & resurrectionem Christi, nostrique cum ea communionem ritu illo non leviter figurari, Apostolus ad Rom. 6: 4, 5. docet. Consepulti sumus igitur et, per baptismum, in mortem: ut, sicut suscitatus est Christus e mortuis, in gloriam Patris, ita & nos nova vita ambulemus. Nam si cum eo plantati coaluimus assimilatione mortis ejus; nimirum etiam resurrectionis assimilatione cum eo coalescemus. Conf. Col. 2: 11, 12.
units.tr: IV. Thus the effect of baptism is that this sacrament sets before us and seals all the benefits of Christ to the Church. For we who are born again are first and chiefly engrafted into Christ by the holy water, Rom. 6:3, 4. After this, as a beginning of faith, we are then justified and obtain the remission of our offences. Those cleansing waters chiefly signify this. The baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, Mark 1:4. Let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, Acts 2:38. Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, Acts 22:16. Further, that image of washing and immersion signifies also our natural filth and the stain of origin; and those external waters are a figure of the Holy Spirit's water, and therefore are also a pledge and seal of sanctification. Hence the "washing of regeneration," in which we put off the old filth, and the "baptism of repentance," occur in the sacred writers: Titus 3:5; Matt. 3:2; Luke 3:3. Finally, since all these things are very imperfect in this life, and since we are washed chiefly as an omen of the future life, we also possess in those waters a pledge of glorification and the appeal [ἐπερώτημα] of a good and joyful conscience, and an earnest. 1 Pet. 3:21. Nor is there a slight foreshadowing of the future resurrection after death in that mystical immersion and emersion. The Apostle teaches, at Rom. 6:4, 5, that the death and resurrection of Christ, and our communion with it, are not lightly figured by that rite. Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death, so that, as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have grown together with him in the likeness of his death, we shall surely also grow together with him in the likeness of his resurrection. Compare Col. 2:11, 12.

units.la: V. Ex quibus patet, baptismi signum, circumcisioni vicarium, eadem per omnia bona adumbrare, eandemque justitiam fidei obsignare, quam veteri Ecclesiæ circumcisio obsignabat. Nisi quod baptismus, ad novæ Ecclesiæ statum accommodatior, nullo jugo, ac nulla prisæ servitutis imagine, eam territ & premat. Quæ in circumcisionis sacramento fuerunt.
units.tr: V. From these things it is clear that the sign of baptism, the vicar of circumcision, portrays in every respect the same blessings and seals the same righteousness of faith which circumcision sealed for the old Church. Except that baptism, being better suited to the state of the new Church, frightens and oppresses no one with any yoke or image of former bondage, as there was in the sacrament of circumcision.

units.la: VI. Sicut autem baptismus fidem nostram confirmat, ita ab altera parte fidem requirit: absque qua inanis pompa, & scena, & vilis aquæ libatio, & magica propemodum februatio est: nuda nimirum ablutio sordium corporis, non vero firmamentum interrogationis bonæ conscientiæ ad Deum. 1. Pet. 3. 21.
units.tr: VI. But just as baptism confirms our faith, so on the other side it requires faith. Without faith it is an empty show, a stage play, a cheap sprinkling of water, and nearly a magical ritual: a mere washing away of the filth of the body, and not the firm pledge of a good conscience toward God. 1 Pet. 3:21.

units.la: VII. Repræsentatur autem omne baptismi mysterium in solenni ejus formula Matth. 28: 19. Baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, Filii, & Spiritus S. Istis enim verbis partim Ecclesia in S.S. Trinitatis nomen inauguratur; istisque tanquam salutis testibus & auctoribus gloriatur; ac nomen istud Dei sui palam in mundo profitetur, tanquam populus ejus peculiaris: partim etiam Deus Ecclesiam in fidem suam accipit, eique infallibilis salutis sponsor existit; ac fideles filiorum & filiarum loco in domo sua habet. Manifesta enim adoptionis imago est, dum pulcherrimum S.S. Trinitatis nomen super baptizandos invocatur. Jac. 2: 7.
units.tr: VII. The whole mystery of baptism is, moreover, represented in its solemn formula, Matt. 28:19: Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. By these words the Church is partly initiated into the name of the Holy Trinity, and takes pride in them as witnesses and authors of salvation, and openly professes in the world that name of its God, as his peculiar people. Partly also God receives the Church into his faith and becomes the infallible surety of its salvation, and holds the faithful in his house in the place of sons and daughters. For there is a clear image of adoption when the most beautiful name of the Holy Trinity is invoked over those who are baptized. James 2:7.

units.la: VIII. Notandi hic adversariorum errores. Socinani, ut solent, in defectu peccant, & tenuiter de hoc sacramento sentiunt, nec mysterii quicquam in eo relinquunt. Nudas enim aquas, nulla vi ac spirituali gratia fœtas, hic agnoscunt; nec ablui iis aut purgari nos ferunt: sed baptismum illum pro nuda Christianæ professionis testera habent, quæ nihil nobis obsignet aut tradat; solummodo, externo ritu, in Christiana sacra transfire nos testetur.
units.tr: VIII. The errors of our opponents are to be noted here. The Socinians, as they usually do, err by defect and think meanly of this sacrament, leaving nothing of mystery in it. For they acknowledge here only bare water, not filled with any power or spiritual grace, and they say we are not cleansed or purified by it. They regard that baptism as a mere badge of Christian profession, which seals and gives us nothing, and only testifies by an outward rite that we pass over into the Christian rites.

units.la: IX. In alteram partem eunt Pontificii, qui aquas illas nimia vi imprægnant; nec pro signo solum aut sigillo, sed pro causa gratiæ continente, eas habent; & regenerationis ac justificationis instrumentum certissimum, per modum operis operati, appellant. Quibus ex parte accedunt Lutherani, qui hic etiam crassius loquuntur, & baptismum causam regenerationis inchoantem esse statuunt. De quibus libri hujus cap. 1. latius egimus.
units.tr: IX. The Papists go to the other extreme, charging those waters with excessive power. They regard them not only as a sign or seal but as a cause containing grace, and they call them, by the operation of the work done (ex opere operato), the most certain instrument of regeneration and justification. The Lutherans come in part to the same position, speaking here even more crudely, and they hold that baptism is the beginning cause of regeneration. Concerning these matters we have treated at greater length in chapter 1 of this book.

units.la: X. Errat pariter Romana Ecclesia circa baptismi effectum, quem nimis augent. Nam non solum peccatorum remissionem, & prisci reatus extinctionem; sed & labis originalis ac concupiscentiæ ablationem, & reliquæ maculæ abstersionem, ci adscribunt: atque in eum finem vim quandam miraculosam genitali isti undæ indunt; aut saltem eam ad sacratem ac sepulturam Christi, nostrique cum illa communionem; cujus rei ἀντίτυπον in Veteri Test. fuit arca, diluvii undis innatans, iisque mersa, nec unquam submersa: partim peccatorum ablutionem per sanguinem & Spiritum Christi, sive peccatoris justificationem & sanctificationem significat. Consepulti sumus ipsi, per baptismum in mortem ut in novitate vitæ ambulemus. Rom. 6: 4. Cui rei, arcæ, nunc respondens exemplar baptismi nos quoque servat; non quo carnis sordes abjiciuntur, sed stipulatio bonæ conscientiæ apud Deum &c. 1. Pet. 3: 20. Respiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum, in nomen Jesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 2: 38. Salvavit nos per lavacrum regenerationis. Tit. 3: 5.
units.tr: X. The Roman Church likewise errs about the effect of baptism, which it greatly exaggerates. For it ascribes to baptism not only the remission of sins and the extinction of former guilt, but also the removal of original stain and concupiscence and the wiping away of the remaining blemish. To this end it attaches some miraculous power to that native water, or at least relates it to the death and burial of Christ and our communion with it. The antitype [ἀντίτυπον] of this in the Old Testament was the ark, floating on the waves of the flood and sunk by them, yet never sunk. Partly it signifies the washing away of sins through the blood and Spirit of Christ, that is, the justification and sanctification of the sinner. We were buried with him by baptism into death, that we also should walk in newness of life. Rom. 6:4. The like figure whereunto, even baptism, doth also now save us, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God, etc. 1 Pet. 3:20. Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins. Acts 2:38. He saved us by the washing of regeneration. Titus 3:5.

units.la: IV. Ita ut baptissimi effectus fit, omnia Christi in Ecclesiam beneficia isto sacramento nobis adumbrare & obsignare. De sacra enim unda renati primum & præcipue Christo inserimur, Rom. 6: 3, 4. post quod fidei tyrocinium, deinceps justificamur, & noxarum remissionem adipiscimur. Quod expiatrices illæ aquæ vel præcipue significant. Baptizma respiscentiæ ad remissionem peccatorum. Marc. 1: 4. Baptizetur quisque vestrum in nomine J. Christi, in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 2: 38. Surgens, baptizator, & abluitor a peccatis tuis. Act. 22: 16. Porro & nativas sordes & originis labem, ista ablutionis ac mersionis imago significat; & Spiritus S. aquas aquæ illæ externæ figurant; ac proinde Sanctificationis quoque pignus ac obsces sunt. Unde regenerationis lavacrum, in quo veteres sordes ponimus; & respipiscentiæ baptismus apud sacros scriptores occurrit. Tit. 3: 5. Matth. 3: 2. Luc. 3: 3. Tandem, cum ista omnia in hac vita valde imperfecta sint, atque in futuræ vitæ auspicium potissimum abluamur, etiam glorificationis pignus, & bonæ ac lætæ conscientiæ ἐκφώνησιν, ac arrhabonem, in aquis istis possidemus, 1 Pet. 3: 21. Nec levis futuræ post mortem resurrectionis adumbratio est in mystica illa immersione & emersione. Saltem mortem & resurrectionem Christi, nostrique cum ea communionem ritu illo non leviter figurari, Apostolus ad Rom. 6: 4, 5. docet. Consepulti sumus igitur ei, per baptismum, in mortem: ut, sicut suscitatus est Christus e mortuis, in gloriam Patris, ita & nos nova vita ambulemus. Nam si cum eo plantati coaluimus assimilatione mortis ejus; nimirum etiam resurrectionis assimilatione cum eo coalescemus. Conf. Col. 2: 11, 12.
units.tr: IV. So the effect of baptism is that in this sacrament we are shown and sealed all the benefits of Christ for the Church. For in the holy water we who are reborn are first and above all engrafted into Christ (Rom. 6:3, 4). After this, as the first stage of faith, we are then justified and obtain the forgiveness of our offences, which those cleansing waters chiefly signify. A baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins. (Mark 1:4) Let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins. (Acts 2:38) Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins. (Acts 22:16) Moreover, that image of washing and immersion signifies also our inborn filth and the stain of origin, and those external waters figure the Holy Spirit; and so they are also a pledge and guarantee of sanctification. Hence the sacred writers speak of the washing of regeneration, in which we put off our old filth, and of the baptism of repentance (Titus 3:5; Matt. 3:2; Luke 3:3). Finally, since all these things are very imperfect in this life, and since we are washed chiefly as an earnest of the life to come, we also possess in those waters a pledge of glorification, a declaration [ἐκφώνησιν] of a good and joyful conscience, and an earnest (1 Pet. 3:21). Nor is the mystical immersion and emergence a slight foreshadowing of the resurrection after death. The Apostle teaches, at Rom. 6:4, 5, that the death and resurrection of Christ, and our fellowship with them, are not lightly figured by that rite. We have been buried with him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead to the glory of the Father, so we too should walk in new life. For if we have grown together with him in the likeness of his death, we shall certainly also grow together with him in the likeness of his resurrection. Compare Col. 2:11, 12.

units.la: V. Ex quibus patet, baptismi signum, circumcisioni vicarium, eadem per omnia bona adumbrare, eandemque justitiam fidei obsignare, quam veteri Ecclesiæ circumcisio obsignabat. Nisi quod baptismus, ad novæ Ecclesiæ statum accommodatior, nullo jugo, ac nulla prisćæ servitutis imagine, eam territ & premat. Quæ in circumcisionis sacramento fuerunt.
units.tr: V. From these things it is clear that the sign of baptism, the substitute for circumcision, shadows in every respect the same blessings, and seals the same righteousness of faith which circumcision sealed for the old Church. Except that baptism, better suited to the state of the new Church, does not terrify or oppress with any yoke or any image of former servitude. These things belonged to the sacrament of circumcision.

units.la: VI. Sicut autem baptismus fidem nostram confirmat, ita ab altera parte fidem requirit: absque qua inanis pompa, & scena, & vilis aquæ libatio, & magica propemodum februatio est: nuda nimirum ablutio sordium corporis, non vero firmamentum interrogationis bonæ conscientiæ ad Deum. 1. Pet. 3. 21.
units.tr: VI. But just as baptism confirms our faith, so on the other side it requires faith; without which it is an empty show, a stage play, a cheap libation of water, and almost a magical purification: a mere washing away of the filth of the body, not the firm pledge of a good conscience toward God. (1 Pet. 3:21)

units.la: VII. Repræsentatur autem omne baptismi mysterium in solenni ejus formula Matth. 28: 19. Baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. Istis enim verbis partim Ecclesia in S.S. Trinitatis nomen inauguratur; isti sque tanquam salutis testibus & auctoribus gloriatur; ac nomen istud Dei sui palam in mundo profitetur, tanquam populus ejus peculiaris: partim etiam Deus Ecclesiam in fidem suam accipit, cique infallibilis salutis sponsor exstitit; ac fideles filiorum & filiarum loco in domo sua habet. Manifesta enim adoptionis imago est, dum pulcherrimum S.S. Trinitatis nomen super baptizandos invocatur. Jac. 2: 7.
units.tr: VII. The whole mystery of baptism is set forth in its solemn formula: Baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit (Matt. 28:19). For by these words the Church is partly initiated into the name of the Holy Trinity, glories in it as in witnesses and authors of salvation, and openly professes this name of its God in the world, as his peculiar people; and partly God receives the Church into his faith, and has become the guarantor of infallible salvation for it, and holds the faithful in his house in the place of sons and daughters. For there is a clear image of adoption when the most beautiful name of the Holy Trinity is invoked over those to be baptized (James 2:7).

units.la: VIII. Notandi hic adversariorum errores. Sociniani, ut solent, in defectu peccant, & tenuiter de hoc sacramento sentiunt, nec mysterii quicquam in eo relinquunt. Nudas enim aquas, nulla vi ac spirituali gratia foetas, hic agnoscunt; nec ablui iis aut purgari nos ferunt: sed baptismum illum pro nuda Christianæ professionis testera habent, quæ nihil nobis obsignet aut tradat; solummodo, externo ritu, in Christiana sacra transfire nos testetur.
units.tr: VIII. The errors of the adversaries must be noted here. The Socinians, as is their habit, err by deficiency, and think poorly of this sacrament, leaving nothing of mystery in it. For they acknowledge here only plain water, pregnant with no power or spiritual grace; and they say that we are not cleansed or purged by it. Rather, they hold that baptism is merely a bare testimony of Christian profession, which seals or gives us nothing; it only attests, by an external rite, that we have passed over into the Christian sacred community.

units.la: IX. In alteram partem eunt Pontificii, qui aquas illas nimia vi imprægnant; nec pro signo solum aut sigillo, sed pro causa gratiæ continente, eas habent; & regenerationis ac justificationis instrumentum certissimum, per modum operis operati, appellant. Quibus ex parte accedunt Lutherani, qui hic etiam crassius loquuntur, & baptismum causam regenerationis inchoantem esse statuunt. De quibus libri hujus cap. 1. latius egimus.
units.tr: IX. The Papists go to the other extreme: they impregnate those waters with excessive power, and regard them not merely as a sign or seal but as containing the cause of grace, and they call them, by the mode of the work done (ex opere operato), the most certain instrument of regeneration and justification. The Lutherans also come close to this side, speaking here even more crudely, and they hold that baptism is the beginning cause of regeneration. About these matters we have treated at greater length in chapter 1 of this book.

units.la: X. Errat pariter Romana Ecclesia circa baptismi effectum, quem nimis augent. Nam non solum peccatorum remissionem, & prisci reatus extinctionem; sed & labis originalis ac concupiscentiæ ablationem, & reliquæ maculæ abstersionem, ei adscribunt: atque in eum finem vim quandam miraclificam genitali isti undæ indunt; aut saltem eam ad sacra{a}tem ac sepulturam Christi, nostrique cum illa communionem; cujus rei ἀντίτυπον in Veteri Test. fuit arca, diluvii undis innatans, iisque mersa, nec unquam submersa: partim peccatorum ablutionem per languinem & Spiritum Christi, sive peccatoris justificationem & sanctificationem significat. Consepulti sumus ipsi, per baptismum in mortem — ut in novitate vitae ambulemus. Rom. 6: 4. Cui rei, arcae, nunc respondens exemplar baptismi nos quoque servat; non quo carnis sordes abjiciuntur, sed stipulatio bonae conscientiae apud Deum &c. 1. Pet. 3: 20. Respiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum, in nomen Jesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 2: 38. Salvavit nos per lavacrum regenerationis. Tit. 3: 5.
units.tr: X. The Roman Church likewise errs concerning the effect of baptism, which it greatly exaggerates. For it ascribes to baptism not only the forgiveness of sins and the extinction of former guilt, but also the removal of original stain and concupiscence and the wiping away of the remaining blemish; and to that end it places a certain miraculous power in that generative water, or at least it relates it to the death and burial of Christ and our fellowship with it. The type of this in the Old Testament was the ark, floating on the waters of the flood and immersed in them, yet never submerged. Partly it signifies the washing away of sins through the blood and Spirit of Christ, that is, the justification and sanctification of the sinner. We have been buried with him through baptism into death, that we might walk in newness of life. (Rom. 6:4) Corresponding to this, the ark, baptism now saves us too, not by removing the filth of the flesh, but as the pledge of a good conscience toward God, etc. (1 Pet. 3:20) Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins. (Acts 2:38) He saved us through the washing of regeneration. (Titus 3:5)

units.la: IV. Ita ut baptismi effectus fit, omnia Christi in Ecclesiam beneficia isto sacramento nobis adumbrare & obsignare. De sacra enim unda renati primum & praecipue Christo inserimur, Rom. 6: 3, 4. post quod fidei tyrocinium, deinceps justificamur, & noxarum remissionem adipiscimur. Quod expiatrices illae aquae vel praecipue significant. Baptisma respiscentes ad remissionem peccatorum. Marc. 1: 4. Baptizetur quisque vestrum in nomine J. Christi, in remissionem peccatorum. Act. 2: 38. Surgens, baptizator, & abluitor a peccatis tuis. Act. 22: 16. Porro & nativas sordes & originis labem, ista ablutionis ac mersionis imago significat; & Spiritus S. aquas aquae illae externae figurant; ac proinde Sanctificationis quoque pignus ac obsessunt. Unde regenerationis lavacrum, in quo veteres sordes ponimus; & respiscentiae baptismus apud sacros scriptores occurrit. Tit. 3: 5. Matth. 3: 2. Luc. 3: 3. Tandem, cum ista omnia in hac vita valde imperfecta sint, atque in futurae vitae auspicium potissimum abluamur, etiam glorificationis pignus, & bonae ac laetae conscientiae ἐκφύτωμα, acarrhabonem, in aquis istis possidemus, 1 Pet. 3: 21. Nec levis futurae post mortem resurrectionis adumbratio est in mystica illa immersione & emersione. Saltem mortem & resurrectionem Christi, nostrique cum ea communionem ritu illo non leviter figurari, Apostolus ad Rom. 6: 4, 5. docet. Consepulti sumus igitur et, per baptismum, in mortem: ut, sicut suscitatus est Christus e mortuis, in gloriam Patris, ita & nos nova vita ambulemus. Nam si cum eo plantati coaluimus assimilatione mortis ejus; nimirum etiam resurrectionis assimilatione cum eo coalescemus. Conf. Col. 2: 11, 12.
units.tr: IV. So the effect of baptism is that in this sacrament all the benefits of Christ for the Church are shadowed and sealed to us. For it is in the holy water that we who are reborn are first and above all engrafted into Christ (Rom. 6:3, 4).
