In the year 42, Paul and Barnabas made many Christians at Antioch, and the name "Christians" was first heard there (Acts 11:25, 26), with no mention of Peter. In the year 44, the 2nd of Claudius, Baronius says that Peter came to Rome. But rather, according to others, he was committed to prison and custody at Jerusalem (Acts 12:3, 4). Freed from it, he departed for another place (Acts 12:17), not to Rome but to other regions and different parts, as will also appear afterwards. Hence the Papists conclude in vain that he ran off to Rome.

units.la: XV. Anno 47. Petrus priorem suam epistolam scripsit Babylone 1 Pet. 5: 13. atque id serio triumphant Pontificii. Babylonem Romam esse dicentes. At vero 1. licet Ecclesiæ Babylonicæ nomine salutem scribat, non ideo Babylone fuisse necesse esset. nam Ecclesiarum Asiæ & omnium fratrum nomine salutem eodem tempore impertitur Paulus. 1 Cor. 16: 19, 20. 2. Fatemur Babylone ipsum fuisse: verum Babylon illa non Roma est, sed propriedicta Babylon, quæ erat metropolis Asiaticæ; Judæorum autem Apostolus erat Petrus. Nec inconstantiæ vel levitatis argumentum est, quod in Apocalypsi, Babylon denotet Romam; cum mystica ejus descriptio id requirat; alia vero ratio est in epistola, ubi nude & aperte res narratur; nec aliam causam Petrus habuerit, occultandi nomen urbis, quam Paulus, qui illud tamen aperte præ se fert, cum Romam scribit. Cæterum, sic per Sodomam 2 Pet. 2: 6. etiam intelligi poterit Roma, cum in Apocalypsi eandem notet. Apoc. 11: 8.
units.tr: XV. In the year 47 Peter wrote his first epistle from Babylon (1 Pet. 5:13), and the Papists triumph seriously over this, saying that Babylon is Rome. But, first, although he sends greetings in the name of the Church of Babylon, it does not follow that he had to be at Babylon; for Paul sends greetings at the same time in the name of the churches of Asia and of all the brethren (1 Cor. 16:19, 20). Second, we grant that he was at Babylon itself; but that Babylon is not Rome. It is rather the properly so-called Babylon, which was the metropolis of Asia, while the Apostle of the Jews was Peter. Nor is it a proof of inconstancy or levity that in the Apocalypse Babylon denotes Rome, since its mystical description requires this; but the case is different in the epistle, where the matter is related plainly and openly. Nor did Peter have any other reason for concealing the name of the city than Paul, who nevertheless openly names it when he writes from Rome. Moreover, in the same way Rome could also be understood by "Sodom" (2 Pet. 2:6), since in the Apocalypse it denotes the same thing (Rev. 11:8).

units.la: XVI. An-
units.tr: XVI. In the year-

units.la: XVI. Anno 52. habitum putatur concilium Hierosolymitanum, quò ibat Paulus. Act. 15: 2, 3. Gal. 2: 1. Cui etiam interfuit Petrus. Act. 15. Sicut & Paulus Jerosolymis illum offendit. Gal. 2: 1. Si vero censeatur, post habitum demum hoc concilium, Romam contenditsse, & per annos 25 ibi sedisse; non sub Nerone, sed Vespasiano principe mitissimo, illum in crucem actum, necesse erit. At, habito illo concilio Antiochiæ Petrum invenit Paulus, Gal. 2: 11. Adde quod Claudii tempore Romæ exacti sint omnes Christiani; ut Romæ agere Petro tum non licuerit. Act. 18: 2. Anno 60. Nicopoli aut Romæ scribit Paulus ad Galatas; nullam vero, in eadem urbe morantis, ut illi volunt, Petri mentionem facit. Eodem anno Corintho ad Romanos scripsit: in qua Epistola tam prolixum amicorum catalogum texens, tamen Petri non meminit, cap. 16. Quod plane arguit Petrum Romæ non fuisse. Anno 61. Romam venit Paulus quarto Neronis anno: nullum autem hactenus Petri Romæ occurrit vestigium. conf. Act. 28: 21. Nondum igitur Petrum Romæ fuisse apparet; cum per integrum biennium Romæ manserit Paulus Act. 28:30. de Petro tamen altum ubique silentium. Vide 2 Tim. 4: 10. Phil. 4: 22.
units.tr: XVI. In the year 52 the council of Jerusalem is thought to have been held, to which Paul went (Acts 15:2, 3; Gal. 2:1), and at which Peter was also present (Acts 15). Just as Paul also found him at Jerusalem (Gal. 2:1). But if it is supposed that, only after this council had been held, he went to Rome and sat there for 25 years, then it must follow that he was crucified not under Nero but under Vespasian, a most mild emperor. Yet after that council Paul found Peter at Antioch (Gal. 2:11). Add that under Claudius all Christians were driven out of Rome, so that Peter could not then have been allowed to act at Rome (Acts 18:2). In the year 60 Paul wrote to the Galatians from Nicopolis or from Rome; yet he makes no mention of Peter, although, as they maintain, Peter was staying in the same city. In the same year he wrote from Corinth to the Romans, and in that epistle, though he weaves so long a catalogue of friends, he does not mention Peter (ch. 16). This plainly proves that Peter was not at Rome. In the year 61 Paul came to Rome in the fourth year of Nero; yet no trace of Peter at Rome has appeared so far (cf. Acts 28:21). It therefore appears that Peter was not yet at Rome, since Paul remained there for a whole two years (Acts 28:30), and yet there is deep silence about Peter everywhere. See 2 Tim. 4:10; Phil. 4:22.

units.la: XVII. Anno 62. Paulus ab omnibus deseritur. 2 Tim. 4: 16, 17. an ergo item a Petro? Anno 63. Roma scribit Paulus epistolam ad Ephesios. cap. 3: 1. & 6: 20. De Petro vero ne γεγὼ quidem. Vide cap. 1: 1. & 6: 19. Nec quicquam de illo occurrit in Epistola ad Philippenses, eodem anno scripta. Vide Phil. 1: 1. & 4: 21, 22. Anno 64. Epistolam ad Colossenses Romæ exarat Paulus; ubi tamen inter συνεργὸς ejus Petrus non apparet. Vide Col. 4: 10, 11. Idem dicendum de Epistola ad Philemonem, comm. 23, 24. Idem etiam pertinet ad Epistolam ad Hebræos, eodem anno & loco scriptam; in qua præcipue Petri mentio facienda fuisset. Vide Hebr. 13: 17, 24. Biennio in illa custodia transacto, Paulus ex ore Leonis liberatus 2 Tim. 4: 17. non tamen hic Petri meminit.
units.tr: XVII. In the year 62 Paul is deserted by all (2 Tim. 4:16, 17). Was he then likewise deserted by Peter? In the year 63 Paul writes from Rome the epistle to the Ephesians (ch. 3:1; 6:20). But of Peter there is not even a word. See ch. 1:1 and 6:19. Nor does anything about him occur in the epistle to the Philippians, written in the same year (see Phil. 1:1; 4:21, 22). In the year 64 Paul writes the epistle to the Colossians at Rome, where yet Peter does not appear among his fellow-workers (see Col. 4:10, 11). The same must be said of the epistle to Philemon (vv. 23, 24). This also applies to the epistle to the Hebrews, written in the same year and place, in which especially a mention of Peter should have been made (see Heb. 13:17, 24). After two years had passed in that custody, Paul was freed from the mouth of the lion (2 Tim. 4:17), yet he does not mention Peter here either.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Anno 69. Neronis 12. Petrus secundam epistolam scribit, sub finem vitæ. cap. 1: 14, 15. ubi nihil minus, quam successorem suum declarat. Eodem anno scripsit Paulus epistolam posteriorem ad Timotheum, paulo ante mortem: nihil vero de Petro. Vide cap. 4: 21. & 4: 9, 11. & 1: 16, 17, 18. Eodem anno Petrus Romæ Simonem Magum vicisse retertur; quam fabulam esse, doctis jam pridem suboluit. An. 70. secundum alios 71. Neronis ultimo, Petrus & Paulus Martyrio Romæ affecti dicuntur; quamvis alii non eodem, sed diversis temporibus illud contigisse affirment. Sed semel tantum in Christianos sævitum est, idque non cruce, sed gladio. Paulus vero, tanquam civis Romanus gladio occidi potuit.
units.tr: In the year 69, the twelfth of Nero, Peter writes his second epistle near the end of his life (2 Pet. 1:14, 15), where he declares nothing less than that he has a successor. In the same year Paul wrote his second epistle to Timothy shortly before his death, and says nothing about Peter (see 2 Tim. 4:21; 4:9, 11; 1:16, 17, 18). In the same year Peter is said to have defeated Simon Magus at Rome. That story has long since been recognised by learned men as a fable. In the year 70, or according to others 71, in the last year of Nero, Peter and Paul are said to have suffered martyrdom at Rome, although others affirm that this happened not at the same time but at different times. Yet Christians were persecuted only once, and then not by the cross but by the sword. Paul, as a Roman citizen, could be put to death by the sword.

units.la: XIX. Atque ita nec in actibus, nec in epistolis Apostolicis ullum unquam vestigium se ostendit Petri Romæ agentis. Quin per 25 annos ibi commoratum non esse, liquido inde patet & demonstratur. Quod enim alii obtendant, illum Roma sæpius huc illuc discurrisse, quippe qui universalis esset Episcopus; haud sane convenit cum ea sententia, quæ illum per tot annos ibi sedem fixisse statuit. Amicitiam ejus cum Philone Romæ contractam, eodem loco habemus, quo ἀμοιβαῖαι Pauli & Senecæ epistolas
units.tr: XIX. Thus no trace of Peter's residence at Rome appears anywhere in the Acts or in the apostolic epistles. Indeed, it is clear and demonstrated that he did not stay there for twenty-five years. For what others put forward, that he often ran back and forth from Rome to here and there because he was the universal bishop, does not at all agree with the opinion that holds he fixed his seat there for so many years. We have his friendship with Philo, formed at Rome, in the same place where we have the reciprocal [ἀμοιβαῖαι] letters of Paul and Seneca.

units.la: XX. Post finem actuum Apostolicorum, ab anno Christi 70. usque ad 100. hiatus est historiæ Ecclesiasticæ; quem veteres supplev- erunt fabulis de Petro aliisque; ut veterum in hisce fides subtilis sit; præsertim cum primi eorum, qui hasce fabulas memoriæ prodiderunt, jam ultra seculum a Christo abfuerint; unde magna etiam illorum est discrepantia. Nec omnes etiam illum solum Episcopum Romanum faciunt, cum multi Paulum illi adjungant; aliisque multis modis a se invicem mirum in modum abeant.
units.tr: XX. After the end of the Acts of the Apostles, from the year of Christ 70 to 100, there is a gap in ecclesiastical history. The ancients filled it with fables about Peter and others, so that the faith of the ancients in these matters is thin, especially since the first of those who committed these fables to writing lived more than a century after Christ. Hence there is also great disagreement among them. Nor do all make Peter alone the Roman bishop, since many join Paul to him, and in many other ways they differ wonderfully from one another.

units.la: XXI. Pandenda igitur est origo hujus fabulæ, de 25 annis a Petro Romæ transactis; nempe ab anno 2. Claudii ad annum 19. Neronis. Diserte memoraptur hi anni in Chronico Eusebii Basileensi; verum ibidem totidem annis in cathedra Antiochena Petrus sedisse dicitur, ad An. Christi 44. ut corruptus procul dubio sit locus. Græcus textus ita habet: Πέτρος τὸν ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ πεώτην Ἰεμελιώσας ἐκκλησίαν εἰς Ῥώμην ἀπῆσι, κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, Petrus Antiochiæ, prima stabilita Ecclesia, Romam abit, prædicans Evangelium. Additur, eundem primum Antiochenæ & Romanæ Ecclesiæ præfuisse usque ad mortem. Præterea nil quicquam: ut annos illos ab Hieronymo, ipso etiam satis fatente, dum Eusebium interpretatur, adjectos esse vero simile sit. Nec aliter de 7. annis Antiochiæ exactis statuendum videtur; cum in Græco nulla annorum in alterutro loco exactorum, mentio fiat. Et postremos hosce annos falsos esse, supra etiam ex S. Scriptura deprehendimus.
units.tr: XXI. The origin of this fable about the twenty-five years Peter spent at Rome must therefore be laid open: namely, from the second year of Claudius to the nineteenth year of Nero. These years are expressly mentioned in the Basel Chronicle of Eusebius; but in the same place Peter is said to have sat in the Antiochene chair for the same number of years, up to the year of Christ 44, so the passage is undoubtedly corrupt. The Greek text reads: Peter, having established the first Church at Antioch, departs for Rome, preaching the Gospel [Πέτρος τὸν ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ πρώτην ἱδρυσάμενος ἐκκλησίαν εἰς Ῥώμην ἀπῆλθε, κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον]. It is added that he presided over the Antiochene and Roman Churches first, until his death. Beyond this, nothing. So it is likely that those years were added by Jerome, who himself admits this fairly, while translating Eusebius. Nor does it seem right to judge otherwise about the seven years spent at Antioch, since the Greek makes no mention of years spent in either place. And we have already seen from Holy Scripture that these later years are false.

units.la: XXII. Aliunde etiam probare se posse putant, Petrum Romæ fuisse, cum Ecclesia ibi collecta fuerit ante Pauli adventum; id vero alterius quam Petri opera fieri non potuit. Qua in re misere falluntur, cum Euangelii doctrina multis Romanis jam innotuisset, ante Petri vel Pauli ad eos adventum; tum Hierosolymis. Act. 2: 10. ubi etiam Romani recensentur; tum Romæ ex Pauli comitibus & prodromis; uti videre licet ex Rom. 16: 1. & seqq.
units.tr: XXII. They also think they can prove from another source that Peter was at Rome, since a Church was gathered there before Paul's arrival, and this could not have been done by anyone but Peter. In this they are miserably mistaken, since the teaching of the Gospel had already become known to many Romans before the arrival of either Peter or Paul among them; and at Jerusalem, where the Romans are also listed (Acts 2:10); and at Rome from the companions and forerunners of Paul, as can be seen from Rom. 16:1 and following.

units.la: XXII. Quid vero, si liberali manu largiamur, & vixisse, & mortuum esse Romæ Petrum; magisne Romæ principatum hunc hæsisse putabimus, quam Joppæ, vel Antiochiæ, ubi item vixit Petrus? & an non magis primatus Ecclesiæ Hierosolymitanæ & dignitas Apostolatus pertinebit ad Episcopos Hierosolymitanos, ubi mortem obiit ipse Servator noster, & Jacobus Apostolus, & unde lux Euangelii in omnes terrarum angulos fuit diffusa? Quid quod nec recte Petrus dicatur Romanus Episcopus, etiamsi Romæ fuisset; nisi latiore duntaxat sensu, quali apud ipsum Petrum venit. 1. Epist. 2: 25. Eratis ut oves errantes, sed converti nunc estis ad pastorem & episcopum animarum vestrarum: & quo sensu veteres non solum Petrum, sed & Paulum urbis Romæ Episcopum vocant. Cæteroquin Apostoli licet diutius aliquantum in celebrioribus urbibus, Euangelii prædicandi causa, commorarentur, non continuo istarum urbium Episcopi, arctiori significatu, poterant haberi; propter Apostoli scilicet nomen, ad quod universalis Ecclesiæ cura pertinebat.
units.tr: XXIII. But what if we grant with a generous hand that Peter both lived and died at Rome? Would we think this primacy clung more to Rome than to Joppa or Antioch, where Peter also lived? And would not the primacy of the Church of Jerusalem and the dignity of the apostolate belong rather to the bishops of Jerusalem, where our Saviour himself died, and where the apostle James was, and whence the light of the Gospel was spread to every corner of the earth? Moreover, Peter could not rightly be called the bishop of Rome even if he had been there, except in a broader sense, such as he himself uses: You were like sheep going astray, but now you have been converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls (1 Pet. 2:25). It is in this sense that the ancients call not only Peter but also Paul the bishop of the city of Rome. Otherwise, although the apostles remained for some time in the more celebrated cities for the sake of preaching the Gospel, they could not at once be regarded as the bishops of those cities in the stricter sense, because of course the name of apostle carried with it the care of the universal Church.

units.la: XXIII. Dilutius adhuc est, quod de Sede Petri produnt; ac si illa thronus & solium quoddam regium esset; cum per illam nihil aliud significetur quam Petrum alicubi Euangelium prædicasse. Vide Matth. 23: 2. Act. 18: 11. Tum quoque cathedra Petri, veteribus tantopere decantata, fuit cathedra Antiochena, incidens in 22. Februarii, & anniversario festo culta: cum Romana Petri cathedra, ante seculum duntaxat, a Paulo IV. instituta fuerit, & in 18. Februarii conjecta; ut non nisi summa cum fraude, ex cathedra Petri primatum Romanum firmare conentur Pontificii.
units.tr: XXIV. Even more feeble is what they put forward about the Seat of Peter, as if it were a throne and a kind of royal seat, when by it nothing else is meant than that Peter preached the Gospel somewhere. See Matt. 23:2; Acts 18:11. Likewise the chair of Peter, so much sung by the ancients, was the Antiochene chair, falling on 22 February and kept with an annual feast; whereas the Roman chair of Peter was established only a century ago by Paul IV and placed on 18 February. So the Papists try to establish the Roman primacy from the chair of Peter only with the greatest deceit.

units.la: XXIV. Verum obducunt nobis, Romam celebrari sedem Apostolicam; tales vero nuncupabantur veteribus, quas fundarant Apostoli, & in quibus tanquam Episcopi sederant. Verum 1. tales dicebantur omnes, quas aut Apostoli primum stabilierant, aut quibus ipsi prædicarant, non vero quibus ut Episcopi præsederant; quod ab Apostolis alienum fuisse, jam innuimus.
units.tr: XXV. But they throw at us that the Apostolic See is celebrated at Rome; yet such sees were called apostolic by the ancients, those which the apostles had founded and in which they had sat as bishops. But, first, all sees were called such which either the apostles had first established or to which they had preached, not those over which they presided as bishops; and we have already hinted that this was foreign to the apostles.

units.la: 2. Romana sedes hoc elogio insignitur ab Occidentalibus, quod præter illam, nulla sedes Apostolica in Occidente foret; non vero, ac si, ex speciali Episcopatus Petri privilegio, reliquis fuisset prælata. 3. Nomen Apostoli, latiori significatione, aliis etiam Episcopis, passim a veteribus tribuitur. Nec pro Romano primatu hinc quicquam extundi poterit.
units.tr: 2. The Roman see is marked with this title by the Westerners, because, apart from it, there was no apostolic see in the West; not as if, by a special privilege of Peter's episcopate, it had been preferred to the rest. 3. The name of apostle, in a wider sense, is passim ascribed by the ancients also to other bishops. Nor can anything be wrung from this in favour of the Roman primacy.

units.la: XXVI. Fuerit igitur Romae Petrus; sederit ibi ut Episcopus, tandemque etiam mortem ibi obierit; non tamen Papae aliquid contulit Petrus; ut jam undequaque liquet; neque sane Petrus Romae principatum dedisset, sed Roma potius Petro. Vera idcirco origo & ratio primatus Ecclesiae Romanae repetenda est; non ex successione Petri, sed ex illustri urbis ipsius amplitudine. In veteri enim imperio Romano dignitas Episcoporum aestimabatur, pro politica & civili dignitate urbium, in quibus sedebant. Quamobrem sicut imperii civilis dignitati primatum omnem debet Romanus Pontifex; atque adeo, florente imperio, ea gaudere potuit, secundum canones Ecclesiasticos: ita collapso jam dudum imperio, omni etiam sua praerogativa jure meritoque excidit. Quamvis saecularis Romae principatus, principatum in Ecclesiam nunquam invehere potuerit.
units.tr: XXVI. Let it be granted, then, that Peter was at Rome; that he sat there as bishop, and finally died there too. Yet Peter conferred nothing on the Pope, as is now clear on every side; nor indeed would Peter have given the primacy to Rome, but rather Rome to Peter. The true origin and ground of the primacy of the Roman Church must therefore be sought not in the succession of Peter, but in the illustrious greatness of the city itself. For in the ancient Roman empire the dignity of bishops was estimated according to the political and civil dignity of the cities in which they sat. Therefore, just as the Roman Pontiff owes every primacy to the dignity of the civil empire, and so, while the empire flourished, he could rejoice in it according to the ecclesiastical canons, so, now that the empire has long since collapsed, he has rightly and deservedly lost all his prerogative along with it. Although the secular principate of Rome could never bring a principate into the Church.

units.la: XXVII. In arctum tandem cogamus, quae fusius hactenus de hoc negotio a nobis disputata sunt. Summa omnium huc redit, successionem Papae in praerogativas Petri nullam esse; nam. 1. Nullas ejusmodi unquam habuit Petrus. 2. Et si vel habuisset, nullus ipsi in iis datus fuit successor. 3. Saltem non Pontifex Romanus, quidem successio illa non juri, sed facto innitatur. 4. Et quidem tali Petri facto, cujus in Scriptura nulla fit mentio, & cum plane incertum sit, nec constet Petrum Romae unquam fuisse; aut, si fuerit, mortuum esse. 5. Et si vel indubia foret horum omnium veritas, non inde divinum, sed humanum tantum & Ecclesiasticum jus emergeret. 6. Quin verius nullum, cum Apostoli successores non habuerint, nec Petrus ullum constituerit. 7. Cum insuper non Petro tantum, sed & Paulo Episcopatus Romanus tribuatur. 8. Et olim Patriarchae omnes pares fuerint; Romano tantum, ordinis gratia, primae partes datae. 9. Nec Papae auctoritas se latius explicaret, quam ad Ecclesias suburbicarias, ex statuto Niceni Concilii. 10. Et quem deinceps primatum, vel etiam jurisdictionem nactus, imperio Romano omnem debuerit; quo collapso, illam etiam omnem amisit. 11 Contra suprematum hunc totus Oriens, multique praeclari viri, etiam Ecclesiae in Occidente, insurrexerunt. Ut nulla superfuit ratio, quae Papam Ecclesiae monarcham & successorem Petri evincat: vera enim successio est in doctrina: nec is jure Petri cathedram occupat, qui doctrinam Petri non conservat. Sed totius hujus controversiæ fons & fundus est, spes obtinendi primatus, qui Petro videbatur datus: nisi enim per hanc stetisset, & Petro datæ fuissent claves; a Paulo potius, quam a Petro successionem suam deduxissent Pontifices Romani.
units.tr: XXVII. Finally, let us gather into a narrow compass what we have so far argued at greater length about this matter. The sum of everything comes to this: that there is no succession of the Pope to the prerogatives of Peter. For (1) Peter never had any such prerogatives. (2) Even if he had, no successor was given to him in them. (3) At least, the Roman Pontiff is not such a successor; and that succession rests not on right but on fact. (4) And indeed on such a fact of Peter's as is not mentioned in Scripture at all, and it is quite uncertain whether Peter was ever at Rome, or, if he was, that he died there. (5) And even if the truth of all these things were beyond doubt, there would arise from them not a divine right but only a human and ecclesiastical one. (6) Indeed, on the contrary, there is none at all, since the apostles had no successors and Peter appointed none. (7) Moreover, the Roman episcopate is ascribed not to Peter alone but also to Paul. (8) And formerly all patriarchs were equals, the first place being given to Rome only by reason of order. (9) Nor did the authority of the Pope extend further than to the suburbicarian churches, according to the statute of the Council of Nicaea. (10) And whatever primacy or even jurisdiction he afterwards acquired, he owed entirely to the Roman empire; and when that collapsed, he lost all of it. (11) Against this supremacy the whole East, and many distinguished men, even in the Churches of the West, have risen up. So no reason remained that could prove the Pope to be the monarch of the Church and the successor of Peter. For the true succession is in doctrine, and he does not occupy the chair of Peter by right who does not keep the doctrine of Peter. But the whole source and foundation of this controversy is the hope of obtaining a primacy which seemed to have been given to Peter. For unless this had stood, and the keys had been given to Peter, the Roman Pontiffs would have derived their succession from Paul rather than from Peter.

units.la: CAPUT XVIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XVIII.

units.la: De ANTI-CHRISTO.
units.tr: Of the ANTICHRIST.

units.la: I. ISce artibus in viscera Ecclesiæ irrepsit fatalis illa lues, & doctrinæ integritatem depasta, non omnem solum prioris & divini regiminis formam, sed & speciem & colorem exedit; & fœcunda jacuit semina, unde natus & tandem exclusus, editusque partibus omnibus absolutus, in hunc mundum est Anti-Christus: in quo cudendo & ornando, sicut omnis hæc opera consumpta est, & confectæ hæ machinæ; ita nobis omnia hæc cognoscenda ante fuerunt, & longius eradicanda hæc arbor, quo facilius cum omni apparatu suo everti queat. De Antichristo igitur acturi, de nomine ejus in antecessum quædam delibemus.
units.tr: I. By these same arts that deadly plague crept into the vitals of the Church. Having devoured the integrity of doctrine, it consumed not only the whole form of the earlier divine government but also its appearance and colour. The seeds that lay there in abundance gave birth to Antichrist, who was at last hatched, brought forth, and born into this world complete in every part. Just as all this work was spent in forging and adorning him and these machines were finished, so all these things had to be known to us beforehand, and this tree had to be uprooted more thoroughly, so that it could be overturned more easily together with all its equipment. Therefore, as we are about to treat of Antichrist, let us first say something in advance about his name.

units.la: II. Vox Ἀντίχριστος, ex virtute particulæ ἀντί, notat, tum eum qui est vice Christi, tum qui est contra Christum; in quo utroque nomini etiam suo responsuros erat Anti-Christus; quamvis palmaria hujus vocis notio sit ἐναντιῶς & τῷ Χριστῷ; ut sit vel contrarius Christi, vel contrarius Christo. Nomen illud præterea vel generatim accipitur de multis; vel speciatim & κατ' ἐξοχὴν de uno. Prima notione occurrit variis in locis; ut 1 Joh. 2: 18. Filioli, novissima hora est: & sicut audivistis quia Antichristus venit, & nunc Antichristi multi facti sunt. conf. 2 Joh. 7. Phil. 3: 18. κατ' ἐξοχὴν vero & singulari cum emphasi; vox hæc de uno sumitur, qui præ reliquis omnibus sit conspicuus, cujusque reliqui tantum prodromi & rudimenta fuerunt. 1 Joh. 2: 18. & 2 Thess. 2: 3. Quoniam si non venerit defectio primum, & revelatus fuerit homo peccati, ille filius perditionis, ὁ ἀντίχριστος qui adversatur &c.
units.tr: II. The word Ἀντίχριστος, by the force of the particle ἀντί, signifies both one who is in place of Christ and one who is against Christ. Antichrist will answer to both senses of his name, although the principal meaning of this word is ἐναντιῶς and τῷ Χριστῷ, so that he is either the opposite of Christ or opposed to Christ. Moreover, the name is taken either generally, of many, or specifically and κατ' ἐξοχήν, of one. In the first sense it occurs in various places, as in 1 John 2:18: Little children, it is the last hour; and as you have heard that Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have appeared. Compare 2 John 7; Phil. 3:18. In the sense κατ' ἐξοχήν and with singular emphasis, the word is taken of one who is more conspicuous than all the rest, and of whom the others were only the forerunners and first beginnings: 1 John 2:18, and 2 Thess. 2:3: For unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition, ὁ ἀντίχριστος, who opposes etc.

units.la: III. Antichristus hic aliis nominibus dicitur ψεύδοχριστος, Matt. 24: 24. item ὁ ἀντίχριστος. 1 Tim. 5: 14. 2 Thess. 2: 4. rex adversarius. Hos. 5: 13. Vitis aliena, & vertex capillosus. Deut. 32: 32, 42.
units.tr: III. This Antichrist is called by other names: ψεύδοχριστος, Matt. 24:24; likewise ὁ ἀντίχριστος, 1 Tim. 5:14; 2 Thess. 2:4; the adversary king, Hos. 5:13; a strange vine and a hairy crown, Deut. 32:32, 42.

units.la: Ex hac Ecclesia corruptione natus. Nomen illud quid dicat. ut & nomina paralle. Pfal. 68: 22. Et caput Pfal. 110: 6. Hab. 3: 13. pastor fluitus. Zach. 11: 15. Vide & Dan. 11: 36, 37. ubi Rex se effert, consociatus cum Deo quodam peregrino. Facit huc in Apocalypsi, emblema bestia, & praecipue secunda. cap. 13: 11. & seqq. ut & pseudo-propheta; ex quibus nata est imago bestia, quae refert imaginem Christi. Ut alia ejus nomina omittamus. Civitas autem seu imperium, in quo dominatur Antichristus, vocatur Sodoma & Aegyptus. Apoc. 11: 8. item Tyrus. Esai. 23. & Babel. Apoc. 17. & 18.
units.tr: Born from this corruption of the Church. What that name means, and likewise the parallel names: Ps. 68:22, and the head; Ps. 110:6; Hab. 3:13, the head of the house of the wicked; Zech. 11:15, the foolish shepherd. See also Dan. 11:36, 37, where the king exalts himself, allied with a certain foreign god. To this belongs the emblem of the beast in the Apocalypse, and especially the second beast, Rev. 13:11 and following, as well as the false prophet; from these came the image of the beast, which copies the image of Christ. To pass over his other names: the city or empire in which Antichrist rules is called Sodom and Egypt, Rev. 11:8; likewise Tyre, Isa. 23; and Babylon, Rev. 17 and 18.

units.la: IV. Ut Antichristus sit haereticus, seu pseudo-Propheta, Christo vel clam, vel palam se opponens; quales maxime sunt Antichristi illi magni, ex quorum numero, tandem unus aliquis supra reliquos eximius emersit, qui sub nomine Christi, Christum maxime oppugnavit.
units.tr: IV. Antichrist is a heretic, or false prophet, opposing Christ either secretly or openly. Such were especially those great Antichrists, out of whose number at last one singular man emerged above the rest, who, under the name of Christ, most of all attacked Christ.

units.la: V. Antichristianismi illud mysterium aliquomodo jam se exeruit per multa retro saecula, in ipso mundi exordio; mox enim a promissione femine benedicto & post mentionem feminis serpentini, Gen. 3: 15. Abeli cum Caino intercessit inimicitia, quae non vulgares vel externas ob causas suborta est; sed propter justitiam fidei. Gen. 4: 7. Heb. 11: 4. Fide majus sacrificium Deo obtulit, prae Cain. 1 Joh. 3: 12. Non sicut Cain, ex malo erat, & occidit fratrem suum. Et cujus rei gratia occidit ipsum? quia opera ejus mala erant, fratris vero ejus, justa. Talis etiam contentio fuit inter Noachum & mundum infidelem. Hebr. 11: 7. 2 Pet. 2: 5. Idem etiam certamen fuit inter Isaacum & Ismaelem; Jacobum & Esavum. Vide Gal. 4: 22. & seqq.
units.tr: V. That mystery of antichristianity has already in some measure shown itself through many ages past, from the very beginning of the world. For immediately after the promise of the blessed seed, and after the mention of the serpent's seed, Gen. 3:15, enmity arose between Abel and Cain. It arose not from common or external causes but on account of the righteousness of faith: Gen. 4:7; Heb. 11:4: By faith Abel offered to God a greater sacrifice than Cain. 1 John 3:12: Not as Cain, who was of the evil one, and slew his brother. And why did he slay him? Because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous. Such a contest was also between Noah and the unbelieving world, Heb. 11:7; 2 Pet. 2:5. The same conflict was between Isaac and Ishmael, and between Jacob and Esau. See Gal. 4:22 and following.

units.la: VI. In Vetere Test. eadem semper fuit Satanae machinatio, quando variis & gravissimis afflictionibus Ecclesiam intricavit; quales potissimum fuerunt Aegyptiaca, Babylonica, Antiochena; cumque omnes monarchias adversas Ecclesia experta sit. In Novo vero Test. intrinsecus per haereses, schismata & hanc potissimum monarchiam, labefactavit magis doctrinam; tum vi, tum fraudibus: quum enim persecutionibus augeretur potius Ecclesia, quam exscinderetur, in omnigenas fraudes se convertit Satan, & frequentes impostores seu Antichristos excitavit; unde Spiritus Antichristi jam in mundo erat. 1 Joh. 4: 3. & iniquitatis mysterium jam tum peragebatur. 2 Thess. 2: 7. & ultima jam aderat hora, in qua Antichristi multi exstarent. 1 Joh. 2: 18.
units.tr: VI. In the Old Testament the devil's scheme was always the same, when he entangled the Church in various and most grievous afflictions. The chief of these were the Egyptian, Babylonian and Antiochene; and the Church has experienced hostile monarchies of every kind. In the New Testament, however, he has weakened doctrine from within, through heresies, schisms and above all this monarchy, both by force and by frauds. For since the Church was increased rather than destroyed by persecutions, Satan turned himself to frauds of every kind and raised up many impostors or antichrists. Hence the spirit of Antichrist was already in the world, 1 John 4:3; and the mystery of iniquity was already at work, 2 Thess. 2:7; and the last hour was already present, in which many antichrists would arise, 1 John 2:18.

units.la: VII. Tales autem erant falsi fratres & pseudo-Apostoli, de quibus passim graviter conqueritur Paulus. qui erant ψευδαπόστολοι. Gal. 2: 4. 2 Cor. 11: 13. ψευδαπόστολοι. com. ϛ6. οἱ ἐξ ἰεσδαίας. Phil. 1: 16. Nominatim vero illi fuerunt Ebion, aliique, qui de Christo perversa & blasphema locuti sunt. 1 Joh. 2: 22. Quis est mendax? nisi negans, quod Jesus sit Christus? hic est Antichristus negans patrem & filium. & 4: 3. Ex quibus haeresibus natae fuerunt contentiones, ut se invicem odissent Christiani. Matth. 24: 10. Et tunc offendentur multi, & se invicem prodent, & odio habebunt se invicem. Sicut contra in melio rum partium factionibus dignatio & aestimatio Doctorum nimium quantum augebatur; indeque Episcoporum evectio & πρωτοκαθεδρία.
units.tr: VII. Such were the false brothers and false apostles about whom Paul complains bitterly on all sides, who were false apostles [ψευδαπόστολοι], Gal. 2:4; 2 Cor. 11:13; false apostles [ψευδαπόστολοι], compare those of the circumcision, Phil. 1:16. By name they were Ebion and others, who spoke of Christ in a perverse and blasphemous way. 1 John 2:22: Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. And 4:3. From these heresies arose contentions, so that Christians hated one another. Matt. 24:10: And then many will be offended, and will betray one another, and will hate one another. On the other hand, within the factions of the better party, the esteem and reputation of the teachers grew excessively; and from this came the elevation of bishops and the πρωτοκαθεδρία.

units.la: VIII. Haec prima fuerunt initia, quae paulatim eo excreverunt, ut in universalem apostasiam, & omnimodam a fide defectionem erumperent; quam praedixerat Paulus 1 Tim. 4: 1. & seqq. ad quam non uno statim impetu, sed sensim miro astu Ecclesiam transvexit Satanas: qui cum in Imperio hactenus vi veritatem oppresserat, quam tamen inde non obscurari, sed splendidiorem undique emicare comperiebatur; in alias se vertit artes, & in Angelum lucis se transfiguravit; ut jam regno suo inter gentes deturbandus, hac specie in ipsa Ecclesia regnum obtineret; ad quod institutum non Romani Caesares erant sollicitandi, sed adeundi Pontifices Romani; quos, ostensa mundi gloria, omnique hierarchiae splendore, facile in suas partes pertraxit. Accensa igitur in illis ambitione dentissima dominandi libidine, ipsam religionem pessum dedit, & foedavit turpiter; tandemque etiam postliminio paganismum nomine Christi incrustatum in Ecclesiam reduxit. Ne vero invitis imperatoribus & Clero grande hoc opus moliretur, singularis auctoritas Episcopo Romano fuit concilianda, tum ex magnitudine urbis Romae; tum ex praetensa Petri cathedra & successione; tum ex primorum illius urbis Episcoporum pietate & virtutibus. Unde paulatim in illud fastigium ascendit Papa; ut per imperii casum; partim deferentibus Romam imperatoribus; partim deferrente & rejiciente imperatores suos Roma, omnibus major sit visus, & pro capite Ecclesiae, atque universali Episcopo se venditare ausus.
units.tr: VIII. These were the first beginnings, which gradually grew to such a point that they burst forth into a universal apostasy and a complete defection from the faith, which Paul had foretold, 1 Tim. 4:1 and following. Satan carried the Church over to this not in one sudden onslaught but gradually and with wonderful craft. For since in the Empire he had hitherto oppressed the truth by force, yet found that it was not obscured by this but shone forth more brightly on every side, he turned to other arts and transformed himself into an angel of light. Thus, since he was to be thrown down from his kingdom among the nations, he might obtain a kingdom in the Church itself under this appearance. For this purpose he had to court not the Roman emperors but the Roman bishops, whom, by displaying the glory of the world and all the splendour of the hierarchy, he easily drew to his side. Thus, once ambition was kindled in them with the most shameless lust of domination, he ruined religion itself and shamefully defiled it. At last, by a kind of return, he brought paganism, plastered over with the name of Christ, back into the Church. But so that he might not undertake this great work against the wishes of the emperors and the clergy, the unique authority of the Roman bishop had to be secured, partly from the greatness of the city of Rome, partly from the supposed chair and succession of Peter, and partly from the piety and virtues of the first bishops of that city. From this the Pope gradually rose to that height, so that, through the fall of the empire (partly because the emperors brought themselves to Rome, partly because Rome both sent away and cast off its emperors), he seemed greater than all and dared to present himself as the head of the Church and universal bishop.

units.la: IX. Firmato Papatui accessit Papismus, ex Judaismo & Ethnicismo conflatus, & utrumque, nefarie religionis adulterio, cum Christianismo commiscens. Ab Ethnicis enim ritus, idololatriam & superstitionem; Judaeis ritus quoque & paedagogiam Veteris T. mutuantes Pontifices, utramque Christiano nomine & habitu tinxerunt & circumvestierunt; quas tres religiones, hierarchiae vinculo culo colligatos,exhibet Papismus. Ne igitur aperta videretur Christianismi ejuratio, retentæ sunt in speciem Scripturæ Sacræ, Symbolum Apostolicum;& præterea ventilata fuit condemnatio præcipuarum hæresium tum florentium,ut Arianorum & Pelagianorum.
units.tr: IX. To the established papacy was added Papism, compounded of Judaism and heathenism, mixing both with Christianity in a wicked adultery of religion. For the Popes borrowed rites and idolatry and superstition from the heathens, and rites and the tutelage of the Old Testament from the Jews, and they dyed and clothed both with the Christian name and appearance. Papism presents these three religions bound together by the chain of the hierarchy. So that the renunciation of Christianity might not seem open, the Holy Scripture and the Apostles' Creed were retained in appearance; and besides, the condemnation of the chief heresies then flourishing, such as those of the Arians and Pelagians, was put forward.

units.la: X. Ut autem verum & indubitatum Antichristum se proderet, omnia Christi munera invasit. Propheticum puta, per substitutionem novi verbi ἀγενεῖς: sacerdotale per introductionem novi sacrificii, & intercessorum præter Christum: regium per dominium in conscientias, & imperium in vivos non solum, sed & mortuos. Magistratibus summum in modum injurius fuit; dum se & universum Clerum obedientiæ illius substraxit; & peculiare nullique obnoxium tribunal Romæ erexit, jus singulare condidit;calendarium novum pro auctoritate sua, orbi Christiano obtrusit; subjectos multos juramento fidelitatis exsolvit, regesque varios imperio & regnis exuit; atque ita sese supra omnem dictum Deum extulit. 2 Thess. 2:4. & in universam Ecclesiam intolerabilem tyrannidem usurpavit. quæ supra à nobis latius ostensa sunt.
units.tr: X. But so that he might reveal himself as the true and undoubted Antichrist, he seized every office of Christ: the prophetic, that is, by substituting a new word [ἀγενεῖς]; the priestly, by introducing a new sacrifice and intercessors besides Christ; and the kingly, by lordship over consciences and dominion not only over the living but also over the dead. He did the greatest injury to the magistrates, when he withdrew himself and the whole clergy from their obedience and set up a peculiar tribunal at Rome, answerable to no one, and established a law of his own. On his own authority he forced a new calendar on the Christian world, released many subjects from their oath of allegiance, stripped various kings of their rule and realms, and so exalted himself above every so-called god. 2 Thess. 2:4. He also seized an intolerable tyranny over the whole Church, as we have shown more fully above.

units.la: XI.Ex hac origine & progressu Antichristi,facilis est exist imatio quis eo titulo insigniendus sit. Romanus puta Episcopus; sive eo nomine intelligatur universus ille, ab aliquot seculis, Episcoporum ordo; sive etiam unus aliquis ex illis, cui καί ἐξοχὴν Antichristi conditiones & mores ad unguem conveniant. Dignoscendum vero illud est ex certissimis notis, quibus illum distinxit S. Scriptura,quæ non singulatim dividi, sed simul conjungi debent; quas potissimum posuit nobis Spiritus sanctus circa doctrinam, modum quo doctrinam suam orbi propinat & diffundit; tum etiam scelera, arrogantiam, tempus denique & locum, aliasque circumstantias. Atque eas ut nunc deprehendamus, & qui in Papam Romanum quadrent, videamus, opera danda est.
units.tr: XI. From this origin and progress of Antichrist, it is easy to judge who ought to be marked with that title: the Roman bishop, whether by that name is understood the whole order of bishops for some centuries, or even one of them in particular, in whom the conditions and character of Antichrist fit exactly, as it were pre-eminently. This must be recognised from the most certain marks by which Holy Scripture has distinguished him, which must not be divided one by one but joined together. Chiefly, the Holy Spirit has set these before us in regard to his teaching, the manner in which he pours out and spreads his teaching to the world, and then his crimes, arrogance, and finally the time and place, and other circumstances. Let us now take pains to see these, and which of them fit the Roman Pope.

units.la: XII. Doctrinam ejus, secundum quam futurus esset ἀντικείμενος & Antichristus, deformat egregie Apostolus Paulus 2 Thess. 2: 4. Sese opponens & superextollens in omnem dictum Deum, vel colendum; usque ut ipse in templo Dei, tanquam Deus sedeat, ostendens se ipsum, quod sit Deus. & Johannes 1 Epist. 2: 22. Quis est mendax, nisi is qui negat quod Iesu non sit Christus? Hic est Antichristus ille, qui negat Patrem & Filium. & 4: 3. Hinc Bestia secunda licet habeat duo cornua similia Agno, loquitur tamen ut Draco, Apoc. 13: 11. Sic & apostasia illi tribuitur 2 Thess. 2:3. 1 Tim. 4: 1. & αἱ ὀφθαί, Matth. 24: 12. & seductio, Apoc. 13:14. & fornicatio ac blasphemia, Apoc. 17: 2, 4, 5. quæ omnia Pontifici tifici Romano exacte conveniunt; cum doctrina Papismi, non solum sit apostasia à dogmatis Christianis; verum ipsorum etiam dogmatum canon, nimirum Scriptura omnibus modis in eo labefactetur & deprimatur.
units.tr: XII. The teaching by which Antichrist was to be the opponent [ἀντικείμενος] and Antichrist is well described by the Apostle Paul, 2 Thess. 2:4: he sets himself against and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God as God, showing himself that he is God. And John, 1 John 2:22: "Who is the liar, but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son." And 4:3. Hence the second beast, although it has two horns like a lamb, nevertheless speaks like a dragon, Rev. 13:11. Thus apostasy too is ascribed to him, 2 Thess. 2:3; 1 Tim. 4:1; and the love of many [ἡ ἀγάπη], Matt. 24:12; and seduction, Rev. 13:14; and fornication and blasphemy, Rev. 17:2, 4, 5. All of these agree exactly with the Roman Pontiff. For the doctrine of Papism is not only an apostasy from Christian dogmas, but also the very rule of those dogmas, namely Scripture, is in every way undermined and cast down by it.

units.la: XIII. Secunda nota concernit modum & rationem, qua falsa hæc doctrina diffusa est & propagata; quam indicat tum Paulus, tum Johannes. Ille triplicem eam facit. prima est per operationem mysterii iniquitatis. 2 Thess. 2. 7. quod notat, 1. Antichristum non subito emersurum; sed paulatim promovendum esse. Nec aliter in Papa repræsentatum est; cujus ne quidem nomen in Novo Test. inter tot alios Episcopos legitur, sed deinceps ex tenuibus initiis, lento progressu, ad culmen illud summæ & haud impune contemptæ auctoritatis pervenit. Quod etiam adumbratum est Apoc. 13: 1. in bestia secunda, quæ ex terra prodiisse dicitur. 2. Hæreses primas Antichristo inservisse, & utilem navasse operam; ideoque etiam, quoad ejus fieri potuit, ab illo esse adoptatas, sicut ex plurimis hæresibus, ingens eorum chaos conflavit & Papismum cudit.
units.tr: XIII. The second mark concerns the manner and method by which this false doctrine has been spread and propagated; both Paul and John indicate it. Paul makes it threefold. The first is by "the working of the mystery of iniquity," 2 Thess. 2:7. This signifies, first, that Antichrist would not emerge suddenly but would be advanced little by little. Nor is he represented otherwise in the Pope, whose name is not even read in the New Testament among so many other bishops; but from slender beginnings, by slow progress, he reached that peak of supreme authority, which is not contemned without penalty. This is also foreshadowed in Rev. 13:1, in the second beast, which is said to have come up out of the earth. Second, the first heresies served Antichrist and performed a useful work for him; and therefore, so far as possible, he adopted them, just as from very many heresies he fused together their vast chaos and coined Papism.

units.la: XIV. Alter modus; est quod venturus sit cum signis & prodigiis mendacii. 2. Thess. 2: 9. Apoc. 13: 13, 14. Et faciebat signa magna, ut & ignem fuceret descendere ex cœlo in terram coram hominibus. Et seducebat habitantes in terra, propter signa, quæ ipsi datum erat facere coram bestia. Signa vero mendacii appellantur, 1. quia falsa sunt, non vera miracula. 2. quia conficta sunt. 3. quia, licet quandoque vera fuerint, tamen mendacio inserviunt. Atque hæc Papismo convenire, quis non videat? cum apud eos miracula notam ponant veræ Ecclesiæ; & pleraque vel commentitia sint, vel in speciem tantum facta; vel saltem ad doctrinam falsam fulciendam faciant, etiamsi forte, quod præfracte negare nolumus, vera quandoque miracula, ad invocationem nominis divini, in Papatu a doctoribus patrata sint, per quæ fideles in Papatu superstites tentarentur, qualia nonnunquam fieri patet ex cautela illa Deut. 13: 1. & seqq. & infideles in superstitione confirmarentur.
units.tr: XIV. The other manner is that he will come "with signs and lying wonders," 2 Thess. 2:9; Rev. 13:13, 14: "And he did great signs, so that he even made fire come down from heaven to earth before men. And he deceived those who dwell on the earth, because of the signs which were given to him to perform before the beast." The signs are called "lying" because, first, they are false, not true miracles; second, because they are made up; third, because, although they are sometimes genuine, they nevertheless serve a lie. Who does not see that these apply to Papism, since among them miracles are counted as the mark of the true Church, and most of them are either fabricated or done only in appearance, or at least serve to prop up false doctrine? Even though, as we do not wish to deny stubbornly, true miracles were sometimes wrought in the Papacy by teachers, through the invocation of the divine name, by which the faithful who remained in the Papacy might be tested, as it is plain such things sometimes happen from that caution in Deut. 13:1 ff., and the unbelievers might be confirmed in superstition.

units.la: XV. Tertius modus est, omnis απάτη, fraus injustitia, 2 Thess. 2:10. qua nihil in Papatu manifestius est, & quæ omnium se oculis ingerit, in pervertenda S. Scriptura, falsandis patribus, & mille aliis, piis, sed falso nomine, fraudibus. Tribus hisce adjicit quartam rationem disseminandi adulteratam hanc doctrinam; crudelitatem nimirum Apoc. 17:6. Et vidi mulierem illam, ebriam de sanguine sanctorum et de sanguine testium Jesu. Vide & Apoc. 12: 13. &. 13: 7. Et datum est ei bellum facere cum sanctis, et vincere eos. & com. 15. & cap. 11: 7. Et cum finierint (duo testes) testimonium suum, bestia ascendens de abysso faciet cum iis bellum, et vincet eos: et occidet eos, quae omnia in Papam quadrare, testantur horrendae ejus a tempore Gregorii VII. in Albigenses, aliosque fideles persecutiones.
units.tr: XV. The third manner is "all deceit of unrighteousness," 2 Thess. 2:10, in which nothing is more evident in the Papacy, and which thrusts itself before everyone's eyes: in perverting Holy Scripture, in falsifying the Fathers, and in a thousand other frauds, pious in name but false in fact. To these three he adds a fourth means of spreading this corrupted doctrine: namely, cruelty, Rev. 17:6: "And I saw that woman, drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus." See also Rev. 12:13 and 13:7: "And it was given to him to make war with the saints and to overcome them," and verse 15, and chapter 11:7: "And when they (the two witnesses) have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up from the abyss will make war with them, and will overcome them, and kill them." All these things apply to the Pope, as the horrible persecutions of the Albigenses and other faithful ones since the time of Gregory VII bear witness.

units.la: XVI. Scelerosa vita & luxus, tertia nota est, ex qua discernendus Antichristus. Hanc ob causam, ex phrasi Hebraica vocatur filius peccati 2. Thess. 2: 3. & improbus. Esai. 11: 4. ὁ ἄνομος. 2. Thess. 2: 8. scelerum ejus catalogus nectitur Apoc. 17: 1. & seqq. quem non minorem Paparum vita ex vitiorum omnium confluge & perpetua serie constans, exhibet. Luxus eius enarratur Apoc. 17: 4. Et mulier illa amicta purpura et coccino, et inaurata auro et lapide pretioso et margaritis, habens aureum poculum in manu sua. & 18: 14. qui in patrimonio Petri & infinitis pecuniarum aucupiis luculenter se exleruit.
units.tr: XVI. A sinful life and luxury is the third mark by which Antichrist is to be discerned. For this reason, in Hebrew phrasing he is called "son of sin," 2 Thess. 2:3, and "wicked," Isa. 11:4; "the lawless one," 2 Thess. 2:8. His catalogue of crimes is set out in Rev. 17:1 ff., which the life of the Popes, consisting of a confluence of all vices and an unbroken series, displays no less. His luxury is described in Rev. 17:4: "And that woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stone and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand"; and in 18:14. He has shown himself brilliantly in the patrimony of Peter and in endless pursuit of money.

units.la: XVII. Quarta nota Antichristi est, arrogantia qua se supra omnia effert. 2. Thess. 2: 4. Qui se superextollit in omnem dictum Deum, aut colendum. Quae superbia peccatorum omnium ultimum & summum est, in regno Christi, ubi fratres sedent pariter, Psal. 133: 1. Praedicta illa est de Antichristo. Dan. 11: 36, 37. Et efferet se et magnificabit se supra omnem Deum, et contra Deum Deorum loquetur mirabilia — et non habebit rationem ullius Dei; quia supra omnia magnificabit se. & Esai. 14: 4. & seqq. ubi sub typo & typho regis Babylonii, qui similis volebat esse altissimo, Babylon mystica describitur.
units.tr: XVII. The fourth mark of Antichrist is arrogance, by which he lifts himself above all things. 2 Thess. 2:4: "who exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship." This pride is the last and greatest of all sins, in the kingdom of Christ, where "brothers dwell together in unity," Ps. 133:1. This was foretold of Antichrist, Dan. 11:36, 37: "And he will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and will speak marvellous things against the God of gods ... and he will not regard any god, for he will magnify himself above all." And Isa. 14:4 ff., where, under the type and pride of the king of Babylon, who wished to be like the Most High, mystical Babylon is described.

units.la: XVIII. Ordine & distincte proponitur haec arrogantia. 1. In eo, quod sese superextollat in omnem dictum Deum, com. 4. seu Deos nuncupativos, quales erant sub Veteri Test. quique in N. Test. abrogati sunt a Christo Psal. 82: 6, 7. Dixi quidem Dei estis — attamen moriemini. Unde illi dicti Dei, ad quos sermo Dei factus est, Joh. 10: 34. qui sunt principes saeculi hujus qui abolentur. 1. Cor. 2: 6. 8. atque ita se effert Papa, 1. subjiciens sibi eos, qui in Veteri Test. & quo tempore scribebat Paulus, appellabantur dii: vult enim sacerdotes & principes omnes Veteris Test. sibi subjectos esse, & ad se accedere debere, ob peccatorum expiationem, utpote, qui praeter Christum fungatur sacerdotio, secundum ordinem Melchizedechi. 2. Subjicit Ecclesiam Novi Test. sibi ipsi, tanquam Deo nuncupativo, majori cum violentia, quam olim sub Veteri Test. cum ibi dii isti nihil agerent, nisi ex jussu & permissione; hic autem plurima & omnia ferme operetur ex motu & ἐνεργείᾳ proprio.
units.tr: XVIII. This arrogance is set out in order and distinctly. First, in that he exalts himself "above every so-called god," v. 4, that is, the nominal gods, such as existed under the Old Testament and which were abrogated by Christ in the New Testament, Ps. 82:6, 7: "I said, indeed, you are gods ... nevertheless you shall die." Hence those "gods to whom the word of God came," John 10:34, who are "the rulers of this age, who are brought to nothing," 1 Cor. 2:6, 8. So the Pope exalts himself: first, by subjecting to himself those who in the Old Testament, and at the time Paul wrote, were called gods; for he wishes all the priests and princes of the Old Testament to be subject to him and to come to him for the expiation of sins, as one who, apart from Christ, exercises priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek. Second, he subjects the Church of the New Testament to himself, as to a god in name, with greater violence than under the Old Testament, when those gods did nothing except by command and permission; but he now works very many, almost all things, by his own motion and power.

units.la: XIX. ii. Quod efferat se ipsum supra omne σέβασμα, colendum, cultumve. com. 4. Quo vocabulo tum omnes dii falsi significantur, Act. 17: 23. tum etiam imperatores Romani. Ita etiam diis suis fictitiis, sanctis, quos divos facit, & Deo missatico majorem se exhibet Papa. Quo pacto etiam imperatoribus Romanis, qui olim Σεβαστοι, augusti dicebantur, non solum se praeposuerit saepe, sed & sceleste saepe eos infra se abjecerit, supra vidimus.
units.tr: XIX. ii. That he exalts himself above every sebasma [σέβασμα], that is, every object of worship or cult. com. 4. By this word are signified both all false gods, Acts 17:23, and also the Roman emperors. So too the Pope shows himself greater than his fictitious saints, whom he makes into gods, and than the god of the Mass. In the same way he has often set himself above the Roman emperors, who were once called Sebastoi [Σεβαστοί], Augusti, and he has often wickedly cast them beneath himself, as we have seen above.

units.la: XX. iii. Quod sit sessurus in templo Dei, tanquam Deus, demonstrans semet ipsum, quod Deus sit. com. 4. Quomodo in templo Dei sedeat, jam explicavimus. Quod autem tanquam Deum se ibi ostendat, undecunque patet. Nam 1. Arrogat sibi titulos Dei; cum vocatur 1. Unicus in terris Deus, & supremum in terris numen. 2. Christus. 3. Fundamentum Ecclesiae. 4. Sponsus Ecclesiae. 5. Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. 6. Leo e tribu Juda, radix David, & Salvator. 7. Ille, cui data est potestas in coelo & in terra. 8. Sacerdos summus, secundum ordinem Melchizedek. 9. Dominus, Rex, monarcha, caput Ecclesiae: quae omnia & similia sunt nomina blasphemiae. Apoc. 17: 3. 11. Non solum titulos sibi arrogat, sed & usurpationem divinae potestatis. 1. Cum statuitur Dei vicem in terris gerere, & coelste habere arbitrium, & rationes rerum posse immutare, & dispensandi potestas ipsi tribuitur, contra statum universalem Ecclesiae, contra concilia, Apostolos, Euangelium & ipsum Deum. 2. Cum sibi adscribit quae Dei & Christi sunt, ut 1. quando fidem sibi adstringit, tanquam unico verbi Dei interpreti, & legislatori infallibili, qui nemini rationem negotiorum suorum debet. 2. Quando ex auctoritate peccata vel retinet vel remittit, & leges fert conscientiam obligantes.
units.tr: XX. iii. That he will sit in the temple of God, as God, showing himself to be God. com. 4. How he sits in the temple of God we have already explained. That he presents himself there as God is evident everywhere. For 1. he claims for himself the titles of God. He is called 1. the only God on earth and the supreme divinity on earth. 2. Christ. 3. The foundation of the Church. 4. The bridegroom of the Church. 5. The Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world. 6. The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, and the Saviour. 7. He to whom power is given in heaven and on earth. 8. The high priest, after the order of Melchizedek. 9. Lord, King, monarch, head of the Church. All these and similar names are names of blasphemy. Rev. 17:3. 11. He not only claims titles for himself but also usurps divine power. 1. When he is set up to act in God's place on earth, to hold authority in heaven, to be able to change the reasons of things, and when the power of dispensing is attributed to him, against the universal state of the Church, against councils, the Apostles, the Gospel and God himself. 2. When he ascribes to himself what belongs to God and Christ: 1. when he binds faith to himself as the sole interpreter of God's word and infallible lawgiver, who owes an account of his dealings to no one; 2. when by his authority he either retains or remits sins, and issues laws that bind the conscience.

units.la: 3. Quando omnem potestatem & missionem ministrorum Ecclesiae intervertit, & ad se revocat. 4. Quando se constituit ut medium inter Deum & homines, sine quo ad Deum accedi non possit.
units.tr: 3. When he overturns all power and mission of the ministers of the Church and recalls it to himself. 4. When he sets himself up as the mediator between God and men, without whom there can be no access to God.

units.la: XXI. iii. Tribuit sibi quae regno Christi omnimodo adversantur, cum nempe mutat tempora & legem. Dan. 7: 25. Tempora scilicet, cum pro temporibus Spiritus, gratiae & libertatis, revocat tempora literae, irae, & servitutis; & regnum suum terrestre introducit; cum peccatorum quotidiana commemoratione, & multiplici servitutis onere. Legem mutat, per omnigenas alterationes & dispensationes; contra legem Christi. XXII. iv. Ipsam denique non respuit adorationem. 1. Cum imperatores & reges ipsum adorare dicuntur. 2. Cum Cardinales ipsum humeris suis altari impositum adorant. 3. Cum acquiritur; an adoratio hæc ὑπερδουλία, an vero λατρεία sit, qua Christianorum hic Deus colitur; juxta illud Pf. 72: 11. Et incurvabunt se ei omnes reges: omnes gentes ei servient: ex illorum detorsione.
units.tr: XXI. iii. He attributes to himself things utterly opposed to the kingdom of Christ, namely that he changes times and law, Dan. 7:25. The times, that is, when in place of the times of the Spirit, of grace and of liberty, he recalls the times of the letter, of wrath and of servitude, and introduces his own earthly kingdom, with the daily remembrance of sins and a manifold burden of servitude. He changes the law through alterations and dispensations of every kind, against the law of Christ. XXII. iv. Finally, he does not reject adoration itself. 1. When emperors and kings are said to adore him. 2. When Cardinals adore him, carried on their shoulders and placed upon the altar. 3. When it is asked whether this adoration is hyperdoulia [ὑπερδουλία] or rather latreia [λατρεία], by which the God of the Christians is worshipped here, according to that of Ps. 72:11, And all kings shall bow down before him: all nations shall serve him, from their twisting of it.

units.la: XXIII. Tempus designatur 2. Theff. 2: 6, 7. Et nunc, quid impediat, nostis; ut reveletur suo tempore. Mysterium enim defectionis jam peragitur: tantum qui impedit nunc, donec de medio prodeat. Per quem retinentem Paulus Romanum imperium quod abolendum & imminuendum erat, denotare creditur. Quod ubi factum esset, continuo retegendus erat Antichristus; illud autem jam dudum contigisse, ipsa res clamat; cum nomen magis & umbra imperii Romani superfit, quam vera forma.
units.tr: XXIII. The time is indicated at 2 Thess. 2:6, 7: And now you know what restrains, so that he may be revealed in his time. For the mystery of iniquity is already at work; only he who now restrains will do so until he is taken out of the way. By the one restraining, Paul is believed to denote the Roman empire, which was to be abolished and diminished. Once this had happened, Antichrist was to be unveiled at once. That this had long since come to pass the thing itself cries aloud, since the name and shadow of the Roman empire survive rather than its true form.

units.la: XXIV. Præditus fuit locus Antichristi, tum a Paulo, tum Johanne. Paulus 2 Theff. 2: 4. dicit, τὸν ἀντικείμενον in templo Dei sedere: templum autem illud non aliud est, quam Ecclesia Dei.
units.tr: XXIV. The place of Antichrist was described both by Paul and by John. Paul, 2 Thess. 2:4, says that the opposer sits in the temple of God [τὸν ἀντικείμενον ... ἐν τῷ ναῷ τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι]. The temple, however, is none other than the Church of God.

units.la: 1. Cor. 3: 16. non quæ talis & adhuc sit & maneat; sed quæ talis antea fuerit, & esse debeat. Non aliter ac Jerusalem tempore Christi ἡγία πόλις vocatur, Matth. 4: 5. & 27: 53. eademque meretrix facta, fidelis tamen urbs nominatur. Esai. 1: 21. & templum ejus, domum Patris sui nuncupat Christus. Joh. 2: 16. & domam suam, cum esset spelunca latronum. Matth. 21: 13. In quo templo sessurus erat; id est, cum auctoritate dominaturus in eam, seu primam sedem occupaturus: sicut universam Ecclesiam sibi subjecit Papa.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 3:16: not the Church as it is now and still remains, but as it formerly was and ought to be. Just as Jerusalem in Christ's time is called the holy city [ἡγία πόλις], Matt. 4:5 and 27:53, and the same city is named a harlot made, yet a faithful city, Isa. 1:21, so Christ calls its temple my Father's house, John 2:16, and my house, when it was a den of robbers, Matt. 21:13. In this temple he was to sit: that is, he was to rule in it with authority and occupy the chief seat, just as the Pope has subjected the whole Church to himself.

units.la: XXV. Locum hunc etiam describit Johannes, Apoc. 17: 3, 9. Super 7 montes; & quod sit urbs illa, quæ regnum tenet in reges terræ. com. 18. quæ omnia tam clare Romam designant, ut fateri illud cogatur Bellarminus, quamvis ethnicam subsitituat; quod textui omnino repugnat; quandoquidem 10 reges, qui regnum nondum acceperant, illud à bestia accepturi narrentur com. 12: quod sub Papa demum factum est, non vero sub imperio Romano ethnico; cum quo nulla alia regna simul fuerunt, & à quo erepta quidem, non vero data aliis sunt nova regna.
units.tr: XXV. John also describes this place, Rev. 17:3, 9: upon seven mountains; and that it is that city which reigns over the kings of the earth. com. 18. All these things designate Rome so clearly that Bellarmine is compelled to admit it, although he substitutes a pagan city. This utterly contradicts the text, since the ten kings, who had not yet received a kingdom, are described as going to receive it from the beast, com. 12. That happened only under the Pope, not under the pagan Roman empire, alongside which no other kingdoms existed at the same time, and from which kingdoms were indeed seized, but new kingdoms were not handed over to others.

units.la: XXVI. Ex quibus argumentis omni dubitatione majoribus, invicte videtur probari, Pontificem Romanum esse Antichristum. Suboritur hinc vero quæstio, Num scilicet, hodiernus Papa, Antichristus sit: cui ut nunc satisfaciamus, res exigere videtur. Antichristum igitur eum dicimus, in quantum Pontificii affirmant esse Papam Romanum: cum vero illi negent de fide esse, Papam praesentem esse Papam, quandoquidem ex multis circumstantiis, iisque incertis, illud dependet; ita etiam de fide non est, praesentem Papam esse Antichristum, nisi quatenus constat eum esse Papam. Unde tamen non damnatur ipsius persona, sed munus tantum; licet satis probabile sit plurimos Papas esse <bl>αντιχριστους</bl>. Hinc pro varia rerum facie, orandum erit pro Papa, vel non orandum. Non orandum scilicet pro eo respectu muneris; orandum pro eo, quatenus homo est, & proximus noster, & viator; quatenus etiam orbis sui & terrarum suarum politicus est princeps, a subjectis pro eo orari debet.
units.tr: XXVI. From these arguments, more certain than any doubt, it seems invincibly proved that the Roman Pontiff is Antichrist. There arises from this, however, the question whether the present Pope is Antichrist, and the matter seems to demand that we now answer it. We say, then, that he is Antichrist insofar as the Papists affirm that he is the Roman Pope. But since they deny that it is a matter of faith that the present Pope is Pope, since that depends on many circumstances, and those uncertain, so also it is not a matter of faith that the present Pope is Antichrist, except insofar as it is established that he is Pope. Yet thereby the person is not condemned, but only the office, although it is quite probable that many Popes have been antichrists. Hence, according to the varying aspect of things, one must either pray for the Pope or not pray for him. He is not to be prayed for with respect to his office; he is to be prayed for insofar as he is a man, our neighbour and a fellow traveller. Insofar as he is also the political prince of his own world and lands, he ought to be prayed for by his subjects.

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Nos autem non tenemur crimine laesae majestatis Principum Pontificiorum, ubi Papam Antichristum appellamus. Nam 1. Non animo convitiandi id dicimus, sed jubente conscientia. 2. Non magis quam cum idololatriae accusamus Papatum. 3. Hoc ipso consulimus principibus Christianis, eorumque libertati, contra Papae tyrannidem. 4. Agnoscunt illud ipsum, ii Principes Pontificii, qui Papae auctoritatem, quam sibi in reges arrogat, repudiant. 5. Non omnes qui illi subsunt, antichristianos appellamus; cum plurimi eorum profunditates Satanae ignorent Apoc. 2:24. nec Papam Ecclesiae monarcham, sed primae sedis Episcopum duntaxat agnoscant.
units.tr: We are not, however, liable to the charge of treason against Pontifical princes when we call the Pope Antichrist. For (1) we say this not out of a desire to revile, but because conscience bids us. (2) We are no more guilty in this than when we accuse the Papacy of idolatry. (3) By this very act we look after Christian princes and their liberty, against the tyranny of the Pope. (4) Those Pontifical princes who reject the authority which the Pope claims over kings acknowledge this themselves. (5) We do not call all who are subject to him antichristian, since most of them are ignorant of the depths of Satan (Apoc. 2:24) and acknowledge the Pope not as monarch of the Church but merely as bishop of the first see.

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Asserta veritate, sequuntur refutanda Pontificiorum commenta, quos mirum non est hac in re tam turpiter hallucinari, & toto coelo aberrare; cum longe aliam sibi Antichristi faciem fingant, & ideam ejus plane mutent. Qua in re dum molimina eorum perpendimus, eadem fere caecitas occurrit, quae Judaeorum fuit in negando Christo, & pervicaciam suam iisdem ferme artibus defendunt; nec hic quicquam illis concedunt; a quibus etiam multa in hoc negotio mutuati sunt. Judaei enim commenti sunt Antichristum, Armillum ipsis dictum, quasi Ἐπημολαων vastatorem populi; quem narrant Romae e lapide marmoreo nasciturum, prodigiosae staturae; & gentium Messiam se jactaturum; donec cum ipso pugnet & inferior evadat Messias Ben Joseph; post quem caesum, surget tandem Messias Ben David, qui Armillum funde & occidet. Quae fabula iis demum temporibus contexta est, quando Papa Romanus, Christianis non solum, verum etiam Judaeis gravis esse coepit; unde per Armillum hunc Judaeos Romanum Anti-Christum designasse, ex omnibus indiciis liquidum fit. Quamvis recentiores fabulam hanc, paulo aliter recitent, alioque referant.
units.tr: Having established the truth, there follow the refutations of the Papists' inventions. It is no wonder that they wander so shamefully in this matter and stray so far from the truth, since they devise an entirely different face for Antichrist and wholly change his idea. As we weigh their efforts in this matter, almost the same blindness appears as was the Jews' in denying Christ, and they defend their obstinacy by nearly the same arts. Nor do they concede anything here to those from whom they have borrowed much in this business. For the Jews invented an Antichrist, called by them Armillus, as if [Ἐπημολαων] meant "destroyer of the people". They tell that he will be born at Rome from a marble stone, of prodigious stature, and will boast that he is the Messiah of the nations; until Messiah ben Joseph fights with him and proves the weaker. After he has been slain, Messiah ben David will at last arise, who will pour out and kill Armillus. This fable was woven in those times when the Roman Pope began to be burdensome not only to Christians but also to Jews; whence it is clear from all the indications that by this Armillus the Jews designated the Roman Antichrist. Although more recent writers recount this fable somewhat differently and refer it to other matters.

units.la: Dddd 3
units.tr: Dddd 3

units.la: XXIX. Horum vestigia prementes Pontificii, Antichristum fingunt singularem quendam hominem futurum, ex tribu Dan oriundum, qui pro Judæorum Messia se venditaturus sit; & spatio trium annorum cum dimidio, templum Hierosolymitanum instaurabit, orbemque subiget, usque dum à Christo in monte Oliveti vincatur & conficiatur. Verum nec Judæi e tribu Dan Messiam exspectant, nec cultus Judaicus unquam restituetur; nec tantillo temporis intervallo fieri possunt, quæ de Antichristo omnia prædicta sunt; & tum porro tam aniles sunt hæ nugæ, ut refutari dignæ non sint. Horum autem venia dari poterat experientia necdum edoctis, sicubi in similes gerras etiam aliquando sint quidam Patrum delapsi; quorum somnia avide arripuerunt Pontificii, dummodo eorum institutio aliqua ex parte favere viderentur.
units.tr: XXIX. Following in their footsteps, the Papists imagine that Antichrist will be a single particular man, born of the tribe of Dan, who will offer himself as the Messiah of the Jews. In a space of three and a half years he will restore the Temple at Jerusalem and subdue the world, until he is conquered and destroyed by Christ on the Mount of Olives. But the Jews do not await a Messiah from the tribe of Dan, nor will Jewish worship ever be restored; nor can all the things foretold of Antichrist come to pass in so tiny an interval of time. Moreover these fancies are so old-womanish that they are not worth refuting. Pardon could perhaps be granted for them to those not yet taught by experience, if some of the Fathers have at some time slipped into similar follies. The Papists have eagerly seized upon their dreams, provided that their own position might seem in some way to be favoured by them.

units.la: XXX. Majus igitur operæ pretium futurum erit, si paulo propius quæ contra nostram sententiam afferunt perspiciamus, & ad veritatem contendamus. Sic 1. respectu persona ejus, censent Antichristum esse singularem personam, ideoque Papam non esse, cum multi sint Papæ. Postulatum porro suum ita firmant. 1. Joh. 5:43. Antichristus vocatur alius qui venturus est in nomine proprio: ergo unus aliquis est & singularis. Resp. Censent quidam de Antichristo ibi proprie, saltem solo, non moneri, sed de quocunque pseudo-Propheta & pseudo-Christo, qui Judæos delusurus erat, qualis fuit Barcochebas, aliique. Sed & cum de Antichristo ibi quoque agatur, vox alius, indefinite ibi sumenda est, pro quocunque alio. ut Joh. 21:18. Alius te cinget & feret quo non vis. conf.
units.tr: XXX. It will therefore be more worthwhile if we look a little more closely at what they advance against our view, and press on to the truth. Thus (1) with respect to his person, they hold that Antichrist is a single person, and therefore that the Pope is not he, since there are many popes. They confirm this claim thus: 1 John 5:43. Antichrist is called "another who will come in his own name"; therefore he is some one singular individual. Answer: some think that the passage does not properly speak of Antichrist, at least not solely, but of any pseudo-prophet and pseudo-Christ who was going to deceive the Jews, such as Bar Kokhba and others. But even if Antichrist is also treated there, the word "another" must be taken indefinitely, for any other, as in John 21:18: "Another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish." Compare

units.la: XXXI. 2.2. Thess. 2:3,4. Ubi cum articulo dicitur; ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὁ υἱὸς, ὁ ἀνομος. Verum 1. articulus notat sæpe personam indefinitam, ut Matth. 12:35. ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος. Marc. 2:27. Luc. 4:4. Joh. 4:37. 2. Imperatores Romani communiter, dicuntur ὁ κατέχων. 3. Fuit etiam inter Pontifices, cui nomen illud κατ' ἐξοχὴν convenerit. 4. Incipiebat jam tempore Pauli operari spiritus Antichristi. 2. Thess. 2:7. 1. Joh. 4:3. non idcirco numero unus esse potuit Antichristus, sed potius repræsentative & successive. 3. Dan. 7. & 11. & 12. capp. Antichristus aliquoties dicitur unus rex. Resp. Eodem modo ac reliquæ monarchiæ, in quibus successive plures regnarunt, licet unus forte uniusque rex dicatur. 4. Apoc. 13:18. numerus bestiæ exprimitur, quo nomen ejus constet scilicet; nomina vero individuis tantum tribuuntur. Verum in textu nulla fit mentio nominis proprii; deinde ipsis saepe generibus nomina induntur; quare Irenaeus etiam nomen & numerum istum in populo Latino quaesivit. 5. Filius perditionis nuncupatur 2. Thess. 2:3. quem unam tantum personam esse, patet ex Joh. 17:12. & nemo ex iis periit, nisi filius perditionis. Verum eo ipso, quod hoc nomen pluribus in locis legitur, apparet illud competere multis individuis, licet non omnibus.
units.tr: XXXI. (2) 2 Thess. 2:3,4. Where it is said with the article: ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὁ υἱὸς, ὁ ἀνομος. But (1) the article often denotes an indefinite person, as in Matt. 12:35, ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος; Mark 2:27; Luke 4:4; John 4:37. (2) The Roman emperors are commonly called ὁ κατέχων. (3) There was also among the Popes one to whom that name κατ' ἐξοχὴν could apply. (4) The spirit of Antichrist was already beginning to work in Paul's time (2 Thess. 2:7; 1 John 4:3); therefore Antichrist could be one not numerically but representatively and successively. (3) Dan. 7, 11 and 12: Antichrist is sometimes called one king. Answer: in the same way as the other monarchies, in which several reigned in succession, although one king may perhaps be called the king of each. (4) Apoc. 13:18: the number of the beast is given so that his name may be known; but names are attributed only to individuals. Yet in the text there is no mention of a proper name; moreover names are often given to kinds themselves, wherefore Irenaeus also sought that name and number among the Latin people. (5) He is called the son of perdition (2 Thess. 2:3), whom it is clear is only one person from John 17:12: "none of them perished, except the son of perdition." But by the very fact that this name is read in several places, it appears that it belongs to many individuals, although not to all.

units.la: XXXII. 11. Respectu temporis habent etiam quae nobis op- ponant.
units.tr: XXXII. 11. Also in respect of time, there are objections they can bring against us.

units.la: Nimirum, ante adventum Antichristi, Euangelium jam toto orbe praedicari debuit; quod cum nondum factum sit, nec Antichristum etiam venisse oportet; secundum definitionem Salvatoris Matth. 24:14. Et praedicabitur istud Euangelium regni, in tota habitabili & tunc veniet finis. At praestitum illud non solum est ante adventum Antichristi, sed jam ante excidium Hierosolymorum; ad quod praedicto loco etiam respici videtur. ita Col. 1:5. Sermo veritatis jam in toto mundo esse dicitur.
units.tr: Clearly, before the coming of Antichrist, the Gospel had to be preached throughout the whole world. Since this has not yet happened, Antichrist cannot yet have come, according to the Saviour's definition in Matt. 24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the inhabited world, and then shall the end come. But this was accomplished not only before the coming of Antichrist, but already before the destruction of Jerusalem, to which the prophecy in that passage also seems to refer. So Col. 1:5 says that the word of truth is already said to be in all the world.

units.la: XXXIII. 111. Tempore Antichristi contingit tribulatio qualis, nec fuerit, nec erit.
units.tr: XXXIII. 111. In the time of Antichrist there will be a tribulation such as never was nor will be.

units.la: Matth. 24:21. illa vero necdum fuit. Resp. Non agitur ibi de Antichristo, sed excidio Hierosolymitano; cum ex ipsorum sententia, persecutio Antichristi ultima sit sutura; hanc vero ultimam non esse, ex textu apparet. iv. Sub Antichristo cessabit sacrificium juge, Dan. 11:31. 12:11. id est, caerimoniae & Missa. Sed 1. ibi, secundum multos, de externo & typico jugi sacrificio sermo est, quod per Antiochum fuit interruptum. Tum etiam verus cultus Dei, & meritum Christi per juge sacrificium adumbratum, tollitur quam maxime a Papa.
units.tr: Matt. 24:21 says this, but it has not yet happened. Reply: that passage is not about Antichrist but about the destruction of Jerusalem, since by their own view the persecution of Antichrist is still to come, and the text shows that this tribulation is not the last. iv. Under Antichrist the continual sacrifice will cease, Dan. 11:31 and 12:11, that is, the ceremonies and the Mass. But (1) there, according to many, the reference is to the outward and typical continual sacrifice, which was interrupted by Antiochus. Moreover, the true worship of God, and the merit of Christ foreshadowed by the continual sacrifice, is above all taken away by the Pope.

units.la: XXXIV. v. Enoch & Elias Antichristo se opponent, illi autem necdum venerunt.
units.tr: XXXIV. v. Enoch and Elijah will oppose Antichrist, but they have not yet come.

units.la: Sed fabulae & nugae haec sunt, quae simili modo etiam Judaeos dementarant. Matth. 17:10. Marc. 9:11. Urgent, tamen haec praedici. Mal. 4:1. Ecce, ego mitto Angelum meum, ut vacuam faciat viam coram me. Matth. 17:10. Apoc. 11:3. Et dabo duobus testibus meis, & prophetabunt dies mille ducentos. &c. At duobus prioribus locis Eliae tantum fit mentio, quia Johanne Baptista fuit repraesentatus. Luc. 1:17. Et ipse praecedet coram eo in spiritu & potentia Elia. Matt. 17:10.13. & 11:14. ultimo vero loco, non prioris, sed solius Antichristi fit mentio. vi. Apoc. 11:3. agitur de duobus testibus; atqui hi Enoch & Elias sunt. Verum de Enocho & Elia silet sacer textus. 2. Occidendi erant hi duo testes; quod illis non
units.tr: These are fables and trifles, which in a similar way have also driven the Jews mad. Matt. 17:10; Mark 9:11. Still, these things are urged as predicted.
