Mal. 4:1: Behold, I send my messenger, to prepare the way before me. Matt. 17:10; Rev. 11:3: And I will give to my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred days, etc. But in the first two passages only Elijah is mentioned, because he was represented by John the Baptist. Luke 1:17: And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah. Matt. 17:10, 13; and 11:14. In the last passage, however, mention is made not of the first but only of Antichrist. vi. Rev. 11:3 speaks of two witnesses; but these are Enoch and Elijah. Yet the sacred text is silent about Enoch and Elijah. 2. These two witnesses were to be killed, which does not fit them.

units.la: 5. Enochi & Elia.
units.tr: 5. Of Enoch and Elijah.

units.la: 6. duorum testium. non conveniet. Hebr. 11: 5. Persidem Enoch fuit translatus, ne videret mortem. & Elias in coelum vectus. 2. Reg. 2. 3. Testes hi secundum literam intelligi non possunt; vocantur enim etiam duo olea &c. sed mystice notant Scripturam Veteris & Novi Test. vel, ut alii volunt, paucissimos quosdam pios, qui Antichristo restiterunt.
units.tr: 6. Of the two witnesses. It does not agree. Heb. 11:5: By faith Enoch was translated, that he should not see death; and Elijah was carried up into heaven, 2 Kings 2. These witnesses cannot be understood according to the letter; for they are also called two olive trees, etc. Rather they mystically signify the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, or, as others prefer, a very few pious men who resisted Antichrist.

units.la: XXXV. vii. Antichristus regnabit tantum tres annos cum dimi- dio.
units.tr: XXXV. vii. Antichrist will reign only three and a half years.

units.la: Dan. 7: 25. & 12: 7. Sed 1. multi haec intelligunt de Antiocho, tanquam figura Antichristi, qui tanto tempore templum profanarit. Vide 1. Mach. 1: 21. & 4: 52. Ita Dan. 12: 11, 12. memorantur dies 1209. conser cap. 11: 31. & 1 Mach. 1: 58. & 6: 16. & 2. Macch. 11: 33. 2. Cum vero Apoc. 12: 14. illud Antichristo applicetur; fieri non potest, ut tantillo tempore illa efficiat, quae ipsi tribuuntur, & efficienda ab eo dicuntur. Dies ergo hi 1260 pro annis sumi debent. Vide Apoc. 12: 6. Nec insolitum hoc est; ut videre licet Ezech. 4: 6. Dan. 4: 29. & seqq. Apoc. 2: 10. de quibus annis infra etiam dicetur. viii. Nomen & character Antichristi non conveniunt Papae. Sed 1. nomen ejus in voce Λατεῖνος invenit Irenaeus; 2. Character bestiae in variis testeris communionis Romanae conspicuus est: communis character est in professione fidei Romanae, & obedientia illius. sed de his etiam infra.
units.tr: Dan. 7:25 and 12:7. But (1) many understand these things of Antiochus, as a figure of Antichrist, who profaned the temple for such a time. See 1 Macc. 1:21 and 4:52. So Dan. 12:11, 12 mentions 1209 days; compare 11:31, 1 Macc. 1:58, 6:16, and 2 Macc. 11:33. (2) But since Rev. 12:14 is applied to Antichrist, it cannot be that in so short a time he accomplishes what is attributed to him and said to be done by him. These days, therefore, of 1260 must be taken for years. See Rev. 12:6. Nor is this unusual, as may be seen in Ezek. 4:6, Dan. 4:29 and following, and Rev. 2:10, concerning which years will also be said below. viii. The name and character of Antichrist do not agree with the Pope. But (1) Irenaeus found his name in the word Λατεῖνος; (2) the character of the beast is conspicuous in the various testimonies of the Roman communion: the common character lies in the profession of the Roman faith and obedience to it. But of these things too, more below.

units.la: XXXVI. ix. Antichristus est gente Judaeus, proditurus e tribu Dan, & propter Judaeos praecipue venturus: quae longissime a Papa absunt. Verum falsae etiam sunt hae Antichristi notae, & male efficiuntur ex locis Gen. 49: 17. Num. 2: 25. conf. Esai. 14: 13. Dan. 11: 7. Jer. 8: 16. Apoc. 7: 5. & seqq. x. Sedem Antichristi esse Jerusalem & templum Salomonis: utpote qui in templo Dei sessurus. 2. Thess. 2: 2, 4. Apoc. 11: 8. Dan. 11: 45. Verum fabulosa haec sunt; nam 1. Hierosolyma & templum ita excisa sunt, ut nunquam sint restauranda. Matth. 24:
units.tr: XXXVI. ix. Antichrist is of Jewish race, will come forth from the tribe of Dan, and will come especially for the sake of the Jews: all of which are very far from the Pope. Indeed these marks of Antichrist are false too, and are wrongly derived from Gen. 49:17, Num. 2:25, compare Isa. 14:13, Dan. 11:7, Jer. 8:16, Rev. 7:5 and following. x. That the seat of Antichrist is Jerusalem and Solomon's temple, as one who is to sit in the temple of God, 2 Thess. 2:2, 4; Rev. 11:8; Dan. 11:45. But these things are fabulous; for (1) Jerusalem and the temple were so destroyed that they will never be restored. Matt. 24:

units.la: 2. Dan. 9: 26, 27. 2. Apoc. 11: 8. In foro civitatis illius magnae, quae vocatur spiritualiter Sodoma & Aegyptus, ubi Dominus crucifixus est. non ibi sermo fit de Hierosolyma externa; sed mystica, quae & Sodoma & Aegyptus dicitur; cum Dominus proprie Hierosolymae non sit crucifixus, sed extra portam, Hebr. 13: 12. 3. Dan. 11: 45. Et plantabit tentoria Appadno inter maria montis sancti. Sermo est aut de Antiocho; aut si ad Anti-Christum referatur, regnum aliquod in quo erit Ecclesia, designatur. XXXVII. xi. Doctrinam Antichristi, uti describitur in Scriptura, non profitetur Papa. ut 1. Negare Jesum esse Christum. 1. Joh. 2: 22. & negare adventum Christi in carnem. 1. Joh. 4: 2, 3. 2. Profiteri se Christum. 3. & Deum. Respond. Non illud aperte & directe fieri debebat, sed clam & indirecte; factis nimirum verba ejus negantibus; ut homines illi Tit. 1:16. uti etiam ab illo fit. 1. Cum maximam redemptionis partem Christo surreptam, in alias res transfert. 2. Cum mediatoris officium aliis etiam commune facit; hoc enim modo Salvator noster, nec Jesus, nec Christus est. 3. Cum veritatem carnis Christi negat in transubstantiatione &c. 4. Cum justificationem per solam in Christum fidem obtinendam negat. 5. Cum liberum arbitrium in bono, & perfectam obedientiam obtineri posse statuit. 6. Cum negat concupiscentiam esse peccatum, & peccata minuit, & quaedam ex eorum numero tollit. 7. Cum aliud fingit sacrificium λαςικὸν, quam Christi. 8. Cum dicit illum non solum venisse cum aqua & sanguine, sed & cum accidentibus panis & vini. 9. Cum, praeter legem Christi, aliam praescribit legem, aliud verbum, alium doctorem, aliaque plura, contra & praeter ea quae Christus instituit.
units.tr: (2) Dan. 9:26, 27. (3) Rev. 11:8: In the street of that great city, which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. The passage is not speaking of external Jerusalem but of a mystical one, which is also called Sodom and Egypt; for the Lord was not properly crucified in Jerusalem but outside the gate, Heb. 13:12. (4) Dan. 11:45: And he shall plant the tents of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain. The passage speaks either of Antiochus, or, if it is referred to Antichrist, it designates some kingdom in which the Church will be. XXXVII. xi. The Pope does not profess the doctrine of Antichrist as described in Scripture, such as: 1. To deny that Jesus is the Christ, 1 John 2:22, and to deny the coming of Christ in the flesh, 1 John 4:2, 3. 2. To profess himself Christ. 3. And God. Reply: this was not required to be done openly and directly, but secretly and indirectly, that is, by deeds that deny his words, as those men do in Titus 1:16, and as is also done by him. (1) When he transfers to other things the greater part of redemption, which has been taken from Christ. (2) When he makes the office of mediator common to others too; for in this way our Saviour is neither Jesus nor Christ. (3) When he denies the truth of Christ's flesh in transubstantiation, etc. (4) When he denies that justification is to be obtained through faith in Christ alone. (5) When he holds that free will can attain good and perfect obedience. (6) When he denies that concupiscence is sin, diminishes sins, and removes some from their number. (7) When he devises a sacrifice lay [λαϊκόν], other than Christ's. (8) When he says that Christ has come not only with water and blood, but also with the accidents of bread and wine. (9) When, besides the law of Christ, he prescribes another law, another word, another teacher, and many other things, against and beyond what Christ has instituted.

units.la: XXXVIII. 2. Christum se esse non aperte quidem profitetur & prae se fert Papa, quod nec in Antichristo requiritur; nec uti diximus, debet cogi ex loco Joh. 5:43. Per varias tamen ambages, non uno modo se Christum facere, ostendimus. 3. Deum se dicit Papa; id est ostendit se, tanquam sit Deus. 2. Thess. 2:4. non tanquam verbis prae se ferret, & se Deum salutari faceret; sed quia res eas praestat, quas non nisi Deus praestare potest; atque ita factis magis se Deum exhibens: quod tamen nemini nisi Deo competit. Confer Act. 12:22. Haec vero num frustra in Papa quaerantur, ex iis, quorum specimina superius a nobis edita, judicare licet. XXXIX. xii. Miracula Antichristi nunquam patravit Papa. Ut 1. ignem e coelo elicere. 2. Facere, ut imago bestiae loquatur. Apoc. 13:13,15. Resp. 1. Ignis ille vario significatu accipitur: vel pro donis Sp. Sancti; quae jactat Papa a se conferri; vel pro fulmine excommunicationis ad imaginem Eliae ignem e coelo impetrantis: seu de igne coelitus in terram demisso; tum a monachis, tum a Gregorio vii. novo Jove Elicio: seu potius id proponatur in exemplum magnorum signorum; & ignem de coelo elicere, tantundem sit ac stupenda miracula patrare. Nihil horum vero Papae denegari potest, cum omnia ipsi non uno nomine conveniant. 2. Imago bestiae quomodo per eum & in ipso loquatur, infra videbitur. XL. Atque ita absolvimus Pontificios; restat nunc debellandus, qui iii. ill.
units.tr: XXXVIII. 2. The Pope does not openly profess that he is Christ, nor does he display it, though this is not required in Antichrist; nor, as we have said, ought it to be forced from John 5:43. Yet, by various circumlocutions, we have shown that he makes himself Christ in more than one way. 3. The Pope says that he is God; that is, he shows himself as if he were God, 2 Thess. 2:4, not as if he declared it in words and had himself greeted as God; but because he does those things which only God can do, and so by his deeds displays himself as God more than by words. Yet this belongs to no one but God. Compare Acts 12:22. From those whose examples we have set forth above, one may judge whether these things are sought in vain in the Pope.

units.la: Pontificiis hac in parte velificatus fuit, illustris Hugo Grotius: qui, sicut Christum in Veteri Test. ita Antichristum in novo deprehendere vix potuit: atque ideo vaticinia Pauli ad Caligulam & SimonemMagum detorsit; ea quae in Epistola Johannis dicuntur, ad Barcochebam; quae vero tam exsertim in Apocalypsi canuntur, ad Trajanum & Apollonium Magum, & Domitianum deflexit, invitis licet verbis & rebus.
units.tr: Grotius sailed in the Papists' favour on this point, the illustrious Hugo Grotius. Just as he could hardly find Christ in the Old Testament, he could hardly find Antichrist in the New. He therefore twisted Paul's prophecies over to Caligula and Simon Magus, applied what is said in John's Epistle to Barcochebas, and bent what is sung so plainly in the Apocalypse to Trajan, Apollonius Magus and Domitian, though both the words and the facts resist him.

units.la: XLI. 1. 2. Thess. 2: 3, 4. Homo peccati & filius perditionis ipsi est Cajus Caligula.
units.tr: XLI. 1. 2 Thess. 2:3, 4. The man of sin and son of perdition is Gaius Caligula himself.

units.la: Sed inepte; sic enim Paulus vaticinatus fuisset, non de re futura, sed praeterita. Caligula enim diem clauserat, aliquot jam annis, & secundum Baronium, decem minimum, antequam Paulus haec scriberet; quae singula latius probare, nostrum non fert institutum. 11. Dies Christi. com. 2. cum ipsi sit dies excidii Hierosolymitani; ridiculum foret dicere, ante hunc diem proditurum Cajum suam impietatem, cum Cajus multis abhinc annis mortuus esset. 111. Templum Dei, ipsi est templum Hierosolymitanum, in quo imaginem suam positurus erat Caligula. At 1. templum Hierosolymitanum hic non intelligi supra docuimus. 2. Aliud est in templo sedere, aliud imaginem in eo collocare. 3. Neque Cajus imaginem suam in templum intulit, sed tantum conatus est.
units.tr: But this is foolish. Paul would have prophesied in that case not about a future event but about a past one. Caligula had ended his days some years earlier, by Baronius's reckoning at least ten years before Paul wrote these words, and it is not part of my plan to prove each of these points at length. 2. The day of Christ (v. 2) is the day of the destruction of Jerusalem, and it would be ridiculous to say that Gaius would reveal his impiety before that day, when Gaius had been dead for many years. 3. The temple of God is the temple at Jerusalem, in which Caligula was to set up his image. But (1) we have shown above that the temple at Jerusalem is not meant here; (2) to sit in a temple is one thing, and to place an image in it is another; (3) Gaius did not bring his image into the temple, but only attempted to.

units.la: XLII. iv. Apostasia, com. 3. est ipsi impietas Caligulae.
units.tr: XLII. iv. Apostasy (v. 3) is for him the impiety of Caligula.

units.la: Sed.
units.tr: But:

units.la: 1. Apostasia ita simpliciter & nude posita, nunquam notat malitiam unius hominis; nisi hoc expresse addatur. 2. Caligula Apostata non fuit, non enim defecit a fide, seu majorum, seu sui ipsius, cum ipse idololatriae a majoribus acceptae innutritus fuerit. v. Mysterium iniquitatis, sunt ipsi occulta Caji consilia. Verum 1. Mysteria proprie sunt arcana religiosa, quae hic nulla. 2. Nulla etiam consilia Caji, jam dudum mortui. vi. ὁ κατέχων, ipsi est Lucius Vitellius, Syriae praeses, qui remorabatur Caji impietatem. At 1. uti jam saepius responsum, Cajus jam dudum mortuus. 2. Nec reverebatur Vitellium Cajus, quem Syria excedere jussit. 3. Nec quidem Vitellius obstabat, quo minus Caligula se Deum appellaret.
units.tr: (1) Apostasy, stated simply and without qualification in this way, never denotes the wickedness of a single man unless this is expressly added. (2) Caligula was not an apostate, for he did not fall away from the faith, whether that of his ancestors or his own, since he had been brought up in the idolatry he had inherited from his ancestors. v. The mystery of iniquity (v. 7) is for him the hidden plans of Gaius. But (1) mysteries are properly religious secrets, and there are none here; (2) nor are there any plans of Gaius, who has been dead for a long time. vi. "He who restrains" [ὁ κατέχων] is for him Lucius Vitellius, governor of Syria, who held back Gaius's impiety. But (1) as has often been answered already, Gaius has been dead for a long time; (2) nor did Gaius show any respect for Vitellius, whom he ordered to leave Syria; (3) nor indeed did Vitellius stand in the way of Caligula calling himself God.

units.la: XLIII. vii. ὁ ἄνομος, qui revelandus est, non alius ipsi est, quam Simon Magus. Sed 1. repugnat series orationis; cum ex filo textus appareat, eundem esse τὸν ἄνομον cum eo, qui com. 3, 4. dicebatur homo peccati & filius perditionis. conf. com. 6, 7. 2. Particula τότε tunc com. 8. ex Grotii hypothesi, indicat illum revelandum fore, ubi Cajus occultum suum scelus animo aperuerit: haec vero advertens absurda esse, dicit Simonem Magum demum cognosci coepisse, anno Claudii secundo. Verum illud nec fert adverbium τότε nec cum reipsa convenit; siquidem Simon Magus jam antea impia sua dogmata disperserat. Vide Act. 8: 9.
units.tr: XLIII. vii. "The lawless one" [ὁ ἄνομος], who is to be revealed, is for him none other than Simon Magus. But (1) the sequence of the argument contradicts this, since it is clear from the thread of the text that "the lawless one" [τὸν ἄνομον] is the same as the one who in vv. 3 and 4 was called "the man of sin and son of perdition"; compare vv. 6 and 7. (2) The particle "then" [τότε], v. 8, on Grotius's hypothesis, indicates that he is to be revealed when Gaius has disclosed his hidden crime in his mind. But noticing that this is absurd, he says that Simon Magus only began to be known in the second year of Claudius. Yet that word "then" [τότε] neither bears this sense nor agrees with the facts, since Simon Magus had already spread his impious doctrines before that. See Acts 8:9.

units.la: XLIV. v. 1 1 1. Verbam ejusdem commatis; quem absumet Dominus Spiritu oris sui, detorquet ad adventum Petri Romam, & conflictum ejus cum Simone Mago, & reportatam ab eo victoriam. Sed falsa haec fabula est.
units.tr: XLIV. v. iii. He twists the words of the same verse, "whom the Lord will consume with the Spirit of his mouth", to refer to Peter's coming to Rome, his contest with Simon Magus and the victory he won over him. But this story is false.

units.la: Nam 1. Cum certamen illud publice peractum dicatur, nullus scriptor Romanus illius meminit. 2. Ipsi inter Patres quidam, pro dubio & falso hoc factum habent. 3. Deceptus fuit Justinus Martyr, & post illum alii; qui inscriptionem statuae in ponte Tiberino; SEMONI. SANCO. DEO. interpretatus est, Simoni Sancto, Deo; ac si Simon Magus illa esset posita. Vero simile autem nequaquam fit, Magus publice tam turpiter victo collocatam esse hanc statuam. Inscripta erat haec statua non Simoni, sed Semoni, qui & Sancus, & Sangus, & Fidius dicitur.
units.tr: For (1) although that contest is said to have taken place publicly, no Roman writer mentions it. (2) Some of the Fathers themselves regard this event as doubtful and false. (3) Justin Martyr was deceived, and after him others, who interpreted the inscription on the statue on the Tiber bridge, SEMONI SANCO DEO, as "To Simon the Holy God", as though this statue had been set up to Simon Magus. Yet it is by no means likely that a statue would have been erected publicly to a magician who had been so shamefully defeated. The statue bore the inscription not to "Simon" but to "Semo", who is also called "Sancus", "Sangus" and "Fidius".

units.la: XLV. Ad Johannem transit Grotius, eumque male accipit, verba ejus detorquens.
units.tr: XLV. Grotius passes on to John, and treats him badly, twisting his words.

units.la: Sic 1. τὼ ἰᾶχάτῳ ὥεγν, 1. Joh. 2: 18. transfert ad excidium templi & Hierosolymorum: sed, cum omnes in eo conveniant, epistolam hanc ab Johanne, ab exilio reduce, in extrema senectute, scriptam esse, jam post excidium Hierosolymorum; eadem ergo haec ultima hora est, cum diebus extremis. 2. Tim. 3: 1. temporibus posterioribus. 1. Tim. 4: 1. & cum tempore illo, quod prope abest. Apoc. 1: 3. 11. Antichristus, qui venit. com. 18. ipsi est Barcochebas, qui sub Adriano imperatore Judaeos ad seditionem deduxit Sed 1. Non defecit ille Barcochebas a Christo. 2. Nec sedit in templo Dei. 3. Nec miraculis, aut mysterio, sed vi armata rem gessit. Idem ergo Johanni est ἀντίχριστος, qui Paulo est ὁ ἀντιχείμενος. 111. Antichristi multi, qui jam erant. com. 18. sunt ex ejus sententia pseudo-Christi, Judas Galilaeus, Theudas, Aegyptius ille. Act. 5: 36, 37. Simon Magus &c. Sed hoc erit tempora & rerum ordinem invertere, cum omnia illa contigerint, antequam Johannes haec scriberet. Intelligit igitur Johannes haereticos, Anti-Christi magni prodromos. 1. Joh. 2: 19.
units.tr: Thus (1) he refers "the last hour" [τελευταία ὥρα / ἐσχάτη ὥρα] of 1 John 2:18 to the destruction of the temple and of Jerusalem. But since all agree that this epistle was written by John, in extreme old age, after his return from exile, and after the destruction of Jerusalem, this is the same "last hour" as "the last days" of 2 Tim. 3:1, "the latter times" of 1 Tim. 4:1, and the "time that is at hand" of Rev. 1:3. (2) "The Antichrist who comes", v. 18, is for him Barcochebas, who under the emperor Hadrian led the Jews into rebellion. But (1) that Barcochebas did not fall away from Christ; (2) nor did he sit in the temple of God; (3) nor did he act through miracles or mystery, but by armed force. So for John the Antichrist is the same as what for Paul is "the adversary" [ὁ ἀντικείμενος]. (3) "Many antichrists, who already were", v. 18, are, in his view, the false Christs: Judas the Galilean, Theudas, the Egyptian, Acts 5:36, 37, Simon Magus, and so on. But this would invert the order of times and events, since all those things happened before John wrote these words. So John means heretics, the forerunners of the great Antichrist, 1 John 2:19.

units.la: XLVI. iv. 1. Joh. 4: 3. Ubi dicitur, Antichristum negare, Christum venisse in carnem, vertit cum carne, & carnem accipit pro statu humili, sine pompa & armis; cum quibus ut Judaei Messiam suum exspectabant; ita Antichristum vult, ad exemplum Judaeorum, negare, eum esse Christum, qui venit sine pompa. At glossa haec Sociniana repugnat phrasi Scripturae, ubi caro semper naturam Christi humanam notat. Joh. 1:14.1.Tim.3:16.Hebr.2:14.1.Pet.3: 18.Hebr.10:20.v. Antichristum. com.3.vult esse Barcochebam.Cum tamen ille Barcochebas necdum in mundo esset, quod tamen de Antichristo affirmat Johannes; sed deinceps sub Adriano emerserit. Spiritus igitur est Antichristi, operans in iis qui Christi adventum in carnem negabant; quem jam tum in orbe fuisse ex superioribus liquet.
units.tr: XLVI. iv. 1 John 4:3. Where it says that Antichrist denies that Christ has come "in the flesh" [ἐν σαρκὶ ἐληλυθότα], he renders it "with flesh", and takes "flesh" to mean a lowly state, without pomp or arms. Just as the Jews expected their Messiah with these things, so he wants Antichrist, after the pattern of the Jews, to deny that he is Christ who came without pomp. But this Socinian gloss contradicts the language of Scripture, where "flesh" always denotes Christ's human nature: John 1:14; 1 Tim. 3:16; Heb. 2:14; 1 Pet. 3:18; Heb. 10:20. v. He wants "Antichrist", v. 3, to be Barcochebas, although that Barcochebas was not yet in the world, whereas John asserts this of Antichrist; Barcochebas only emerged later, under Hadrian. The spirit of Antichrist therefore is the one working in those who denied that Christ had come in the flesh, and from what has been said above it is clear that this spirit was already in the world at that time.

units.la: XLVII. Tandem Apocalypsin ita interpretatur. 1. Apoc. 13. Bestia ascendens e mari, ipsi est idololatria: Bestia autem ascendens e terra, magia. Male vero; cum bestiae hae, non vitia quaedam, sed regna & imperia apud Prophetas notent. 11. Bestia secunda, est Apollonius Thyanaeus, magus, aequalis Domitiano imperatori. At 1. reponimus iterum, sic Johannes vaticinatus fuisset de praeteritis.
units.tr: XLVII. Finally, he interprets the Apocalypse in this way. (1) Rev. 13, "the beast rising out of the sea", is for him idolatry, and "the beast rising out of the earth" is magic. But this is wrong, since in the Prophets these beasts denote kingdoms and empires, not certain vices. (2) "The second beast" is for him Apollonius of Tyana, a magician, a contemporary of the emperor Domitian. But (1) again we answer that in this case John would have prophesied about past events.

units.la: 2. Cum Nero & Domitianus magos coercuerint, & speciatim posterior ille hunc Apollonium; ut magia tum multum decresceret; inepte haec bestia tunc emersisse dicitur. 111. Numerum bestiae. Apoc. 13. quaerit in pronomine Trajani ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ. Sed 1. Numerus hic non pertinet ad bestiam primam, sed secundam. 2. Nulla est ratio, cur numerus hic in nomine Trajani quaeratur, quo multi imperatores crudeliores & pejores fuerunt. 3. Neque in eo nomine numerus hic 666 invenitur; sed potius 860. enim finale 200 facit, quod Grotius imperite in vau ιπίσημον commutavit, quod 6 efficit.
units.tr: (2) Since Nero and Domitian had restrained the magicians, and especially Domitian had restrained this Apollonius, so that magic had then greatly declined, it is absurd to say that this beast had emerged at that time. (3) He seeks "the number of the beast", Rev. 13, in the name of Trajan, in the word ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ [basileus]. But (1) this number does not pertain to the first beast but to the second; (2) there is no reason why this number should be sought in the name of Trajan, since many emperors were crueller and worse than he; (3) nor in that name is the number 666 to be found, but rather 860. For the final letter is 200, which Grotius wrongly changed into the digamma (episemon), which makes 6.

units.la: XLVIII. iv. Apoc. 17: 10. & seqq. Septem regum, quinque priores, qui ceciderant, facit Claudium & quatuor sequentes imperatores; Sextum, qui jam erat, habet pro Vespasiano; Septimum, qui nondum venerat, pro Tito. Inepte iterum, cum Apocalypsis scripta fit, extremum, sub finem Domitiani; non vero sub Vespasiano, ut Grotius hic censet. 2. Si vero hi Romani Caesares intelligendi sunt, cur primum eorum facit Claudium, ante quem alii praecesserant? v. Bestia quae erat & non est. com. 11. censet esse Domitianum; quia primo absente patre dominatum Romae exercuerat; deinceps iterum privatus factus. Sed 1. Scripta haec sunt ultimis Domitiani temporibus: ut haec ad illum pertinere non possint. 2. Dilutum nimis est, ut ille tanta cum ιμφαίνει, esse & non esse dicatur, qui solummodo imperium alterius nomine exercet quo postea bstinet.
units.tr: XLVIII. iv. Rev. 17:10 and following. Of the seven kings, he makes the "five who had fallen" Claudius and the four emperors who followed him; the "sixth, who is", he takes to be Vespasian; the "seventh, who had not yet come", to be Titus. Again this is foolish, since the Apocalypse was written, as we have said, toward the end of Domitian's reign and not under Vespasian, as Grotius thinks here. (2) But if these Roman Caesars are to be understood, why does he make the first of them Claudius, before whom others had gone before? v. "The beast that was and is not", v. 11, he judges to be Domitian, because during his father's absence he had held power in Rome, and afterwards was made a private citizen again. But (1) these things were written in the last years of Domitian, so they cannot pertain to him; (2) it is too far-fetched to say that someone is said to "be and not be" with such a flourish, when he merely exercised power in another's name, which he afterwards held on to.

units.la: XLIX. vi. Bestiae decem cornua. com. 12. & 13. Sunt illi Gothi fœderati populi, tum necdum regnantes, sed postea concedentibus Romanis regnaturi. At i. Si bestia, cum qua decem hi reges regnum erant accepturi, sit Domitianus, ut Gothi eorumque fœderati decem illi reges sint, fieri nequit, utpote qui postea demum exorti sint. 2. Nec illi fuerunt cornua potentiæ Romanæ, cum illam everterint potius, quam stabiliverint. Intelliguntur ergo hic regna, quæ cum Antichristo, lapsis jam imperii Romani rebus, potentiam adeptura erant.
units.tr: XLIX. vi. "The ten horns" of the beast. Commentary on 12 and 13. These are the Gothic federated peoples, not yet ruling at that time but destined to rule later, once the Romans granted it. But: 1. If the beast with which these ten kings were to receive their kingdom is Domitian, then the Goths and their federated peoples cannot be those ten kings, since they arose only much later. 2. Nor were they the horns of Roman power, since they overthrew it rather than established it. The kingdoms meant here are therefore those which, with Antichrist, were to obtain power once the affairs of the Roman empire had fallen.

units.la: L. vii. Odium meretricis & illius ruinam rejicit in illa tempora, cum fœderati illi populi imperii hostes facti sunt. Sed populi illi sive reges, non sunt constituti reges, nisi everso jam imperio. Meretrix ergo, illiusque odium, non in imperium Romanum redundat, sed ad Antichristum spectat. viii. & ultimo denique vaticinium de urbe exurenda refert ad Totilæ incendium. Sed i. illud non plenam vel ultimam totius urbis vastationem apportavit; quale hic Babyloni portenditur, præsertim cap. 16.2. Christiani non debuerunt illi incendio insultare, uti præcipitur cap. 18:6, 20. 3. Nec Deus tum suos Roma evocarat, aut ex orbe Romano, in clade illa Gothica, sicut e Babylone populum suum transveturus dicitur. cap. 18:4.
units.tr: L. vii. He refers the hatred of the harlot and her ruin to those times, when those federated peoples became enemies of the empire. But those peoples, or kings, were not established as kings until the empire had already been overthrown. The harlot, therefore, and the hatred of her, do not spill over onto the Roman empire but look to Antichrist. viii. And finally he refers the prophecy about the city being burned up to the burning by Totila. But 1. that did not bring about the full or final devastation of the whole city, such as is foreshadowed here for Babylon, especially in chap. 16:2. Christians ought not to have exulted over that fire, as is commanded in chap. 18:6, 20. 3. Nor did God then call his people out of Rome, or out of the Roman world, in that Gothic disaster, as he is said to be about to bring his people across out of Babylon, chap. 18:4.

units.la: CAPUT XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: De duplici Bestia, & Ecclesiæ cum illa commixtione.
units.tr: On the two-fold Beast, and the mingling of the Church with it.

units.la: I. ON novum autem vel mirandum usque fuit hoc Antichristi regnum, cum jam ab antiquis retro temporibus prænunciatus & præscriptus sit filius hic perniciei; quem præsertim tum novis, tum repetitis ex Veteri Test. coloribus, ad vivum depinxit Apostolus Johannes in Apocalypsi illa admirabili, sub specie duplicis bestiæ; unius decem cornibus insignitæ; alterius bicornis: quas ut nunc repetamus & accuratius conspiciamus, non videtur ab instituto nostro alienum.
units.tr: Yet this kingdom of Antichrist was not new or wonderful, since this son of perdition was foretold and marked out long ago in ancient times. The apostle John painted him to the life in that admirable Apocalypse, with new colours and with colours taken again from the Old Testament, under the image of a double beast: one marked with ten horns, the other two-horned. It does not seem foreign to our purpose to recall these now and examine them more closely.

units.la: II. Prior bestia describitur Apoc. 11:7. & 13:1. & seqq. & cap. 15: 2. 16: 10. 17: 3, 7, 8, 11, 16, 17. & 19: 19. 20. & 20: 4, 10. Per quam bestiam nihil aliud intelligitur, nisi cœtus hominum animalium & car-
units.tr: II. The first beast is described in Rev. 11:7, 13:1 and following, 15:2, 16:10, 17:3, 7, 8, 11, 16, 17, 19:19, 20, 20:4, 10. By this beast nothing else is meant than a gathering of men who are animal and car-

units.la: Ecce 3 ... (signature line) carnalium, Spiritum Dei & fidem Christi non habentium; Christum tamen profitentium; id est, uno verbo, Ecclesia externa. Refertur haec bestia ascendisse ex mari, id est, ex mundo infideli; quando scilicet tempore Constantini, per totum imperium Romanum, ad Ecclesiam se multi adjungent, nimirum per assentationem. Dan. 11: 34. Dedit ei potentiam & thronum suum Draco. Apoc. 13: 2. h. e. diabolus, qui hactenus palam per idololatriam & persecutiones in imperio Romano dominatus fuerat, clam nunc operabatur, in Ecclesia illa externa, & mundanorum hominum regno.
units.tr: nal, who do not have the Spirit of God or the faith of Christ, yet profess Christ; that is, in one word, the external Church. This beast is said to have ascended out of the sea, that is, out of the unbelieving world, when, namely, in the time of Constantine, throughout the whole Roman empire, many joined themselves to the Church, certainly by flattery. Dan. 11:34. The dragon gave him his power and his throne. Rev. 13:2. That is, the devil, who had hitherto ruled openly in the Roman empire through idolatry and persecutions, now worked in secret, in that external Church and in the kingdom of worldly men.

units.la: III. Habebat haec bestia 7. capita. Apoc. 13: 1. quae 7 sunt montes. Apoc. 17:9. quae notant latissimum ejus imperium; unde & 10 cornua, 10 regna ejus significant. com. 12. Describitur etiam Apoc. 17:8. mirabili modo: quae fuit & non est, quamquam est: hoc est, quae consistat in tali externa politia, quae fuit quondam sub Veteri Test. non est, sub Novo: & est tamen, postliminio revocata scilicet ab animalibus hominibus.
units.tr: IV. One of its heads was wounded to death, and its deadly wound was healed (Rev. 13:3). The first happened under the reign of Julian the Apostate, when that external Church seemed to be crushed. The second happened under the succession of Jovian, for then that Church flourished again, and the beast was healed, just when the Church seemed to be healed.

units.la: IV. Unum ejus caput mastatur ad mortem & sanata est plaga. Apoc. 13:3. Prius illud factum, regnante Juliano Apostata; cum opressa videbatur Ecclesia illa externa; posterius autem contigit, succedente Joviano; tum enim illa iterum effloruit, & sanata est bestia, cum sanari videretur Ecclesia.
units.tr: V. There was given to that beast a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies (Rev. 13:5), when, surely, that hypocritical and pretended Church, or the Roman one, began to be regarded as the teacher, and to obtain authority as if it were infallible, and to abuse that authority by saying and doing things that did not serve the glory of God.

units.la: V. Datum est bestiae illi os loquens magna & blasphemias. Apoc. 13: 5. quando nimirum Ecclesia illa hypocritica & simulata, seu Romana, pro magistra coepit haberi, & auctoritatem nancisci, ac si infallibilis esset, eaque abuti ad loquenda & agenda ea, quae non inserviebant gloriae Dei.
units.tr: VI. All the inhabitants of the earth worshipped this beast (ibid. v. 8), that is, they joined themselves to that Church, which they believed to be the true one, and thus the true faithful were mixed with that kingdom.

units.la: VI. Adorabant omnes habitantes in terra bestiam hanc. ibid. com. 8. id est, ad Ecclesiam illam se aggregarunt, quam veram esse putabant, & ita regno illi permixti sunt veri fideles.
units.tr: VII. Then, or rather joined to the first beast, there followed another, having two horns like a lamb (v. 11). This was the rule of the teachers of the Roman Church, who boasted that they had the power of Christ to loose and to bind, which are the two horns of the lamb. This second beast is also called the false prophet (Rev. 16:13, 19:20), and the harlot sitting upon the first beast (Rev. 17:3), that is, subjecting the external Church and making it subject to itself.

units.la: VII. Successit autem, aut conjuncta potius fuit priori bestiae, altera, duo habens cornua, similia agno. com. 11. Quod fuit regnum doctorum Ecclesiae Romanae, jactantium se habere potestatem Christi, ad solvendum & ligandum, quae duo sunt agni cornua: haec secunda bestia, pseudo-Propheta etiam dicitur. Apoc. 16: 13. & 19: 20. & meretrix priori bestiae insidens. Apoc. 17: 3. id est, Ecclesiam externam subjugans, sibique subjiciens.
units.tr: VIII. This second beast persuaded the people to make an image of the beast (v. 14). This image was to represent and reflect the Church. This is the title of the Pope, who, as head of the Church and vicar of Christ, presents and represents the whole Church in himself. Hence it was given to false teachers to give breath to the image of the beast (v. 15), that is, to persuade men that the infallible Spirit of God resides with the Pope.

units.la: VIII. Altera haec bestia persuasit populo, ut facerent imaginem bestiae. com. 14. quae nempe imago Ecclesiam repraesentaret & referret; quod elogium est Papæ, qui tanquam caput Ecclesiæ, & vicarius Christi, omnem Ecclesiam exhibet in se & repræsentat. Inde datum est falsis doctoribus, dare Spiritum imagini bestiæ. com. 15. hoc est, persuadere hominibus, penes Papam residere Spiritum Dei infallibilem.
units.tr: IX. This beast has a law and a charagma, that is, a mark, so that they might give it to men, in their right hand, or on their foreheads (vv. 16, 17). These are the law and doctrines of the Roman Church, received by professing its name and by obeying its commands, just as in the Old Testament the law of God was commanded to be kept as a sign on the hand and on the forehead (Exod. 13:9; Deut. 6:8). Its number is 666, which Irenaeus long ago sought in the word Latinos [Λατεινος], and others have sought in many other ways; I will not describe these now, as I am hurrying on to other matters.

units.la: IX. Legem habet hæc, & χαράγμα seu signaturam, ut illam darent hominibus, in manu illorum dextra, aut in frontibus eorum. comm. 16, 17. Quæ sunt lex & dogmata Ecclesiæ Romanæ, recepta per prosessionem nominis, & obedientiam præceptorum ejus: sicut in Veteri Test. lex Dei jubebatur haberi signum in manu & in fronte. Exod. 13: 9. Deut. 6: 8. Numerus ejus est 666. quem olim Irenæus in voce Λατεινος, aliique multis aliis modis quæsiverunt; quos nunc ad alia properantes non enarrabimus.
units.tr: X. The time of the reign of this beast is forty-two months (Rev. 13:5; 11:2, 3), or 2260 days, which mark that many years. Within these days are included the thousand years during which the Dragon was bound (Rev. 12:9; 20:2, 3). That is, from the time when Diocletian's ten-year persecution ceased and Constantine the Great succeeded, when the external Church began to reign, yet in such a way that Christ reigned at the same time, though the beast itself bore the name of Christ and seemed to do everything in it. Meanwhile that woman is nourished by the Gentiles in the wilderness for 1260 days (Rev. 12:6, 14), that is, as we have already said, for that many years. These begin in the year of Christ 292, when Constantius Chlorus was made Caesar, who defended the Christians in the West, and end in the year 1552, when the Treaty of Passau was concluded, the freedom of the Reformed religion was granted, and peace in religion was then established, so that it was now lawful for all to go out of Babylon.

units.la: X. Tempus regni hujus bestiæ, est mensium 42, Apoc. 13:5. & 11:2, 3. vel dierum 2260; qui totidem annos notant; in quibus diebus comprehenduntur mille anni, quo tempore ligatus Draco fuit. Apoc. 12:9. & 20:2, 3. nimirum ex eo tempore, quo cessavit Diocletiana decennalis persecutio, & successit Constantinus Magnus; quando regnare cœpit Ecclesia externa, ita tamen, ut simul regnaret Christus, cum vel ipsa bestia nomen Christi præ se ferret, & in eo omnia facere videretur. Interea mulier illa alitur à gentibus in deserto per dies 1260. Apoc. 12:6, 14. id est, uti jam diximus, per totidem annos: qui inchoandi sunt ab anno Christi 292. cum Cæsar factus est Constantius Chlorus, qui Christianos in Occidente defendit; & terminandi in anno 1552. ubi facta est transactio Passavien sis, libertas Reformatæ religionis concessa, & pax religionis dein stabilita est; ut è Babylone jam omnibus exire licuerit.
units.tr: XI. Meanwhile the faithful witnesses of God prophesy, clothed in sackcloth (Rev. 11:2). These witnesses are either a few teachers who rose up before the Reformation against those corruptions that were pressing in, or rather, since they are called two, they signify Scripture of the Old and New Covenants, or the two classes of prophets, the Prophets and the Apostles, who prophesied in sackcloth, namely while the word of God was wrapped in human inventions so that its sense was less clear and less effective among men, because of the strife of words which the teachers pursued, which overthrow the hearers (2 Tim. 2:14).

units.la: XI. Interim fideles Dei testes prophetant amicti saccis. Apoc. 11: 2. Qui testes sunt vel pauci doctores, qui ante Reformationem contra ingruentes illas corruptelas insurrexerunt; vel potius, cum duo dicantur, notabunt Scripturam Veteris & Novi Fœd. seu duas classes prophetantium, Prophetas & Apostolos, qui saccis amicti prophetarunt, dum nempe sermo Dei humanis commentis involutus fuit ut sensus ejus minus clarus, nec tam efficax in hominibus fuerit, propter pugnas verborum, quas sectabantur doctores, quæ populum subvertunt. 2. Tim. 2: 14.
units.tr: XI. Meanwhile, the faithful witnesses of God prophesy clothed in sackcloth (Apoc. 11:2). These witnesses are either the few teachers who rose up against those creeping corruptions before the Reformation, or rather, since they are called two, they signify the Scriptures of the Old and New Covenant, or the two classes of prophets, the Prophets and the Apostles, who prophesied clothed in sackcloth, namely while the word of God was wrapped in human inventions, so that its sense was less clear and less effective among men, because of the disputes about words that the teachers pursued, which subvert the hearers (2 Tim. 2:14).

units.la: XII. Hæc ergo fuit Ecclesiæ cum bestia commixtio, seu ejus captivitas, ita tamen, ut manserit semper Ecclesia in ipso bestiæ regno; superstant enim aliqui, quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ &c. Apoc. 13: 8. prout promiserat Christus, portas inferni non prævaluturas Ecclesiæ. Matth. 16: 18. Effigiatur illud etiam Apoc. 17: 14. & præcipue 14: 1. ubi agnus describitur stans in monte Sion, cum 144 chiliadibus, habentibus nomen Patris Christi, in frontibus suis: quæ symbolica est descriptio electorum, significatorum per 12 tribus Israëlis spiritualis, numero duodenario in se reducto, unde efficientur 144. Horum signatorum perhibetur quadruplex vox, quæ audita fuit ante casum Babylonis. Apoc. 14: 2. & seqq. Nempe 1. Aquarum multarum; quæ sonuit sub Carolo Magno, in Francofurtensi & Parisina Synodis, & in Bertramo, aliisque. 2. Tonitrui magni, quæ audita est post annum 1000. sub Henricis Imperatoribus, à Berengario &c. 3. Citharædorum; qui sunt Waldenses. 4. Angeli æternum Euangelium nunciantis; quam vocem ediderunt Reformatores, à Wiclefo & deinceps; quorum prædicatio non cessabit, usque ad finem mundi.
units.tr: XII. This, then, was the mingling of the Church with the beast, or her captivity; yet in such a way that the Church always remained within the very kingdom of the beast. For some remain, whose names are written in the book of life, etc. (Apoc. 13:8), just as Christ had promised that the gates of hell would not prevail against the Church (Matt. 16:18). This is also depicted in Apoc. 17:14, and especially in 14:1, where the Lamb is described standing on Mount Sion, with 144 thousand, having the name of his Father and of Christ, written on their foreheads. This is a symbolic description of the elect, signified by the twelve tribes of spiritual Israel, the number twelve being squared upon itself, whence 144 arises. Of these sealed ones is reported a fourfold voice, which was heard before the fall of Babylon (Apoc. 14:2 and following). Namely: (1) of many waters, which sounded under Charlemagne, at the synods of Frankfurt and Paris, and in Bertram and others; (2) of a great thunder, which was heard after the year 1000, under the Emperors named Henry, from Berengar and others; (3) of harpers, who are the Waldensians; (4) of an angel proclaiming the eternal Gospel, a voice which the Reformers sounded forth, from Wycliffe onwards; whose preaching will not cease until the end of the world.

units.la: XIII. Hisce peractis, subsecuta est secunda mundi resurrectio.
units.tr: XIII. With these things done, the second resurrection of the world followed.

units.la: Apoc. 20: 12, 13. Sicut enim prima mundi resurrectio tum fuit, cum per prædicationem Apostolorum mundo nova vita infusa esset: cumque Deus mortuos in peccatis — vivificavit. Col. 2: 3. Eph. 2: 5. Ita secunda mundi resurrectio facta est, in prædicatione Euangelii, per reformationem, quando bestia & pseudo-Propheta conjecti sunt in stagnum ignis. Apoc. 20: 14. id est, quando cecidit regnum Antichristi. Cujus resurrectionis secundæ qui non facti sunt participes, illi manserunt in morte secunda, id est, defecerunt & indurati sunt, post veritatem agnitam, & ita secundo sunt mortui, sicut prima mors contracta est in Adamo; & horum conditio est miserrima. Nam anfugientes inquinamenta mundi in cognitione Domini & Salvatoris JesuChristi, his vero rursus implicati superantur: facta sunt eis posteriora deteriora prioribus. 2. Pet. 2: 20. Beatus & sanctus, qui habet partem in resurrectione prima: in his secunda mors non habet potestatem. Apoc. 20: 6.
units.tr: Apoc. 20: 12, 13. For just as the first resurrection of the world took place when new life was poured into the world through the preaching of the Apostles, and God made alive those who were dead in sins, Col. 2: 3. Eph. 2: 5, so the second resurrection of the world came about in the preaching of the Gospel, through the Reformation, when the beast and the false prophet were cast into the lake of fire, Apoc. 20: 14, that is, when the kingdom of Antichrist fell. Those who did not share in this second resurrection remained in the second death, that is, they fell away and were hardened after the truth had been known, and so they died a second time, just as the first death was contracted in Adam; and their condition is most wretched. "For if, having escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first." 2 Pet. 2: 20. "Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection; over such the second death has no power." Apoc. 20: 6.

units.la: LOCUS QUINQUAGESIMUS PRIMUS De Abolitione Anti-Christi & ulti- mis temporibus.
units.tr: FIFTY-FIRST HEADING: On the Abolition of Antichrist and the Last Times.

units.la: CAPUT XX. De liberatione Ecclesiæ ab Antichristo & Reformatione illius.
units.tr: CHAPTER XX. On the Deliverance of the Church from Antichrist and Its Reformation.

units.la: I. Rudentes imitati medicos, pestis hujus in Ecclesiam grassantis historiam, ab ultima origine repetiimus; antequam videmus, quo pacto sanata sit & pristinæ valetudini restituta; ut cognitis mali causis & initiis, medelam ejus eo facilius perspectam habeamus. Constat itaque nobis Papam esse Anti-Christum; cundemque sceleste thalamum Christi, verum sponsum mentitum, conscendisse; constat item qua fraude, quibus artibus, torum illum subsederit: contemplemur tandem etiam lætam tragœdiæ hujus catastrophen; ut exactus sit Antichristus, & liberata, magna ex parte, ab ejus jugo Ecclesia, caput extulerit.
units.tr: I. Like physicians, we have traced the history of this plague that spreads through the Church back to its earliest origin, before we look at how it was healed and restored to its former health, so that, with the causes and beginnings of the evil known, we may more easily have its remedy clearly in view. It is therefore established for us that the Pope is Antichrist, and that he mounted the defiled bed of Christ, pretending to be the true bridegroom. It is also established by what deceit and by what arts he settled into that bed. Let us finally consider the happy conclusion of this tragedy, how Antichrist was cast down and the Church, largely freed from his yoke, lifted up its head.

units.la: II. Prædixit jam olim Scriptura 1. regnum Antichristi non universale & perpetuum futurum; utpote quod futurum duntaxat erat usque ad tempus & tempora particulamque temporis. Dan. 7: 25. Unde cum Ægypto mystica, quæ notat regnum Antichristi, Apoc. 11:8. conjungit Scriptura regnum Assyrium, ut aliud & distinctum à regno Ægypti; de cujus progressibus agitur Mich. 7: 12. Dies ille est quo ad te veniet ab Assyria, ad urbes munitas &c. & Esai. 23: 13. Assyrius disposuit illam in ruinam. Quod regnum Assyrium cum regno Orientis convenire videtur. 2. Esai. 14: 22. vaticinium est de excidione Babylonis mysticæ: Excisurusfum Babylonis nomen & residuum filiumque ac nepotem, dictum Jehova. Vide & cap. 23: 18. & 25: 7. & 30: 33. 3. Zach. 5 : 7,8. Et ista mulier una consedebat in medio Epha. Et dixit: hæc est improbitas. Et
units.tr: II. Scripture foretold long ago, first, that the kingdom of Antichrist would be neither universal nor perpetual, since it was to last only for a time, and times, and half a time (Dan. 7:25). Hence Scripture joins the mystical Egypt, which denotes the kingdom of Antichrist (Rev. 11:8), with the Assyrian kingdom, as something other and distinct from the kingdom of Egypt, whose progress is dealt with in Mic. 7:12: That day he shall come to you from Assyria, to the fortified cities, etc. and Isa. 23:13: The Assyrian has appointed her for ruin. This Assyrian kingdom seems to coincide with the kingdom of the East. Second, Isa. 14:22 is a prophecy of the overthrow of mystical Babylon: I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, son and grandson, says the LORD. See also chs. 23:18, 25:7 and 30:33. Third, Zech. 5:7, 8: And this woman was sitting in the midst of the ephah. And he said, This is wickedness. And

units.la: Ffff Et conjecit illam in medium Epha, & conjecit lapidem plumbi in os ejus. Quæ mulier, improbitas appellata & Epha insidens, est meretrix illa, insidens agapis& bonis Ecclesiæ; quæ coercenda est onere validioris imperii, per massam plumbeam denotati. 4. Zach. 11: 15,17. Pastor stultus & nihili dominatur solum in Judam, id est, in illam Ecclesiæ partem, quæ catholica dicitur; non ergo in omnem ejus partem. 5. Huc etiam spectat remotio sceptri̇improbitatis. Psal. 125: 3. & fractio laquei. Psal. 124:7. & interfectio improbi. Esai. 11: 4.
units.tr: [And he cast her into the midst of the ephah, and cast a lump of lead upon her mouth.] This woman, called wickedness and sitting in the ephah, is that harlot who sits upon the love feasts and the goods of the Church; she is to be restrained by the weight of a stronger empire, denoted by the leaden mass. Fourth, Zech. 11:15, 17: a foolish and worthless shepherd rules only over Judah, that is, over that part of the Church which is called catholic, and so not over every part of it. Fifth, to this also belongs the removal of the sceptre of wickedness (Ps. 125:3), the breaking of the snare (Ps. 124:7), and the slaying of the wicked (Isa. 11:4).

units.la: III. 6. Matth. 13: 41, 42. Prædicitur zizaniorum in fasciculos collectio & in ignem conjectio. 7. Præcipue de hoc negotio agitur in Apocalypsi, ubi cap. 11:3. Duo testes revivisc​unt. & cap. 14: 6. æternum Evangelium prædicatur, & deinceps ruina Babylonis denunciatur. Apoc. 16. septem commemorantur plaga, sub septem phialis, bestiæ & adoratoribus ejus, inflictæ: quarum ultima in aërem effusa, vox auditur: Factum esse. Apoc. 17: 8--13. canitur de regno bestiæ & Antichristo coercendo, & tandem in octavo monte, seu regno substituturo.
units.tr: III. Matt. 13:41, 42 foretells the gathering of the tares into bundles and their casting into the fire. Sixth, this matter is treated especially in the Apocalypse. In Rev. 11:3 the two witnesses revive, in Rev. 14:6 the eternal Gospel is preached, and then the ruin of Babylon is announced. In Rev. 16 seven plagues are recounted, inflicted on the beast and its worshippers under seven vials; of these, when the last is poured out into the air, a voice is heard: It is done. Rev. 17:8–13 sings of the kingdom of the beast and of the restraining of Antichrist, and finally of the eighth mountain, or the kingdom that is to succeed.

units.la: IV. Gradus, per quos in ruinam prolapsurus est Antichristus, tres potissimum definiuntur. Et tunc revelabitur defector, quem Dominus consumet spiritu oris sui, & abolebit illucente adventu suo. 2. Thess. 2: 8. Primus gradus igitur est Antichristi revelatio; quæ facta superiori seculo. Alter gradus est, consumptio ejus à Domino, per Spiritum oris sui; quæ est cessatio hostis. Psal. 8:3.quod faciendum per verbum & Spiritum Christi. Esai. 11: 4. Spiritu labiorum suorum interficiet improbum. Conf. Apoc. 1: 16. Tertius gradus, est abolitio per affulgentiam adventus Domini. Confer Matth. 24: 30. Tunc apparebit signum filii hominis in cælo. Ita Apoc. 17:16. Odio habebitur meretrix & desolata fuit. & cap. 18: 21. non amplius invenitur locus Babylonis. Et 19: 20. & 20: 10, 14. Bestia & pseudo-Propheta, mors & infernus in stagnum ignis conjiciuntur; id est, indurantur, veritate detecta, & torquentur conscientia mala & rodente.
units.tr: IV. The steps by which Antichrist is to fall into ruin are chiefly three. And then shall that wicked one be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the breath of his mouth, and shall abolish by the brightness of his coming (2 Thess. 2:8). The first step, then, is the revelation of Antichrist, which took place in the previous century. The second step is his consumption by the Lord through the breath of his mouth, which is the cessation of the enemy (Ps. 8:3), to be accomplished through the Word and Spirit of Christ. Isa. 11:4: With the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked. Cf. Rev. 1:16. The third step is abolition by the brightness of the Lord's coming. Compare Matt. 24:30: Then shall the sign of the Son of Man appear in heaven. Thus Rev. 17:16: the harlot shall be hated and made desolate; and in ch. 18:21 no more is the place of Babylon found. And in Rev. 19:20 and 20:10, 14, the beast and the false prophet, death and hell are cast into the lake of fire; that is, they are hardened, the truth being revealed, and tormented by an evil and gnawing conscience.

units.la: V. Quamobrem primus Babylonis casus Apoc. 14: 8. & 18:2. non dicit omnimodam ejus eversionem, uti patet ex locis laudatis, cum ipsa deinceps accipiat clavim putei abyssi, & tanquam regina sedeat; sed tantum indicat diminutionem auctoritatis & æstimationis ejus. Videtur tamen ex omnibus hisce sensim magis ac magis delapsurum Antichristi regnum; donec ante adventum Christi, vel summum, cum eo, plane aboleatur. Quo pertinet illud Apoc. 18:21. Sic impetu conjicietur Babylon, civitas illa magna, & non invenietur amplius. Vox autem illa casus ejus, originem traxit ex Esai. 21:9. Tunc elocutus est dicens, cecidit, cecidit Babylon, & omnes sculptiles Deos ejus perfringens dejecit in terram.
units.tr: V. Wherefore the first fall of Babylon (Rev. 14:8 and 18:2) does not mean its total overthrow, as is clear from the passages cited, since afterwards it receives the key of the bottomless pit and sits as a queen. It indicates only a diminution of its authority and esteem. Yet it seems that from all these things the kingdom of Antichrist will fall gradually more and more, until before the coming of Christ, or at the moment of that coming, it is utterly abolished. To this belongs the saying of Rev. 18:21: Thus with violence shall Babylon, that great city, be cast down, and shall be found no more. The word fall itself took its origin from Isa. 21:9: Then he spoke, saying, Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and dashing in pieces all her graven gods, he has cast them down to the earth.

units.la: VI. Cum hac Antichristi revelatione & consumptione conjungi debuit Ecclesiæ ab ea liberatio, prædicta & præcepta Apoc. 18: 2, 4. ubi jubetur populus Dei exire è Babylone, ne particeps peccatorum, imo etiam plagarum ejus fiat: per quæ exitus innuitur quoad ipsum locum; cum cæteroquin communio cum ea vitari non possit; ad exemplum & figuram exitus è Babylone antiqua. Esai. 48: 20. Exite è Babylone, fugite à Chaldæis Jer. 51: 6. Fugite è medio Babylonis, & eripite quisque seipsum, ne exscindamini in iniquitate ejus. & com. 45. Exite e medio ejus, populemi, & eripite quisque animam suam, ab æstu iræ Jehovæ. Impletum illud est, quando superiori seculo, lege imperiali, concessa est professio Reformatæ religionis principibus & civitatibus eam amplexis; in Passavien si scilicet transactione. Quam secuta est pax Ecclesiæ in Europa. Esai. 57: 19. Creans proventum labiorum, pacem, longinquo & propinquo, inquit Jehova. conf. Habac. 3:14. Designasti in tribubus ejus caput pagorum ejus. Esai. 19: 18. Villa & civitates in media Ægypto loquentes linguam terræ Canaan, sunt 5 ƀυναςεῖαι, seu provinciæ in illo regno, quod antea Ægyptus spiritualis erat, Euangelium amplexæ. Præcipue hinc prædicitur pax aliqua Ecclesiæ. Esai. 2:4. Tundent gladios suos in ligones, & hastas suas in falces; non attollet gens una in alteram gladium, neque discent amplius bellum. conf. Ezech. 39: 3. Scilicet ad tempus. Qualis etiam fuit ligatio quatuor Angelorum ad Euphratem. Apoc. 9: 14. qui tamen parati fuerunt ad egrediendum.
units.tr: VI. With this revelation and consumption of Antichrist there had to be joined the deliverance of the Church from him, foretold and commanded in Rev. 18:2, 4, where the people of God is bidden to come out of Babylon, lest they become partakers of her sins and even of her plagues. By this going out is meant the leaving of the place itself, since otherwise communion with her could not be avoided, after the pattern and figure of the departure from ancient Babylon. Isa. 48:20: Go out of Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans. Jer. 51:6: Flee from the midst of Babylon, and let each save his own life, lest you be cut off in her iniquity. And verse 45: Come out of the midst of her, my people, and let each save his soul from the fierce anger of the LORD. This was fulfilled when, in the previous century, by imperial law, the profession of the Reformed religion was granted to the princes and cities that embraced it, namely in the Peace of Passau, and this was followed by the peace of the Church in Europe. Isa. 57:19: Creating the fruit of the lips: peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near, says the LORD. Cf. Hab. 3:14: You have pierced with his own staves the head of his villages. Isa. 19:18: The villages and cities in the midst of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan are the dynasties [δυναστεῖαι], that is, the provinces in that kingdom which was formerly spiritual Egypt, which have embraced the Gospel. Chiefly from here a certain peace of the Church is foretold. Isa. 2:4: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. Cf. Ezek. 39:3. Namely, for a time. Such also was the binding of the four angels at the Euphrates (Rev. 9:14), who nevertheless were ready to go forth.

units.la: VII. Babylonem vero cum reliquerit Ecclesia, non plane illa abolita est, sed tacta domicilium dæmoniorum, & omnis avis impura Apoc. 18: 2. phrasi desumpta ex Esai. 34: 11, 13, 14, 15. id est, in Babylone deinceps regnaturi erant dæmones, & homines obscoeni ac mali.
units.tr: VII. But when the Church had left Babylon, Babylon was not utterly abolished; it was made a habitation of demons, and every unclean bird (Rev. 18:2), a phrase taken from Isa. 34:11, 13, 14, 15. That is, demons and obscene and wicked men were thereafter to reign in Babylon.

units.la: VIII. Videamus nunc porro ut & quomodo tam luculentis promissionibus de liberatione & instauratione; sive ut loquimur, reformatione Ecclesiæ, eventus responderit. Exseruit autem ea se maxime superiori seculo: Anno enim ejus seculi 16. alta erat in Ecclesia Romana pax, schismate inter Julium secundum, Papam, & Ludovicum xii. Galliæ regem, sublato, & toto Occidente in obedientia Pontificis Romani secure quieto; cum à paucis veterum Waldensium superstitibus in montibus circa Italiam, ut & in Bohemia; uti nec ab Hussitis Bohemis, nullus esset metus. Leo vero X.PP. per immodicos sumptus & largitiones, profusis suis reditibus, auctore Cardinali quatuor Sanctorum, indulgentiarum illum thesaurum aperuit: A. C. 1516. In quibus promulgandis & distribuendis turpiter nimis se dabant illi, ad quorum curam ea res pertinebat. Cum enim Leo PP. Saxoniae & vicini tractus proventum, Magdalenae sorori dono dedisset; demandavit illa hoc negotium Aremboldo, ex mercatore Genuensi, nupero & recenti Episcopo: qui lucro maxime intentus, promulgationem indulgentiarum, ereptam fratribus ordinis Eremitarum, quorum ordinaria haec erat provincia, per Dominicanos fieri voluit: qui per immensa praeconia; sicut & Aremboldi quaestores, per turpem ipsius lucri in popinis & ganeis dilapidationem, Martino Luthero in indulgentias invehendi occasionem suppeditarunt: qui ab hisce exorsus, alios etiam novos abusus cum veteribus comparando, totius structurae fraudem deprehendit; & opponente se ipsi Johanne Tecelio Dominicano, & dein Johanne Eccio, ut & Sylvestro Priaeria, certamen ab indulgentiis ad alia majoris momenti deflexum est; donec inde ad dogmata, eorumque reformationem perventum est. Idem Ulrico Zwinglio Tiguri de indulgentiis certamen fuit annuo sequenti cum Sampsone Mediolanensi, Francisco, unde ei data fuit occasio ad potestatem Pontificis Romani, qui eas adeo largiter in vulgum profunderet, confutandam, & reformationem, jam antea a se in Helvetia institutam, promovendam. Ille enim anno 1516. Glaronae Euangelium jam praedicabat, cum Lutheri nomen in istis locis necdum esset auditum: & cum eo aliis in locis, missis hominum commentis, decreta Dei auditoribus suis annunciabant, Wolfgangus Fabritius Capito, Johannes Oecolampadius, Johannes Creutzer, alii. Licet enim Lutherus primus in disputationis Pontificiae arenam protractus sit, non tamen unus ex omnibus fuit, qui fraudes Romanae curiae agnosceret.
units.tr: VIII. Let us now see further how and in what way the outcome answered to such clear promises of deliverance and restoration of the Church, or, as we say, its reformation. It broke out most of all in the previous century. For in the sixteenth year of that century there was deep peace in the Roman Church, the schism between Pope Julius II and Louis XII, king of France, having been removed, and the whole West resting securely in obedience to the Roman Pontiff. There was no fear from the few surviving Waldensians in the mountains around Italy, or in Bohemia, nor from the Bohemian Hussites. But Pope Leo X, through excessive expenses and largesses, with his revenues poured out, opened that treasury of indulgences in the year of Christ 1516, with the Cardinal of the Four Saints as sponsor. In promulgating and distributing them, those to whose care the matter pertained behaved shamefully. For when Pope Leo had given the proceeds of Saxony and the neighbouring region as a gift to his sister Magdalena, she entrusted this business to Aremboldo, a former merchant of Genoa and a recent bishop. He, intent above all on profit, wished the promulgation of indulgences, taken from the Hermit friars whose ordinary province this was, to be done by the Dominicans. They, through immense publicity, and Aremboldo's quaestors through the shameful squandering of his profits in taverns and revels, gave Martin Luther an occasion to inveigh against indulgences. Starting from these, and comparing other new abuses with old ones, he detected the fraud of the whole structure. When Johann Tetzel the Dominican opposed him, and then Johann Eck and Silvester Prierias, the dispute was turned from indulgences to matters of greater weight, until from there it came to doctrines and their reformation. The following year, Ulrich Zwingli at Zurich had a dispute over indulgences with Samson of Milan, a Franciscan. This gave him an occasion to refute the power of the Roman Pontiff, who poured indulgences so lavishly among the common people, and to promote the reformation he had already begun in Helvetia. For already in 1516 he was preaching the Gospel at Glarus, when the name of Luther had not yet been heard in those parts. Along with him, in other places, sending away human inventions, they announced God's decrees to their hearers: Wolfgang Fabritius Capito, Johannes Oecolampadius, Johannes Kreutzer, and others. For although Luther was the first to be dragged into the arena of the Papal disputation, he was not the only one of all who recognised the frauds of the Roman curia.

units.la: IX. Cujus Reformationis necessitas ex hisce liquido constat.
units.tr: IX. The necessity of this Reformation is clearly established from the following points.

units.la: 1. Quod plurimi praeclari viri in ipsa Romana communione, ab aliquot jam seculis, reformationem in capite & membris desiderarant non solum, sed & acriter flagitarant; quae tamen incassum a variis Pontificibus, & concilio Tridentino, exspectata fuit. 2. Justissima hujus reformationis eamque subsecutae separationis causa, fuit, haeresis in doctrina, idololatria in cultu, tyrannis in regimine Pontificio.
units.tr: 1. Very many distinguished men within the Roman communion itself had for some centuries not only longed for a reformation of head and members but also vehemently demanded it, yet it was expected in vain from the various Popes and from the Council of Trent. 2. The most just cause of this reformation, and of the separation that followed it, was heresy in doctrine, idolatry in worship, and tyranny in government under the Papacy.

units.la: Illius necessitas iustitia tificio.Hæreses enim ibi foventur & vigent fundamentales,ut præter alia, illa de justificatione per opera, per quam fructus mortis Christi vel intervertitur, vel omnis negatur.Nam si per legem justitia est,Christus igitur gratis mortuus est. Gal.2: 2 1. Idololatria ibi floret, eaque non unius generis, sed omnigena ferme; tum, qua verus Deus in imagine colitur;tum qua falsi dii,ut fictitius Christus in sacramento,crux,Papa,sancti &c. religiose adorantur,partim ipsi, partim in suis imaginibus; quas idoneas maxime segregandi causas esse, nemo negaverit. Quæ enim participatio justitiæ & iniustitiæ? quæ communio lucis cum tenebris? quæ concordia Christo cum Belial? aut quæ portio fideli cum infideli? & quæ consensio templo Dei cum idolis? — Quapropter exite è medio eorum & separamini, dicit Dominus.2.Cor.6:14,17. Filioli cavete vobis ab idolis.1.Joh.5:21. Exite ex illa, populemi, ne communicetis cum peccatis ejus.Apoc.18:4. Tyrannidem ibi summam esse,quis inficietur,ubi fides hæreticis non servatur, flammis traduntur fideles, & in eorum conscientias dominium exercetur per leges & instituta Papæ?
units.tr: The necessity of it is plain from the Papacy itself. For fundamental heresies are fostered and flourish there, among them, besides others, the doctrine of justification by works, by which the fruit of Christ's death is either overturned or wholly denied. For if righteousness comes by the law, then Christ died in vain. Gal. 2:21. Idolatry flourishes there too, and not of one kind but of almost every kind: both where the true God is worshipped in an image, and where false gods are religiously adored, such as the fictitious Christ in the sacrament, the cross, the Pope, the saints, and so on, some in their own persons and some in their images. No one will deny that these are most weighty grounds for separation. For what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? What communion has light with darkness? What concord has Christ with Belial? Or what part has a believer with an unbeliever? And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. 2 Cor. 6:14, 17. Little children, keep yourselves from idols. 1 John 5:21. Come out of her, my people, that you may not share in her sins. Rev. 18:4. Who could deny that tyranny is supreme there, where faith is not kept with heretics, the faithful are handed over to the flames, and dominion is exercised over their consciences through the laws and institutions of the Pope?

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Nec exspectanda erat in hisce omnibus ulla Reformatio:Nam 1. Concilia omnia reformidat Papa, ideoque ea amplius cogere non vult. 2. Eaque ipsa vana erunt & absque ullo fructu, dum à Papa pendent;&c dum 3. Ea errare non posse contendunt. 4. Omnibus Papæ interpretationibus annui debet; & Scripturæ sensus ex ejus solius judicio peti. 5. Manent anathematæ Tridentina, contra veritatem. Ut insanabilis Babylon deleri debeat.Tollite theriacam ad delorem ejus, si forte sanetur. Curavimus Babel, & non est curata. Jer.51:9. quibus malis immedicabilibus accedit etiam, quod nullus turpi huic mansioni prætendi color possit, Antichristo tam aperte revelato: sub cujus vexillis imposterum militare velle, nihil aliud esset, quam Christo se velle opponere, eique bellum inferre. Sicut ergo Israëlitæ Babylone relicta, altare Dei & templum restaurabant; ita nobis valere jussa hac spirituali Babylone, externo etiam opere instaurandus fuit cultus Dei. Neque ideo schismatis crimine tenemur, cum non separatio, sed causa schisma faciat. Noster vero abitus laudabilis est; ut Abrahami è Chaldæis, & Apostolorum è Judæis: præterquam quod non tam exierimus, quam expulsi simus; ut nisi in merum potius Atheismum prolabi voluissemus,de cultu publico nobis prospiciendum fuerit.Schismatica vero, si ulla, est Ecclesia Pontificia. Exivimus ergo non tam ex Ecclesia, quam ad veram Ecclesiam, etiam Romanam antiquam, regressi sumus: neque adeo deseruimus Ecclesiam, quam in nobis Ecclesia dedeseruerit Papatum, exiueritque è Babylone, magis etiam fugata, quam fugiens. Supersunt quidem inter ipsos Reformantes dissidia,& opinionum diuiduæ; nec aliter in terris fieri potest; utrique tamen in fundamentalibus, inque protestatione contra idololatriam & cultus Latinorum, conueniunt. Nec ista labecula Ecclesiæ nomen illis magis eripere potest, quam olim Ecclesiis Apostolicis.Nam quidam, qui descenderant è Iudæa, docebant fratres; nisi circumcidamini ritu Mosis, non potestis salvari. Orta igitur repugnantia, & disceptatione non parva Paulo ac Barnabæ adversus illos, constitutum fuit ut ascenderent ad Apostolos ac Presbyteros Hierosolymam super hac quæstione. Act. 15: 1, 2. Quum inter vos sint invidia, & contentio, & dissidia, nonne carnales estis? 1.Cor. 3:3.Oportet etiam hæreses inter vos esse, ut, qui probi sunt, manifesti fiant inter vos. 1. Cor. 11: 19.
units.tr: Nor was any Reformation to be expected in all these matters. For: 1. The Pope dreads all councils, and therefore does not wish to convene them any more. 2. Such councils would themselves be empty and without any fruit so long as they depend upon the Pope; and 3. they contend that he cannot err. 4. We must assent to all the Pope's interpretations, and the sense of Scripture must be sought from his judgment alone. 5. The anathemas of Trent remain, against the truth. So Babylon, which cannot be healed, must be destroyed. Take balm for her pain, if perhaps she may be healed. We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed. Jer. 51:9. To these incurable evils is added this: no plausible excuse can be offered for remaining in that shameful dwelling, now that Antichrist has been so openly revealed. To wish to serve under his banners from now on would be nothing other than to wish to set oneself against Christ and wage war on him. Therefore, just as the Israelites, having left Babylon, restored the altar and temple of God, so for us, who have bidden farewell to this spiritual Babylon, the worship of God had to be restored also in its outward practice. Nor are we for that reason liable to the charge of schism, since it is not the separation but the cause that makes a schism. Our departure is rather praiseworthy, like Abraham's from the Chaldeans and the Apostles' from the Jews. Moreover, we did not so much leave as were driven out; and unless we had wished to slide into sheer atheism, we had to provide for public worship. The Papal Church, if any church is schismatic, is the schismatic one. So we did not so much leave the Church as return to the true Church, which is also the ancient Roman Church. Nor, in truth, have we abandoned the Church; rather, the Church, having been deserted by the Papacy, has come out of Babylon, having been put to flight rather than fleeing. There remain, to be sure, disagreements and divided opinions among the Reformers themselves, and in this world it cannot be otherwise; yet both agree on fundamentals and in their protest against idolatry and the Latin worship. Nor can this small blemish take from them the name of Church any more than it could from the Apostolic churches. For some who had come down from Judea were teaching the brethren: unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved. Therefore, when Paul and Barnabas had great dissension and debate with them, it was decided that they should go up to the Apostles and the elders at Jerusalem about this question. Acts 15:1, 2. For since there is envy and strife and division among you, are you not carnal? 1 Cor. 3:3. For there must be factions among you, so that those who are approved may be made manifest among you. 1 Cor. 11:19.

units.la: XI. Contra hanc vero tam justam separationem, obducunt adversarii: 1.Mosem & Prophetas idololatricis temporibus nova non erexisse altaria. Illud enim singulari de causa, lege cautum erat sub Veteri Test. ubi cultus Dei certo loco erat affixus; quæ lex abrogata est in Novo T. ante latam vero illam legem, aliter fecit Abrahamus ac Patriarchæ. 11. Ejusdem commatis est, quod dicitur; Christum non separasse Ecclesiam suam à Iudaica. Nec hoc mirum, cum sacrificia adhuc legitime in templo offerrentur, nec idola ulla in eo apparerent; & nec dum tempus maturuisset, uti deinceps, ubi Iudæi obstinati obdurarent, sicut nunc Pontificii.
units.tr: XI. Against this so just a separation, our opponents raise the following objections: 1. Moses and the Prophets did not erect new altars in times of idolatry. But that was permitted by the law under the Old Testament for a particular reason, since the worship of God was fixed in a certain place; this law has been abrogated in the New Testament, and before that law was given, Abraham and the Patriarchs acted otherwise. 2. Of the same kind is the claim that Christ did not separate his Church from the Jewish one. This is no wonder, since sacrifices were still being lawfully offered in the temple, and no idols appeared in it; and the time had not yet ripened, as it did afterwards, when the obstinate Jews hardened themselves, just as the Papists do now.

units.la: XII. ni. Si talis, qualem nos facimus, fuerit Ecclesia Pontificia, Patres nostros periisse necesse fuit. At 1. idem Apostolis Iudæi & gentes oggerere potuissent. 2. nulli electi unquam perierunt. 3. remanserunt in Papatu fundamenta salutis, quamvis multis sordibus obruta & obscurata; quæ tamen discreverunt majores nostri, atque ita salvati sunt. 4. Quamvis ita salutem obtinuerint multi majorum nostrorum; non nobis tamen licet in Papatu & Babylone obsidere; aliud enim est captivitatis tempus, quo illi vixerunt; aliud libertatis, quod nobis illuxit. Præsertim, cum post fastiditam illam lucem, Romanæ Synagogæ nox longe tetrior ac dirior incumbere coëperit; additaque erroribus pertinacia, simplices olim errores in legem, ac Ecclesiæ fundamenta abierint. iv. Irrita sic erit promissio Christi, spondentis Ecclesiæ firmitatem adversus portas inferorum. Matth. 16: 18. Sed 1. Promissum illud est veræ Ecclesiæ; non illi quæ hodie talis habetur.
units.tr: XII. iii. If the Papist Church were such as we make it out to be, our fathers must have perished. But (1) the Jews and the Gentiles could have made the same objection to the Apostles. (2) No elect person has ever perished. (3) The foundations of salvation remained in the Papacy, although they were buried and obscured under many filths; yet our forefathers distinguished them, and so were saved. (4) Although many of our forefathers obtained salvation in this way, it is not permitted us to besiege ourselves in the Papacy and Babylon. The time of captivity in which they lived is one thing; the time of liberty that has dawned upon us is another. Especially since, after that light was despised, a far darker and more dreadful night has begun to settle upon the Roman synagogue, and, with obstinacy added to error, errors that were once simple have passed into the law and the foundations of the Church. iv. The promise of Christ, who pledged the firmness of his Church against the gates of hell, would thus be void. Matt. 16:18. But (1) that promise belongs to the true Church, not to the one that is today held to be such.

units.la: 2. Eadem illos premet difficultas; siquidem futura sunt, quæ de Antichristo prædicuntur. 3. Eo ipso in loco, promittitur veræ Ecclesiæ constantia & firmitas adversus Anti-Christianam, in qua vim suam infernus collocavit.
units.tr: (2) The same difficulty will press them, since the things foretold about Antichrist are yet to come. (3) In that very place the constancy and firmness of the true Church are promised against the Antichristian church, in which hell has placed its strength.

units.la: XIII. v. Diuturna nimis fuisset hæc Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ defectio: Sed 1. tam diuturna apostasia conveniebat mysterio iniquitatis. 2. Æque longa est Judæorum pervicacia, quibus tam speciales tamen & luculentæ promissiones factæ sunt; nec breviores sunt tenebræ Ecclesiarum Asiaticarum, tam insigni elogio laudatarum. Apoc. 2. 3. capp. vi. Definiri nequit tempus, quo labes ista Ecclesiæ fuerit affricata. Resp. Nec opus etiam, dummodo eam nunc esse, liquido pateat. Simile est regnum cælorum homini seminanti bonum semen in agro suo. Quum autem dormirent homines, venit ejus inimicus, & sevit zizania inter triticum, & abiit &c. Matth. 13: 24, 25. Jam enim peragitur mysterium impietatis ejus. 2. Thess. 2: 7. Christus, ejusmodi quæstiones, quas solvere poterat, præcidit uno responso; Non sic fuit ab initio. Matth. 19:8. vii. Regerunt; remanserunt tamen apud nos, vobis ipsis fatentibus, fundamenta veræ religionis; vera ergo Ecclesia penes nos semper hæsit. At fundamenta illa etiam esse possunt in Ecclesia corruptissima, ut apud Samaritanos, Israelitas & Pharisæos. Tum etiam fundamenta illa, aliis fundamentis evertit Antichristus & idolum iis opponit.
units.tr: XIII. v. This defection of the Papist Church would have been too lasting. But (1) so lasting an apostasy suited the mystery of iniquity. (2) The obstinacy of the Jews is equally long, although such special and clear promises were made to them; nor are the darkness of the Asian Churches shorter, though they were praised with so notable a commendation. Rev. 2, 3, ch. vi. It cannot be determined at what time that stain fell upon the Church. Answer: Nor is there any need to determine it, provided it is clear that it is present now. The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field. But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went away, etc. Matt. 13:24, 25. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work. 2 Thess. 2:7. Christ cut off questions of this kind, which he was able to solve, with a single answer: It was not so from the beginning. Matt. 19:8. vii. They reply that the foundations of true religion remained among us, as you yourselves confess; therefore the true Church has always remained with us. But those foundations can also exist in a most corrupt Church, as among the Samaritans, the Israelites and the Pharisees. Moreover, Antichrist overturned those foundations with other foundations and set up an idol in opposition to them.

units.la: XIV. Urgent nos viri. Exhiberi non posse Ecclesiarum Reformatarum successionem, nec ostendi, ubi ante Reformationem fuerit. Resp. Desinant ergo jactare inquisitiones suas & zelum in persequendis hæreticis; inter illos enim hæreticos inveniemus eos, quos novos nunc emersisse calumniantur. Partim igitur in ipso Papatu captiva detinebatur Ecclesia, eodem modo ut temporibus Elianis; nam, quamvis ibi apparuerit etiam Ecclesia, delitescebat saltem in Israële, ut nostra in Papatu: partim extra eum conservata fuit in aliis mundi plagis; sicut nimirum, latens in Israële Ecclesia, in Judæa, extra Israëlem apparuit; ita & in Oriente eadem fuit & viguit. Verum cur per tot ambages hic itur? Siquidem non negabunt Ecclesiam veram deficere non posse, & cum nos nostræ titulum hunc jure vindicemus: constabit satis, licet ex historiarum monumentis illud docere nequiremus, ex verbo Dei, eam semper fuisse; etiamsi semper reformata non fuerit.
units.tr: XIV. The men press us: that the succession of the Reformed Churches cannot be shown, nor where it was before the Reformation.
